docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings
docs.text:
FastSmoothBuildings is a Modelica library of buildings and their heating, cooling and ventilation systems written as smooth, event-free, explicit ordinary differential equations:

  • in closed loop, with its own smooth controllers, it follows the Modelica Buildings library: layered walls, windows with the angular optics and gas gaps of Buildings, long-wave and solar exchanges in the rooms, radiators, valves, pumps, boilers, heat pumps with their buffer, ventilation with heat recovery, photovoltaics;
  • with the controls of its systems as inputs, rumoca translates it into a CasADi model, ready for model predictive control, state estimation and calibration with IPOPT.

It has no dependency, not even the Modelica Standard Library, and runs in OpenModelica, Dymola and rumoca alike.

The library was developed as the FastModel package of trano, which generates its models from a YAML description of a building; its history is in this repository. In trano's validation, the models it generates pass the 27 cases of ASHRAE Standard 140 (BESTEST), with heating and cooling loads within 1.1 % of Buildings on average, and follow Buildings within 0.02 to 0.10 K on the zone temperatures of a six-zone house (BESTEST).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The Modelica library is the folder FastSmoothBuildings:

  • OpenModelica: add the folder that holds it to MODELICAPATH and loadModel(FastSmoothBuildings), or loadFile("<path>/FastSmoothBuildings/package.mo");
  • Dymola, OMEdit: open FastSmoothBuildings/package.mo.

The Python package fastsmoothbuildings carries the library and tells tools where it is:

pip install fastsmoothbuildings

import rumoca

import fastsmoothbuildings

session = rumoca.Session(roots=[str(fastsmoothbuildings.LIBRARY)])  # rumoca reads the library from its folder
model = session.loads(source, model="MyBuilding.building").to_casadi()

text = fastsmoothbuildings.bundle()  # or the whole library as one file, to embed it in a generated model

fastsmoothbuildings.LIBRARY is the folder of the library (rumoca reads every Modelica file below a root, so give it the library itself), fastsmoothbuildings.ROOT the folder that holds it, to put on MODELICAPATH, and fastsmoothbuildings.__version__ the version of the library (its version annotation).

docs.title: The library
docs.text:
The library reference has a page per class, from its Modelica documentation.

Package Content UsersGuide Conventions, the smooth functions and the rules that keep a model translatable by rumoca Examples Rooms, hydronic circuits, ventilation and ideal systems to simulate BoundaryConditions Weather data, solar position, Perez sky model, irradiance on tilted surfaces Envelope Walls, floors, roofs (layers split into sublayers as Buildings), windows (panes, gas gaps, frame, overhangs and side fins) Zones Room air, long-wave exchange between surfaces, distribution of the transmitted sun, internal gains Hydronics Water circuits with set flows (optimal control) or pressure-driven flows (closed loop): pipes, pumps, valves, three-way valves, junctions, EN 442 radiators, boilers, air-to-water heat pumps with buffer Ventilation Ducts and air handling unit with heat recovery Controls Event-free controllers: hysteresis as fast bistable states, anti-windup PI, emission, collector, boiler and heat pump controls, every smoothing width a parameter HVAC Ideal heating and cooling Electrical Photovoltaics Utilities Smooth functions (regStep, smoothMax, smoothMin, smoothLimit, ...), convection laws, valve characteristics

A model built from these classes stays an explicit ODE: no when, pre, sample or event-generating if; switches are regStep transitions whose width is a parameter. rumoca sizes arrays and evaluates subscripts from literal parameters only, so the records of the constructions carry their layer and node counts written out (see the User's Guide).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Example What it shows Examples.FreeFloatingRoom The room of BESTEST case 600FF under clear winter days Examples.IdealHeatingRoom The same room heated to 20 °C and cooled to 27 °C by an ideal system Examples.TwoZones Two rooms with an internal wall, a slab on the ground, an on/off and a proportional room controller Examples.VentilatedRoom Balanced ventilation with heat recovery Examples.BoilerCircuit Gas boiler, pump, three-way valve, radiator and thermostatic valve, pressure-driven flows (closed loop) Examples.BoilerCircuitSetFlows The same circuit with set flows, as the model of optimal control has them Examples.HeatPumpCircuit Air-to-water heat pump with its buffer and two radiators Examples.Photovoltaics Arrays facing south and west

The Validation packages of Utilities, Envelope and Controls exercise the smooth functions, the schedules, the gas gaps, the overhangs and side fins, the hysteresis and the PI controller. Every example translates with rumoca, and its CasADi model integrated by CVODES follows the OpenModelica results within 0.01 K on the rooms.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
uv sync                          # Python environment with rumoca and CasADi
uv run pytest                    # structure, bundle and rumoca tests
uv run pytest -m openmodelica    # simulations of the examples in OpenModelica (Docker)
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy

The OpenModelica tests run the examples in the official image openmodelica/openmodelica:v1.26.9-ompython and compare them with FastSmoothBuildings/Resources/ReferenceResults/OpenModelica; uv run pytest -m openmodelica --update-references rewrites the references after a deliberate change. The rumoca tests integrate the CasADi models and compare them with the same references, without Docker.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: A change merged into main is released once CI passes on it when it changes what users install: the library, the Python package, pyproject.toml, README.md or LICENSE (changes to the tests, the study, the documentation site or CI wait for the next such change, as semantic versioning has it). The release workflow tags the version of FastSmoothBuildings/package.mo when it has no tag yet (the first release, or a version raised by hand in a pull request), and otherwise raises the minor version and commits it (python scripts/bump_version.py minor). The tag publishes the wheel and the sdist on PyPI and creates the GitHub release with the library as a zip for OpenModelica and Dymola; its notes are the section of the version in CHANGELOG.md, or the commits since the previous release. The workflow uses the repository secrets ACCESS_TOKEN (a personal access token that may push to the repository) and PYPI_API_TOKEN (a PyPI API token), as trano does.

docs.title: The study
docs.text:
The study against Buildings (study/) runs the models trano generates from the YAML descriptions of BESTEST cases and two houses, with Buildings and with FastSmoothBuildings, in OpenModelica:

uv sync --group study                                   # trano, trano-simulate, trano-optimization
uv run python -m study.buildings run 950FF              # both libraries, every variant of a case (Docker)
uv run python -m study.buildings report --docs          # the page "Against Buildings" from the committed results
uv run python -m study.replay compare residential_after # FastSmoothBuildings replaying the controls of Buildings
uv run python -m study.analysis.scripts.study_responses # the numbers of a report of the analysis

The simulations need Docker and the Modelica libraries of trano (TRANO_MODELICA_LIBRARIES); the results are committed (study/buildings/results, study/analysis/results), so the reports and the pages render without them. The workflow study.yaml runs the study on demand, or on a push whose commit message carries [study], and commits its results.

docs.title: The documentation
docs.text:
uv sync --group docs
uv run mkdocs serve

The pages of the library are generated from the Documentation annotations of its classes (docs/gen_pages.py), the pages of the analysis from study/analysis. The workflow docs.yaml publishes the site on GitHub Pages.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings: analysis
docs.text: FastSmoothBuildings is trano's reduced building library: the same YAML as Buildings and IDEAS, components written to be smooth and explicit so that rumoca translates them into a CasADi ODE for optimal control (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) and calibration (mpctrano), and so that the closed loop (FastSmoothBuildings) runs in OpenModelica too. This folder gathers the analysis that brought it to its present state: whether it passes BESTEST, whether it reproduces Buildings and responds to the YAML as Buildings does, whether complex houses export and solve as MPC problems, what was changed in the library and why, and what is still open.

docs.title: In short
docs.text:
• BESTEST: 27 of 27 cases, 105 of 105 KPIs inside their band, shading included; FastSmoothBuildings gates as Buildings and IDEAS do. Against Buildings: loads 1.1 % apart on average (4.4 % at most), temperatures 0.38 K (1.70 K). It started at 83 of 85 KPIs of 22 cases with the heating 9 % above Buildings.
  • Against Buildings, closed loop, same YAML: zones within 0.02 to 0.10 K hour by hour (0.46 K in an unheated sun-space), heating within 1.7 % in every base case. Of 45 changes of the YAML, 36 move both libraries alike, 4 closely, 2 differ (both peaks of the heat pump) and 3 move neither.
  • MPC: both residential houses (heat pump with buffer and ventilation; gas boiler) export with rumoca in under a minute (189 and 160 states) and IPOPT solves their 12-hour optimal control in 23 to 55 s, every zone at its bound. The closed loop and the MPC model share their state names, so mpctrano can start one from the other.
  • Boiler house: rooms within 0.02 to 0.09 K, heating +1.7 %, gas +1.9 % (gas per unit of heat within 0.2 %); both water loops conserve energy within 0.15 %.
  • Open: the heat pump at full load and its safety times, the response to the solar absorptance of the opaque surfaces (0.91 to 0.93), the zones that nothing cools keeping a little too much sun.

  • trano-optimization is not a dependency of trano: install it next to trano (uv pip install -e ../trano-optimization, with rumoca >= 0.10.3).
  • Simulations run OpenModelica in Docker (image openmodelica/openmodelica:v1.26.9-ompython) with the libraries in TRANO_MODELICA_LIBRARIES (Buildings 13, IDEAS 3, MSL 4), as the validation does; the runs are cached in .cache/analysis/ by the hash of the model.
  • The detailed validation results these scripts read live in validation/bestest/results, validation/bestest/expected and study/buildings/results, produced by the workflows bestest.yaml and study.yaml; the pages built from them are docs/validation/bestest.md, docs/validation/study.md and docs/validation/improvement_plan.md.

The timings in the results (exports, IPOPT, OpenModelica) are those of the container the analysis ran in (4 cores); they vary from machine to machine, the other numbers do not.

docs.title: 1. The requirements and where each one stands
docs.text:
The goal set for FastSmoothBuildings: a smooth library, compatible with rumoca and CasADi/IPOPT, compatible with complex trano house descriptions with a heat pump, that passes every BESTEST requirement, and can still be used in an MPC; and, for every parameter of the YAML, the same or a comparable impact as in Buildings.

Requirement Status Evidence Smooth, event-free library met every component is an explicit ODE with regStep, smoothMax, smoothMin, smoothLimit and sqrt(x^2 + d^2); no when, pre or sample in the building model; the smoothing of the controllers is exposed as parameters (library changes) rumoca → CasADi met every FastSmoothBuildings and FastSmoothBuildingsMPC model of the tests exports with rumoca 0.10.3, the two residential houses and the shaded BESTEST case 630 included (MPC, shading) IPOPT optimal control met both residential houses solve a 12-hour optimal control (Solve_Succeeded, no comfort slack) with their real systems as controls and their meters as cost Complex house with a heat pump met the renovated house: air-to-water heat pump with a buffer, three-way valve, six radiators with thermostatic valves, balanced ventilation with heat recovery, PV, six zones; closed loop within 0.06 to 0.10 K of Buildings, heating +1.5 %, heat-pump electricity −0.2 % …and with a gas boiler met the house before renovation: rooms within 0.02 to 0.09 K, heating +1.7 %, gas +1.9 %, the same gas per unit of heat within 0.2 % (house before renovation) Every BESTEST requirement met 27 of 27 cases, 105 of 105 KPIs inside their band; FastSmoothBuildings gates in pytest -m bestest as Buildings and IDEAS do (BESTEST) Usable in an MPC (mpctrano) met the closed loop and the MPC model share their state names, so a closed-loop spin-up starts the MPC model; mpctrano's calibration, flexibility, project and model tests pass against the branch (closed loop and MPC) Same or comparable impact of a YAML change as in Buildings met for 40 of the 42 perturbations that move the results 36 alike, 4 close, 2 differ (both peaks of the heat pump), 3 move neither library (study)

What is not met, and the proposal for each, is in open gaps: the heat pump at full load and its safety times (the two perturbations that differ), the response to the solar absorptance of the opaque surfaces (0.91 to 0.93, inside alike but systematically low), and the sun kept in the zones that nothing cools.

docs.title: 2. BESTEST (ASHRAE 140) with FastSmoothBuildings
docs.text:
Question. Does FastSmoothBuildings, the smooth library that rumoca translates to CasADi, pass every requirement of the BESTEST validation that Buildings and IDEAS pass, and how far is it from Buildings on the same YAML?

Answer. Yes: the 27 cases, 105 of 105 KPIs inside their band, and FastSmoothBuildings is now a gating library (pytest -m bestest fails when one of its cases leaves its band, as for Buildings and IDEAS). Against Buildings, the loads differ by 1.1 % on average and 4.4 % at most, the temperatures by 0.38 K on average and 1.70 K at most.

Data: results/bestest_kpis.csv (one row per case and KPI), results/bestest_summary.json, results/bestest_history.csv; script scripts/bestest_comparison.py (--history). The full tables with the bands are on the BESTEST page.

docs.title: Method
docs.text: Each case is a trano YAML file (validation/bestest/cases/) simulated for a year by OpenModelica with each library. The annual loads must fall inside the acceptance limits of the standard; the peaks and the free-floating temperatures inside the spread of the reference programs widened by 5 % of the largest peak or 1 K (validation/bestest/report.acceptance_band). The FastSmoothBuildings results were produced locally and confirmed by the BESTEST workflow on the branch (run 39949636202: pytest -m bestest -k FastSmoothBuildings, 27 passed, the same values); they are frozen in validation/bestest/expected/FastSmoothBuildings.json so that a drift inside the bands fails too.

docs.text:
Every version of expected/FastSmoothBuildings.json in git, set against the Buildings values frozen at the same commit (bestest_comparison.py --history); each line is a library change described in the library changes:

Commit Library Cases Inside Heating, mean Cooling, mean Loads, mean gap Temperatures, mean (largest) 42a466e first FastSmoothBuildings run 22 83 / 85 +9.0 % +3.1 % 5.6 % 0.48 K (1.49 K) 3b04e14 air density at the site, exact smooth limits 22 85 / 85 −0.4 % +5.5 % 3.4 % 1.04 K (4.39 K) b7f503c walls discretised as Buildings, single glazing 23 87 / 89 −0.6 % +5.5 % 3.1 % 1.16 K (4.57 K) ef062cb room long-wave exchange around the surface temperatures 23 89 / 89 −0.6 % +5.0 % 2.7 % 0.93 K (3.82 K) 7658816 exact long-wave exchange with sky and ground 23 89 / 89 +0.6 % +2.4 % 2.0 % 0.80 K (3.52 K) b0e90cd gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes, small hydraulic links 23 89 / 89 +0.2 % +1.4 % 1.2 % 0.38 K (1.70 K) adf7f00 overhangs and side fins; FastSmoothBuildings gating 27 105 / 105 +0.2 % +1.3 % 1.1 % 0.38 K (1.70 K)

Two steps made a number worse before the next one fixed it, and both were diagnosed rather than tuned: removing the excess infiltration (air density) uncovered a heat surplus in the sunny zones (cooling +5.5 %, free-floating peaks up to 4.4 K high), which the long-wave exchange of the room and of the sky (+2.4 %) and the gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes (+1.4 %) then explained.

docs.title: 3. FastSmoothBuildings against Buildings: same YAML, same weather, closed loop
docs.text:
Question. On complex buildings, does FastSmoothBuildings give the zone temperatures, the heating and the meters that Buildings gives, and, when a parameter of the YAML changes, does it move the way Buildings moves? A reduced model is fit for design and for calibration only if its sensitivities are right, not only its results at one point.

Answer. Hour by hour the zones follow Buildings within 0.02 to 0.10 K (0.46 K in the unheated sun-space of 960), the heating within 1.7 % in every base case. Of the 45 perturbations, 36 move both libraries alike, 4 closely, 3 move neither library beyond the resolution of the KPIs, and 2 differ: both are peaks of the heat pump of the renovated house.

Data: results/study_verdicts.csv (one row per perturbation), results/study_responses.csv (every KPI of every perturbation), results/study_fidelity.csv (hour by hour, per zone and variant), results/study_kpis.csv (KPIs and meters of every run), results/study_summary.json, results/study_hour_of_day.csv; script scripts/study_responses.py. The study page with its figures: docs/validation/study.md.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Both libraries are generated by trano from the same YAML file and simulated by OpenModelica in the same container (study/buildings, the workflow study.yaml); FastSmoothBuildings runs in closed loop with its own smooth controllers, nothing is replayed from Buildings. Each case has perturbations, each a change of one field of the YAML, simulated with both libraries; for every KPI the ratio change seen by FastSmoothBuildings / change seen by Buildings is computed (1.0 is a perfect sensitivity, whatever the offset between the libraries). Verdict per perturbation, on every main KPI (mean, lowest and highest zone temperature, heating, cooling, peak heating, heat-pump electricity, gas): alike within 0.9 to 1.1 or 0.05 K / 0.5 % of the base case, close within 0.8 to 1.25 or 0.1 K / 1 %, differs otherwise; a KPI that neither library moves by more than 0.1 K or 2 % gives no ratio. Energies are read from the energy meters of the systems (see the boiler water loop for why).

Case What it is Period Perturbations 950FF heavy BESTEST zone, free floating, night ventilation 1700 m3/h a year, Denver 6 940 heavy zone, ideal heating with night set-back, cooling a year, Denver 14 (two sweeps of four steps) 960 light zone heated and cooled behind an unheated sun-space a year, Denver 4 residential_after six-zone house after renovation: air-to-water heat pump, 100 l buffer, radiators with thermostatic valves, balanced ventilation with heat recovery, PV 28 days of January, Uccle 12 (EPS sweep of three steps) residential_before the same house before renovation: gas boiler at 75 degC, three-way valve, radiators, infiltration n50 = 12 1/h 28 days of January, Uccle 9 (n50 sweep of two steps)

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Case alike close differs neither moves 950FF 6 940 14 960 4 residential_after 6 4 2 residential_before 6 3 all 36 4 2 3

By family (ratios of FastSmoothBuildings's change to Buildings'):

  • Conduction through the envelope. Insulation of 940 from x0.5 to x2: heating 1.00 to 1.01 over the whole sweep, cooling 1.07 to 1.08; EPS of the renovated house from x0.5 to x2: heating 0.98 to 1.00; cavity insulation of the house before renovation (heating −23 %): heating, peak and gas 1.01.
  • Air. Infiltration of 940 from x0.5 to x3: 0.99 to 1.01; airtightness n50 x2 of the renovated house: 0.97; n50 x0.5 and x1.5 of the house before renovation: heating 1.00, gas 0.99 to 1.01, peak 0.88 to 0.98.
  • Thermal mass. Half the mass of the walls: 0.96 to 1.09.
  • Glazing. Solar transmittance x0.75: 0.90 to 1.08; conductivity of the gas of the gap x0.5: 1.02 to 1.07 (940), below the resolution in the house before renovation.
  • Gains. Internal gains x2: 0.99 to 1.01.
  • Sun on the opaque surfaces. Solar absorptance 0.6 to 0.9: 0.91 to 0.93 on every KPI of 950FF and 940, alike but the one envelope parameter FastSmoothBuildings underestimates (open, see open gaps).
  • Two zones (960). Common wall x2, sun-space mass x0.5 and infiltration x2: 0.94 to 1.10.
  • Ideal systems. Heating set points of 940 +2 K: 0.99 to 1.00.
  • Heat pump house. Supply +10 K (electricity 1.04), radiator exponent (peak 0.93), heat recovery 0.5: alike. Set point +1 K (heating 0.87, electricity 0.85), radiators x0.7 (heating 1.28, electricity 1.30 on changes of 3 %), a 2 kW heat pump (peak 1.21) and the ventilation x1.5 (peak 1.14): close. The buffer x3 (FastSmoothBuildings's peak −5 %, Buildings' −1 %) and the EPS x0.5 (peak 1.51) differ: the heat pump of FastSmoothBuildings has no minimum run and off times and takes its condenser from the buffer temperature.
  • Boiler house. Supply −10 K and radiators x0.7: peak 1.06; set point +1 K: heating 0.99, gas 0.99; a 10 kW boiler instead of 16 kW and the radiator exponent move neither library (the peak of the house, 8.7 kW, stays below 10 kW).

docs.title: How the study changed the library
docs.text: The study was run four times. The first run found four defects (the night ventilation dropped by the FastSmoothBuildings zone, a 1 kW leak of the ideal systems, a single glazing that did not translate, an under-determined flat Buildings model) and the gaps that the library changes closed; the second and third runs measured them; the fourth added the house before renovation and read the energies from the meters.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
python -m study.analysis.scripts.study_responses               # tables from the committed results
python -m study.buildings run residential_before --variants base   # one run of both libraries (Docker)
python -m study.buildings report --docs                        # the study page and its figures
The whole matrix runs in CI on a push whose message carries [study] or [study <case> ... | <variant> ...].

docs.title: 4. What was changed in FastSmoothBuildings, why, and what it did
docs.text:
Every change lives in trano/library/FastModel.mo (now this repository) (and its element templates in trano/elements/library/models/fast_model/ and trano/elements/library/library.json), keeps the model an explicit ODE without events (smooth regStep, smoothMax, smoothMin, smoothLimit, sqrt(x^2 + d^2) for |x|; no when, pre or sample) and was checked to export to CasADi with rumoca 0.10.3 (tests/test_fast_model.py). The effects are measured on BESTEST against the bands and against Buildings (BESTEST, history table) and in the study. The plan they came from, with the gaps still open, is docs/validation/improvement_plan.md.

# Change Gap it closes, and the evidence Effect 1 Smoothing of the controllers as parameters (dU, dY, dMax, dT, dtSet, tau), at their previous values a calibration needs to widen the transitions of the thermostats and hystereses (mpctrano FastSmoothBuildings.smooth_controllers) the 27 smoothing parameters of the heat-pump house of the tests (tests/models/house_infiltration_air_water_heat_pump.yaml) are tunable in the CasADi model 2 Night ventilation (ventilationSchedule) reaches the FastSmoothBuildings zone BESTEST 650, 950 and their free-floating twins ran without their fan: the YAML field was dropped by the template the four cases ventilate as in Buildings 3 Air density at the site pressure (the weather bus carries the atmospheric pressure) Denver, 1600 m: FastSmoothBuildings used sea-level air for the infiltration and the scheduled ventilation; docs.title: What was ruled out
docs.text:
• The flow laws of the hydronic circuits (change 10): the gap of the set point response was the resistance of the links, not the linearised valves.
  • The sun on the opaque surfaces (the open gap of open gaps): the irradiance on tilted surfaces, the outside convection with its wind modifier, the long-wave exchange with sky and ground and the discretisation of the walls (tried up to nine sublayers) are those of Buildings; the response to the absorptance stays at 0.91 to 0.93.
  • Energy losses in the water loop of FastSmoothBuildings (the gas of the house before renovation): the loop conserves energy within 0.3 % (the boiler water loop).

docs.title: 5. Overhangs and side fins
docs.text:
Question. Can FastSmoothBuildings shade its windows as Buildings does, smoothly enough for CasADi, so that the four BESTEST cases with shading run and pass?

Answer. Yes. The sunlit fraction of Buildings' Overhang and SideFins was ported to Modelica functions of FastSmoothBuildings with smooth minima, maxima and steps; evaluated through rumoca and CasADi they match the closed form of the shadow within 0.0006; the shaded BESTEST case 630 exports to CasADi with finite derivatives at every hour tried; the four shading cases pass all 16 KPIs, within 2.2 % of Buildings.

Data: results/shading_check.json, the shading rows of results/bestest_kpis.csv; script scripts/shading_check.py; test tests/test_fast_model.py::test_overhangs_and_side_fins_shade_as_buildings.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
• FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.overhangSunlitFraction(verAzi, alt, side, hWin, wWin, dep, gap, wL, wR): the superposition of four rectangles of Buildings, min/max replaced by smoothMin/smoothMax over a width of a hundredth of the window, tan written as a sine over a cosine kept away from zero, the side of the sun chosen by regStep, and the window all in the shade (regStep over 0.01 rad) when the sun is behind the wall or below the horizon.
  • sideFinsSunlitFraction(verAzi, alt, hWin, wWin, dep, gap, h): the same for the two fins.
  • The window (Envelope.Window) computes the solar altitude, the angle of the sun to the normal in the horizontal plane and the side of the sun from the weather bus, and multiplies the direct irradiance absorbed by the panes and transmitted to the room by the sunlit fraction; the diffuse irradiance is not shaded, as in Buildings. With both an overhang and fins the fractions combine as Buildings combines them, smoothMax(f_ove + f_fin − 1, 1e-3).
  • The geometry comes from the YAML (overhang, side_fins of a window) through the FastSmoothBuildings template; a window without shading keeps a fraction of 1 through evaluated Boolean parameters (haveOverhang, haveSideFins), so the other models are unchanged. The geometry parameters are tunable in the CasADi model (14 of them in case 630).

docs.title: 6. The residential houses as MPC models: rumoca, CasADi, IPOPT
docs.text:
Question. Do the complex trano houses, with their real systems (a heat pump with a buffer, a gas boiler, a three-way valve, six radiators with thermostatic valves, a ventilation unit, PV), translate to CasADi through rumoca and solve as an optimal control problem with IPOPT?

Answer. Yes, both. The FastSmoothBuildingsMPC model of each house exports in under a minute, IPOPT solves a 12-hour optimal control in 23 to 55 s (Solve_Succeeded), every zone is held at its comfort bound without slack, and the energy meters are recognised as the cost (electricity of the heat pump and fans, PV production; gas of the boiler).

Data: results/mpc_residential_after_renovation.json, results/mpc_residential_before_renovation.json (exports, roles, the trajectories of every control and zone); script scripts/mpc_houses.py; test tests/test_fast_model.py::test_the_optimal_control_heats_the_residential_house (both houses).

docs.title: Method
docs.text: trano writes the house with the FastSmoothBuildingsMPC library: the same physics as the closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings, with the controllers removed and their outputs made inputs (*_y.y, bounded to 0..1), and one node per layer boundary in the walls (the closed loop splits the layers as Buildings does). rumoca 0.10.3 translates it into a CasADi ODE (trano-optimization CasadiModel.from_modelica); trano-optimization infers the roles of the inputs and states (the controls, the disturbances, the comfort temperatures TAir, the energy meters and their carriers) and builds a collocated optimal control problem solved by IPOPT. The scenario: 12 hourly steps on a cold, sunless night (0 degC outside, sky at −10 degC, wind 3 m/s), every zone at or above 20 degC, energy at 0.25 per kWh, starting from the initial state of the model (zones at 21 degC).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
After renovation (heat pump) Before renovation (gas boiler) FastSmoothBuildingsMPC export 60 s: 189 states, 28 inputs, 4165 parameters 45 s: 160 states, 27 inputs, 3544 parameters Closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings export 54 s: 278 states, 19 inputs 42 s: 224 states, 19 inputs Controls heat pump, three-way valve, ventilation unit, six radiator valves (9) boiler, three-way valve, six radiator valves (8) Meters and carriers heat pump EEle electricity, fans EFan electricity, PV EPro production boiler EFue fuel IPOPT Solve_Succeeded in 55 s Solve_Succeeded in 23 s Comfort slack, largest 0 K 0 K Lowest zone temperature after 3 h 20.00 degC 20.00 degC Energy over the 12 h heat pump 0.93 kWh, fans 0.30 kWh gas 57.1 kWh Cost (0.25 per kWh) 0.31 14.27

What the optimiser does, from the trajectories in the JSON files: both houses let their zones fall from 21 to 20 degC in the first hour and then hold them exactly at the bound. The renovated house first lives on the heat of its buffer and walls (heat pump off for four hours, then rising to 0.20 of its speed), opening the three-way valve and the radiator valves step by step; the old house has no buffer and its walls lose heat fast, so its boiler fires from the first hour (0.19, rising to 0.32 of its power) with the three-way valve fully open on the boiler and the bedroom valves nearly open.

The times are those of this container (4 cores) and include the CasADi construction of the problem; the test of the repository runs both houses in about three minutes.

docs.title: What made it possible
docs.text:
• Every component of the library is an explicit, smooth ODE (no events, no algebraic loops), which CasADi and IPOPT need.
  • rumoca 0.10.3 sizes arrays and evaluates subscripts only from literal parameters: the templates write out the sublayer counts and node indices of the walls (nSta, nNod, lay, nod, sub) instead of computing them.
  • The thermostatic valves, the three-way valve and the production become inputs in FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, with the same hydraulics as the closed loop in their set-flow form.
  • The state names of the walls are shared with the closed loop, so that a closed-loop simulation can start the MPC model (closed loop and MPC).

docs.title: 7. The closed loop and the MPC model share their states
docs.text:
Question. mpctrano runs the closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings model to bring a building to a realistic state ("spin-up") and then starts the MPC model from it, copying the states that have the same name. After the walls of the closed loop were split into sublayers (as Buildings splits them), is that copy still right?

Answer. It was not, and it is now. With the sublayers, T[2] of a wall was the boundary between the first two layers in the MPC model but a node inside the first layer in the closed loop. mpctrano copied the closed-loop value into the MPC model, which then started with the inner surfaces of its walls at the temperature of a node inside the insulation. Its flexibility test found the heat pump at full power all day and no room to run harder. The walls now name T the layer boundaries in both libraries and TSub the nodes inside the layers (closed loop only); every state of the MPC model is a state of the closed loop under the same name and with the same meaning.

Data: the state_names block of results/mpc_residential_after_renovation.json and results/mpc_residential_before_renovation.json; test tests/test_fast_model.py::test_the_closed_loop_and_mpc_models_share_the_layer_boundaries.

docs.title: How it was found
docs.text: The full mpctrano suite against the branch passed 119 tests and failed three: the flexibility envelope, and two tests of the YAML parameters that named one layer conductance by its index (G[2]), which the sublayers renumbered. The flexibility test passed with the released trano 0.58.0. On the heat-pump house of mpctrano's tests, after a two-day spin-up, the baseline MPC plan ran the heat pump at 0.61 of its power in the first hour, leaving 0.75 kWh of upward flexibility over an hour; with the branch it ran at 1.0 at 06:00, 10:00 and 14:00 alike, with no flexibility left. Running the same probe against each library commit of the branch (one git worktree per commit, trano installed from each) gave 0.61 up to the window change (b6ee2b8) and 1.0 from the discretised walls (229dc99) on. mpctrano's spin_up copies the states of the closed loop into the MPC model by name, and the discretisation had given the same names to different nodes.

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
• PartialOpaque holds one heat balance per node of the wall. The construction record says which node is the boundary of each layer (nod) and which nodes are inside the layers (sub); the templates write the arrays out, since rumoca 0.10.3 does not size arrays from computed values.
  • The public states are T[nLay + 1] (the layer boundaries, as before the sublayers, in both libraries) and TSub[nNod − nLay] (the nodes inside the layers, closed loop only).
  • The results did not change: BESTEST within 2.4e-5, the renovated house within 1e-5.
  • mpctrano: the two tests that named a conductance by its index now use the wall resistance and every sublayer of a calibrated layer (branch fix/closed-loop-groups-by-wall-resistance of mpctrano).

docs.text:

docs.title: 8. The house before renovation (gas boiler)
docs.text:
Question. Does FastSmoothBuildings also work with examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml: the same six-zone semi-detached house with uninsulated cavity walls and attic, old double glazing, infiltration only (n50 = 12 1/h), a non-condensing gas boiler at 75 degC, a pump, a three-way valve and six radiators with thermostatic valves?

Answer. Yes, without any change of the library. In closed loop it follows Buildings within 0.02 to 0.09 K per room hour by hour, its heating is 1.7 % above Buildings and its gas 1.9 %; every change of the YAML that moves the results moves both libraries alike, gas included. As an MPC model it exports in 45 s (160 states) and IPOPT solves its optimal control in 23 s (MPC).

The study case residential_before is in study/buildings/cases.py; its runs are in study/buildings/results/residential_before.

docs.title: The gas
docs.text: The gas is 1.9 % above Buildings for 1.7 % more heat: per unit of heat the two libraries burn the same gas within 0.2 % (1.230 and 1.233), and both water loops close their energy balance within 0.15 % over the month. The study first reported +3.3 %, then +2.6 %: it read the gas of both libraries, then of Buildings only, from samples of the fuel power five minutes apart, which catch or miss the two-minute bursts of the boilers when the valves open in the morning. It now reads the energy meters of both. The boiler water loop has the balances and the restart.

docs.title: MPC
docs.text: 160 states, 27 inputs; controls: the boiler, the three-way valve and the six radiator valves; the gas meter EFue is the cost. IPOPT holds the six rooms at 20 degC through a 12-hour night at 0 degC with the boiler at 0.19 to 0.32 of its power and 57 kWh of gas (MPC). The closed loop exports too (224 states), and every MPC state is a closed-loop state of the same name.

docs.title: 9. The water loop of the boiler house: why the gas looked 1 % off, and why it is not
docs.text:
Question. In the house before renovation, the study first reported FastSmoothBuildings's gas 3.3 % above Buildings, then 2.6 %, for 1.7 % more heat in the rooms. Does FastSmoothBuildings lose or misplace heat in its water loop (boiler, pump, three-way valve, six radiators with thermostatic valves), or burn more gas per unit of heat?

Answer. No. Both water loops close their energy balance from the energy meters within 0.15 % over the month, the jacket losses of the boilers are identical (127.3 kWh), and the two libraries burn the same gas per unit of heat within 0.2 % (1.230 and 1.233 kWh of gas per kWh delivered by the radiators). FastSmoothBuildings burns 1.9 % more gas because it delivers 1.7 % more heat. The 1 % in excess came from the study itself, which read the gas from samples of the fuel power five minutes apart. Those samples catch or miss the two-minute bursts of the boiler when the valves open in the morning: −0.75 % for Buildings, +0.6 % for FastSmoothBuildings. The study now reads both meters (study/buildings/harness.py).

Data: results/water_loop_month.json (28 days, by window), results/water_loop_restart.json (days 8 to 10), results/water_loop_restart_table.csv (the morning restart), results/water_loop_components_restart.csv, results/water_loop_restart_tau0.5.json; script scripts/water_loop.py.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The base case is simulated with both libraries in OpenModelica, keeping the variables of the loop. The energy balance of each loop, in kWh over a window:

  • gas: the increments of the fuel meter (EFue, an integrator in Buildings, a state in FastSmoothBuildings), exact whatever the output interval; next to it, the integral of the sampled fuel power, as the study computed it before;
  • into the water: efficiency (0.85) times the gas, minus the jacket loss of the boiler to its room. Buildings 13's BoilerPolynomial injects QWat_flow = eta*QFue_flow + UAOve.Q_flow into the water and then conducts UAOve out of it again, so its loss counts twice; FastSmoothBuildings's port of it does the same with a doubled UA. Plus the pump power, which Buildings adds to the water;
  • out of the water: the heat of the six radiators to their rooms (convective and radiant ports);
  • stored: the change of the heat in the water and metal of FastSmoothBuildings's radiators and boiler;
  • residual: in − out − stored, the energy the loop would create or lose.

docs.text:

The first day is the warm-up from the initial temperatures (20 degC everywhere): both libraries burn 71 to 72 kWh of gas and leave 2.2 kWh in the water and metal of the loop (FastSmoothBuildings's storage is computed, Buildings' is its residual of that day). After it, the residuals are 1.0 kWh (Buildings) and 3.9 kWh (FastSmoothBuildings) on 2700 and 2750 kWh: 0.04 and 0.14 %.

docs.title: The morning restart
docs.text:
At 06:00 the bathroom's set point steps up, at 07:00 those of the living spaces. Day 8, every 15 minutes:

Time Buildings: firing, water, gas FastSmoothBuildings: firing, water, gas 05:45 0.13, 74.87 degC, 2.4 kW 0.13, 74.87 degC, 2.4 kW 06:00 0.13, 74.87 degC, 2.5 kW 1.00, 73.97 degC, 18.8 kW 06:15 0.15, 74.85 degC, 2.8 kW 0.16, 74.84 degC, 3.1 kW 06:30 0.33, 74.67 degC, 6.3 kW 0.27, 74.73 degC, 5.0 kW 07:00 0.24, 74.76 degC, 4.5 kW 0.81, 74.19 degC, 15.2 kW 07:15 0.62, 74.38 degC, 11.7 kW 0.61, 74.39 degC, 11.5 kW

When a thermostatic valve opens, cold water from its radiator returns to the boiler; the water dips and the proportional controller on the boiler temperature (gain 1/K, set point 75 degC, the same in both libraries) fires up to full power for a minute or two. Both libraries do it: the boiler water reaches its lowest at 72.0 degC in Buildings and 72.2 degC in FastSmoothBuildings over these days. FastSmoothBuildings's set points change as a smooth step of 60 s centred on the switch time, so its burst starts 30 s before the hour, where Buildings' starts at the event. That is why FastSmoothBuildings's extra gas shows by hour of the day at 05:00 to 07:00 (results/study_hour_of_day.csv), and why samples five minutes apart misread it: a sample that falls in a two-minute burst at 18.8 kW counts it for five minutes, a sample that falls next to it counts none.

docs.title: Two leads that were not the cause
docs.text:
• The compliance of the pressure nodes. FastSmoothBuildings's pressure-driven circuits give the inlet of each component a small compliance (tauHyd = 5 s) whose stored mass the energy balance does not follow. With tauHyd = 0.5 s the residual over days 8 to 10 is 0.39 kWh against 0.26 kWh at 5 s, on 192 kWh: no difference (water_loop_restart_tau0.5.json).
  • A component that loses heat. The balance of each FastSmoothBuildings component from its port flows and temperatures, sampled every 5 minutes (water_loop_components_restart.csv), does not close: it sums to 42 W where the meters give 5 W, and its terms depend on the reference temperature of the enthalpy, because the samples do not resolve the flow transients of the valves. That per-component audit first suggested a leak in the radiators; the exact balance from the meters shows there is none.

docs.title: What it changed
docs.text:
• The study keeps the meters of Buildings (EFue.y, EEle.y, EFan.y) and reads every production from its meter first (study/buildings/harness.py): the gas of the house before renovation is +1.9 % for +1.7 % heat.
  • Nothing in the library: FastSmoothBuildings's boiler, pump, valves and radiators conserve energy and burn gas per unit of heat as Buildings does.

docs.title: 10. What is still open, and how to close it within rumoca and CasADi
docs.text:
Ranked by what they change in the results of this analysis. Each proposal keeps FastSmoothBuildings an explicit ODE without events and uses only what rumoca 0.10.3 accepts (array sizes and subscripts from literal parameters, no loop in a function over a tunable parameter); the gate is the check that would close it. The same list, with more detail, is in docs/validation/improvement_plan.md.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings
docs.text:
FastSmoothBuildings is a library of fast models close to Buildings. With trano, from the same YAML file as Buildings and IDEAS, it gives a model whose physics follow Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed.MixedAir and the Buildings hydronic and ventilation components, written so that rumoca translates it into a CasADi ODE \(\dot x = f(t, x, u, p)\). The same model simulates in OpenModelica and in CasADi, where trano_optimization estimates its state and solves optimal control problems with IPOPT.

The library comes in two configurations of the same components and templates:

  • FastSmoothBuildings, the closed loop: the controllers of the YAML (thermostatic valves, pump, three-way valve, boiler and heat pump controls, ideal heating and cooling) are part of the model, written without events, and the water flows follow the pressures of the circuits. Its only inputs are the weather and the internal gains: it simulates the building as the Buildings and IDEAS models do;
  • FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, for optimal control: the controllers are left out and the controls of the systems are inputs of the model, which the optimisation decides; the flows are set by the valves.
trano create-model house.yaml FastSmoothBuildings       # closed loop: house.mo with building_mpc and its runnable building
trano simulate-model house.yaml FastSmoothBuildings     # simulates building with OpenModelica
trano create-model house.yaml FastSmoothBuildingsMPC    # the model for optimal control, its controls as inputs

This page describes the components of the library and their equations, what the library does not model, and how close and how fast it is, ending with the most complex YAML file it simulates compared with Buildings and IDEAS. The FastSmoothBuildings tutorial shows how to use the model in CasADi.

FastSmoothBuildings before the closed loop

Until the closed loop was added, FastSmoothBuildings was the model for optimal control. That model is now FastSmoothBuildingsMPC: code that builds an optimal control problem with Library.from_configuration("FastSmoothBuildings") takes Library.from_configuration("FastSmoothBuildingsMPC").

docs.title: How a model is built
docs.text:
trano uses FastSmoothBuildings as it uses Buildings and IDEAS: the Modelica library of this repository, and one template per element of the YAML file in trano, trano/elements/library/models/fast_smooth_buildings/*.yaml. trano embeds the library in every generated package; the constructions and glazings of the YAML are written as records of its Data package. The generated package holds two models:

  • building_mpc, the building: an explicit ODE whose inputs are the weather data and the internal gains, and, with FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, the controls of the systems. It holds no table, no event and no component of another library: this is the model rumoca translates;
  • building, the runnable model: building_mpc fed with the weather file (the Buildings reader, which also gives building_mpc the location of the site), the occupancy schedules and the external data of the network: with FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, the controls replayed from it (each held at 1 without data); with FastSmoothBuildings, the set points of the MonitoredSetpoint emission controls.

Walls, windows and floors are elements of their own connected to the bus of their zone, as in IDEAS. The templates render each system in the mode of the library (library in the templates): with FastSmoothBuildings, each controller of the YAML is a component of FastSmoothBuildings.Controls connected to the system it drives, and every water component is pressure-driven (pressureDriven=true); with FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, each controllable system declares its control as a top-level input of building_mpc named <element>_y (bounded to 0..1) or <element>_Q (a heat flow rate, bounded by the nominal power), and the controllers are not rendered: their decisions are the inputs.

docs.title: Rules for an explicit ODE
docs.text:
Every component keeps a few rules, so that the assembled model translates into \(\dot x = f(t, x, u, p)\):

  • every node joined by connections has a heat capacity, or is solved in closed form inside its component (the radiant star of a room, the mixing of water flows);
  • the equations are smooth (once continuously differentiable): power laws, maxima and table interpolations are regularised, conditions are inside functions or noEvent;
  • water flows are set (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC): each valve sets the flow of its branch, a mixing valve the share of supply water, mass balances the rest; the production (boiler, heat pump) or the ventilation unit closes the balance of its circuit, one per circuit. Or they are pressure-driven (FastSmoothBuildings): each component has a pressure node of small compliance at its inlet, so that the pressures are states and every flow an explicit function of them (see water circuits);
  • controllers have no event (FastSmoothBuildings): hysteresis is a fast bistable state, limits are smooth, PI controllers have anti-windup and a smooth reset;
  • a port with several connections is an array, one element per connection, sized by the template: the inlets of a component mix, its outlets leave at its outlet temperature;
  • parameters computed by functions (the conductance of a radiator, the polynomial fits of the window optics, the scaling of the heat pump tables) take values settled at translation.

docs.title: Components and equations
docs.text: The notation: \(T\) temperatures [K], \(Q\) heat flow rates [W], \(\dot m\) mass flow rates [kg/s], \(A\) areas, \(c_p\) the specific heat capacity of water (4184 J/(kg.K)) or of air (1006 J/(kg.K)), \(\rho\) densities (1000 and 1.2 kg/m3), \(\sigma\) the Stefan-Boltzmann constant.

docs.title: Smooth functions
docs.text:
The library replaces the non-differentiable functions of Buildings by the regularised ones of Buildings.Utilities.Math.Functions:

  • regStep(x, y1, y2, ε): a cubic step from \(y_2\) (\(x < -\varepsilon\)) to \(y_1\) (\(x > \varepsilon\)); smoothMax, smoothMin and smoothLimit are built on it;
  • positivePart(x, δ) \(= \tfrac12\left(x + \sqrt{x^2 + \delta^2}\right)\), a smooth \(\max(x, 0)\);
  • the natural convection law \(Q = A\,c\,|\Delta T|^{4/3}\) is written \(Q = A\,c(\Delta T)\,\Delta T\,(\Delta T^2 + \Delta T_0^2)^{1/6}\), with \(\Delta T_0 = 0.1\) K and the coefficient \(c\) blended smoothly between its values for a surface warmer or colder than the air.

docs.title: Weather and solar irradiance
docs.text:
BoundaryConditions.Weather takes the seven channels of a weather file or a forecast (TDryBul, TBlaSky, winSpe, winDir, HDirNor, HDifHor, HGloHor) and computes the solar position from the model time, as Buildings.BoundaryConditions.SolarGeometry:

\[ \delta = \arcsin\!\left(-\sin 23.45^\circ \cos\frac{2\pi (t/86400 + 10)}{365.25}\right), \qquad t_{sol} = t - t_{zone} + \frac{\lambda\,43200}{\pi} + E(t), \qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi}{24}\left(\frac{t_{sol}}{3600} - 12\right) \] \[ \cos\theta_z = \cos\varphi \cos\delta \cos\omega + \sin\varphi \sin\delta \]

with \(E\) the equation of time, \(\varphi\) the latitude and \(\lambda\) the longitude, and the Perez coefficients \(F_1\), \(F_2\) of the diffuse sky from the sky clearness and brightness (the eight clearness bins joined by smooth steps). BoundaryConditions.TiltedSurface gives the irradiance on a surface of tilt \(\beta\) and azimuth \(\gamma\):

\[ H_{dir} = \max(\cos\theta\, H_{dir,nor}, 0), \qquad H_{dif} = H_{dif,hor}\left[(1 - F_1)\frac{1 + \cos\beta}{2} + F_1 \frac{\max(0, \cos\theta)}{\max(\cos 85^\circ, \cos\theta_z)} + F_2 \sin\beta\right] + H_{glo,hor}\,\rho_g\frac{1 - \cos\beta}{2} \]

where \(\theta\) is the incidence angle on the surface and \(\rho_g = 0.2\) the ground reflectance. The site (latitude, longitude, time zone) comes from the weather file in building; in building_mpc it is a parameter.

docs.title: Opaque surfaces
docs.text:
Envelope.OuterWall, BoundaryWall, AdiabaticWall and InternalWall conduct heat through the layers of their construction, with a node at each layer boundary (\(n\) layers, \(n + 1\) nodes). The capacity of a node is half of each adjacent layer, the conductance of a layer \(k/x\):

\[ C_j = A\left(\tfrac12 x_{j-1}\rho_{j-1} c_{j-1} + \tfrac12 x_j \rho_j c_j\right), \qquad G_j = \frac{A\,k_j}{x_j} \] \[ C_1 \dot T_1 = Q_{sol} - Q_{ext} - G_1 (T_1 - T_2), \qquad C_j \dot T_j = G_{j-1}(T_{j-1} - T_j) - G_j (T_j - T_{j+1}), \qquad C_{n+1} \dot T_{n+1} = G_n (T_n - T_{n+1}) - Q_{int} + Q_{rad} \]
  • Outer surface (OuterWall): absorbed sun \(Q_{sol} = \alpha_{sol} A (H_{dir} + H_{dif})\); exchange with the outside \(Q_{ext}\) as Buildings.HeatTransfer.Convection.Exterior (TemperatureWind) and SkyRadiationExchange: natural convection, forced convection \(h_F = 2.537\, W R \sqrt{P v / A}\) for a square surface (\(P = 4\sqrt A\)), with \(W\) = 1 windward, 0.5 leeward and 0.75 without wind (smooth in the wind direction and speed) and \(R = 1.67\) for a rough surface, and the long-wave exchange with sky and ground linearised around their mean radiant temperature \(T_{env} = \left(F_{sky} T_{sky}^4 + (1 - F_{sky}) T_{out}^4\right)^{1/4}\), \(F_{sky} = (\pi - \beta)/\pi\): \(Q_{lw} = 4\sigma\varepsilon A T_{env}^3 (T_1 - T_{env})\).
  • Floor on ground (BoundaryWall): the outer surface is held at the ground temperature of the YAML (10 degC by default), as trano does for Buildings' datConBou, or at the outdoor air temperature (outdoor_air variant).
  • Party wall (AdiabaticWall): no heat crosses the outer surface.
  • Wall or floor between zones (InternalWall): each face exchanges with its own zone; side b faces the other way (tilt \(\pi - \beta\), a floor seen from below is a ceiling).
  • Inner surface: natural convection to the room air \(Q_{int}\) with the coefficients of Buildings (1.3 for a wall; 0.76 or 1.51 for a ceiling or a floor depending on whether it is warmer than the air), or a fixed coefficient; long-wave and solar exchange with the room \(Q_{rad}\) (see the zone).

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Envelope.Window models each pane of its glazing as a node, the gas gaps as conductances, and the frame as a conductance between the room air and the outside, after Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows:

\[ C_i \dot T_i = Q_{abs,i} + G_{i-1}(T_{i-1} - T_i) - G_i (T_i - T_{i+1}) \quad (\text{outer pane: } - Q_{ext},\ \text{inner pane: } - Q_{int} + Q_{rad}) \]
  • \(G_i = A_{gla} / (R_{pane,i}/2 + R_{gap,i} + R_{pane,i+1}/2)\), the glass area \(A_{gla} = (1 - f_{fra})A\);
  • the optics of the glazing are computed by trano from its layers with the algorithm of Buildings (Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.Functions, after Finlayson et al.: angular properties of each pane from its normal-incidence values, panes combined by the net radiation method): direct transmittance \(\tau\) and absorptance \(a_i\) of each pane at the incidence angles 0, 10, ..., 90 degrees, and their hemispherical values; the gap resistances follow EN 673. The library fits a quartic in \(\cos\theta\) through the ten angles (least squares, at translation), so that the optics are smooth in the sun position: \(Q_{abs,i} = A_{gla}\left(H_{dir}\, a_i(\cos\theta) + H_{dif}\, a_i^{hem}\right)\);
  • transmitted radiation, distributed in the room by the zone: \(Q_{tra,dir} = A_{gla} H_{dir} \tau(\cos\theta)\), \(Q_{tra,dif} = A_{gla} H_{dif} \tau^{hem}\);
  • outside: \(Q_{ext} = A_{gla}(4 + 4v)(T_1 - T_{out}) + Q_{lw}\) (the wind-dependent film coefficient of the Buildings window model and the sky exchange above);
  • frame: \(Q_{fra} = \dfrac{f_{fra} A}{1/h_e + 1/U_{fra} + 1/h_i}\,(T_{air} - T_{out})\), taken from the room air.

docs.title: Zones
docs.text:
Zones.Zone balances the air of the room, exchanges long-wave radiation between its surfaces through a radiant star, and distributes the transmitted solar radiation, after Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed.MixedAir:

\[ m_{sen}\,\rho c_p V\,\dot T_{air} = \sum_i Q_{con,i} + Q_{con,emitters} + A_{flo}\, q_{con} + \rho c_p V \frac{n_{ach}}{3600}(T_{out} - T_{air}) + \sum_k \dot m_k c_p (T_{sup,k} - T_{air}) \]

with \(Q_{con,i}\) the convective heat of each surface, the internal gains \(q_{con}\) per floor area, the infiltration \(n_{ach}\) (air changes per hour, infiltration variant) and the supply air of a ventilation unit (VentilatedZone; the extract air leaves at \(T_{air}\)). The long-wave exchange is linearised at \(T_0 = 20\) degC: each surface \(i\) has the conductance \(G_i = 4\sigma T_0^3 \varepsilon_i A_i\) to the radiant star, whose temperature balances the radiant gains:

\[ T_{rad} = \frac{\sum_i G_i T_i + Q_{rad,emitters} + A_{flo}\, q_{rad}}{\sum_i G_i}, \qquad Q_{rad,i} = G_i (T_{rad} - T_i) + k_{dir,i} Q_{tra,dir} + k_{dif,i} Q_{tra,dif} \]

The transmitted diffuse radiation is absorbed in proportion to \(\alpha_i A_i\) (\(k_{dif,i} = \alpha_i A_i / \sum_j (\alpha_j + \tau_j) A_j\)); the direct radiation hits the floors first, and what they reflect is spread over the other surfaces, as SolarRadiationExchange of Buildings. A radiant emitter sees the mean surface temperature \(\sum_i G_i T_i / \sum_i G_i\).

docs.title: Water circuits
docs.text:
The water ports carry a mass flow rate and the temperature of the water crossing them. A component mixes its inlets (regularised by \(\dot m_{small} = 10^{-6}\) kg/s so that a closed branch keeps a defined temperature) and its outlets leave at its outlet temperature:

\[ T_{in} = \frac{\sum_k \dot m_k T_k + \dot m_{small}\, \overline{T_k}}{\sum_k \dot m_k + \dot m_{small}} \]

Set flows (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC):

Component Equations Valve \(\dot m = y\,\dot m_{nom}\): the valve sets the flow of its branch (control <valve>_y) ThreeWayValve (mixing) \(\dot m_1 = y\,\dot m\), \(\dot m_3 = (1 - y)\,\dot m\), \(T_2 = y T_1 + (1 - y) T_3\) (control <valve>_y) Junction, Junction2 mass balance; the outlets leave at the mixed temperature of the inlets Pump pass-through; electrical power \(P = \Delta p_{nom}\,\dot m / (\rho\,\eta)\) TemperatureSensor pass-through; \(T\) is the water temperature (no sensor dynamics)

Pressure-driven flows (FastSmoothBuildings, the parameter pressureDriven of every component): each component has a pressure node at its inlet, of small compliance, whose pressure \(p_{in}\) is a state; the flow of each outlet is an explicit function of \(p_{in}\) and of the pressure of the inlet node downstream, with the resistances of Buildings linearised as Buildings does (linearized=true):

\[ \tau_{hyd}\, G_{hyd}\, \dot p_{in} = \sum_{inlets} \dot m - \sum_{outlets} \dot m, \qquad \tau_{hyd} = 5\ \text{s} \] Component Flow of an outlet Valve \(\dot m = G\,(p_{in} - p_b)\), \(\dfrac{1}{G\,\dot m_{nom}} = \dfrac{\Delta p_{fix}}{\dot m_{nom}^2} + \dfrac{\Delta p_{valve}}{(\varphi(y)\,\dot m_{nom})^2}\), \(\varphi\) the equal-percentage characteristic of Buildings (rangeability \(R\), leakage \(l\)) ThreeWayValve a node per inlet; \(\dot m_1 = G_1 (p_1 - p_2)\) equal-percentage in \(y\), \(\dot m_3 = G_3 (p_3 - p_2)\) linear in \(1 - y\), the bypass \(K_v\) scaled by fraK Junction, Junction2 \(\dot m = G\,(p_{in} - p_b)\) on each outlet, \(G = \dot m_{nom} / \Delta p_{nom}\) (at least 1000 Pa) Radiator \(\dot m = \dot m_{nom}\,(p_{in} - p_b) / \Delta p_{nom}\) Boiler the quadratic law \(\dot m = \dot m_{nom}\,\Delta p / \sqrt{\Delta p_{nom}}\,(\Delta p^2 + (\delta_M^2 \Delta p_{nom})^2)^{-1/4}\), linear below \(\delta_M \dot m_{nom}\) Pump its curve (SpeedControlled_y: 1.14, 1 and 0.42 times \(\Delta p_{nom}\) at 0, 1 and 2 times \(\dot m_{nom}\)) scaled to the speed \(y\): \(\Delta p / (y^2 \Delta p_{nom}) = 1.14 + 0.08\,x - 0.22\,x^2\), \(\dot m = y\,\dot m_{nom}\,x\), the positive root; \(P = \Delta p^+ \dot m^+ / (\rho\,\eta)\) TemperatureSensor, HeatPump, pipes a small linear resistance, 1000 Pa at the nominal flow (no resistance in Buildings)

While the pressures settle, a flow may reverse for a moment: the components mix the positive parts of their inflows and carry the positive part of their flow, so that the temperatures stay finite. The circuit has no fixed pressure: the compliances hold the mass of the water, and only the pressure differences matter.

Radiator (RadiatorEN442_2 of Buildings): \(n_{ele} = 5\) water and metal elements in series, each emitting by the EN 442 power law, a share \(f_{rad}\) radiant:

\[ \frac{C}{n_{ele}}\dot T_i = \dot m c_p (T_{i-1} - T_i) - Q_{con,i} - Q_{rad,i}, \qquad Q_{con,i} = (1 - f_{rad})\, UA_{ele}\, \Delta T_i (\Delta T_i^2 + \Delta T_0^2)^{(n-1)/2} \]

with \(\Delta T_i = T_i - T_{air}\) (radiant part: \(T_i - T_{rad}\)), \(n = 1.24\), \(C = \rho V_{wat} c_p + 500\, m_{dry}\) and the water volume and dry mass of Buildings (5.8e-6 m3/W and 0.0263 kg/W of nominal power). As Buildings at initialisation, \(UA_{ele}\) is solved (by bisection, at translation) so that the radiator emits its nominal power at its nominal water and room temperatures.

Boiler (BoilerPolynomial), with set flows the reference of its circuit: the part load ratio \(y\) is the control (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) or comes from Controls.BoilerTemperatureControl (FastSmoothBuildings),

\[ Q_{fuel} = y\,\frac{Q_{nom}}{\eta_{nom}}, \qquad C\,\dot T = \dot m c_p (T_{in} - T) + \eta(y, T)\, Q_{fuel} + UA\,(T_{amb} - T), \qquad \dot E_{fuel} = Q_{fuel} \]

with the efficiency curves of Buildings (constant, polynomial in \(y\), or quadratic-linear in \(y\) and \(T\)), its water volume, dry mass and heat loss to the boiler room.

Air-to-water heat pump (AirToWaterTableData2D with the Vitocal 251-A08 data of Buildings, scaled to the capacity of the YAML) charging a mixed buffer, with set flows the reference of its circuit: the compressor speed \(y\) is the control (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) or comes from Controls.HeatPumpControl (FastSmoothBuildings),

\[ T_{con,out} = T + \Delta T_{con}\, y, \qquad Q_{con} = y\, s\, \tilde Q(T_{con,out}, T_{out}), \qquad P_{el} = y\, s\, \tilde P(T_{con,out}, T_{out}) \] \[ C\,\dot T = \dot m c_p (T_{in} - T) + Q_{con} + UA\,(T_{amb} - T), \qquad \dot E_{el} = P_{el} \]

with \(s = Q_{nom} / \tilde Q(T_{set}, T_{out,des})\) the scaling of the tables, \(\tilde Q\) and \(\tilde P\) the EN 14511 tables made differentiable (quadratic in the condenser temperature through the rows at 35, 45 and 55 degC, linear in the source temperature with the kinks smoothed over 1 K), \(C\) the buffer and the condenser water, and \(UA\) the insulation of the buffer. Its coefficient of performance at the current temperatures, \(\mathrm{COP} = \tilde Q / \tilde P\), is a variable of the model, defined also when the compressor is off.

docs.title: Ventilation
docs.text:
Ventilation.Duct carries \(\dot m = y\,\dot m_{nom}\), the speed \(y\) of the fans of its unit travelling along the ducts and through the zones. Ventilation.HeatRecoveryUnit (trano's system D: constant-effectiveness heat exchanger and two constant-pressure fans), the reference of its air loop, with the fan speed \(y\) as its control:

\[ T_{sup} = T_{out} + \varepsilon\,(T_{ext} - T_{out}) + \frac{P_{sup} + \varepsilon P_{ret}}{\dot m_{nom} c_p}, \qquad P_{fan} = y\,(P_{sup} + P_{ret}), \qquad P = \frac{\Delta p_{nom}\,\dot m_{nom}}{\rho\,\eta_{fan}} \]

where \(T_{ext}\) is the mixed extract air of the zones and the fans heat the air (the supply fan after the exchanger, the return fan before it).

docs.title: Controls (closed loop)
docs.text:
FastSmoothBuildings.Controls holds the controllers of trano's Buildings models, written without events so that the closed-loop model stays an explicit, smooth ODE:

  • a hysteresis (CDL Hysteresis) is a bistable state switching within \(\tau = 10\) s, \(\tau \dot y = \mathrm{regStep}\big(u - (u_{high} + (u_{low} - u_{high})\,y)\big) - y\);
  • a PI controller (Modelica LimPID) limits its output smoothly, with back-calculation anti-windup: \(y = \mathrm{lim}(k(e + I))\), \(\dot I = e/T_i + (y - y_{unl})/(k N_i T_i)\); while disabled, its integral relaxes to the reset value in 30 s;
  • the day schedules of set points ({on, off, ...} in seconds of the day) change with smooth steps of 60 s, the time of day taken without events.
Controller Equations EmissionP (emission control PController) \(y = \mathrm{lim}_{0}^{1}\big(k\,(T_{set} - T_{zon})\big)\), \(T_{set}\) the occupied or setback set point of the schedule EmissionPI (default) PI towards \(T_{set}\), \(k = 0.1\), \(T_i = 900\) s (heating loop of Buildings G36) EmissionOnOff (onoff) hysteresis on \(T_{set} - T_{zon}\), band 0.1 K EmissionMonitored (MonitoredSetpoint) P controller towards the set point input <control>_TSet, which building reads from the column of the external data named in the YAML (held at the occupied set point without data) CollectorControl the pump runs when a valve of its circuit opens beyond 0.5 and stops when all are below 0.01 (hysteresis on their smooth maximum); its speed \(y = \mathrm{lim}_0^1\big(k\,(1 - \Delta p/\Delta p_{nom})\big)\) while it runs ThreeWayValveControl \(y = \mathrm{lim}_0^1\big(k\,(T_{col,set} - T_{mea})\big)\), the supply temperature measured downstream with a 10 s lag BoilerDemand (boiler control simple) demand when a valve of its circuits opens beyond 0.5, none when all are below 0.01 BoilerTemperatureControl part load ratio \(y = d\,\mathrm{lim}_0^1\big(k\,(T_{set} - T_{boi})\big)\) with the demand \(d\) (1 without a simple boiler control) HeatPumpControl supply set point on the heating curve, from TSet at the design outdoor temperature to 30 degC at the heating limit (16 degC); heating season by a hysteresis of ±1 K at the limit; the buffer charges below the set point minus half the band dTHys until it is half the band above; the compressor PI (\(k = 0.1\), \(T_i = 300\) s, minimum speed 0.3) on the condenser outlet, towards the set point plus dTHys

docs.title: Electricity and ideal systems
docs.text:
• Electrical.Photovoltaic (PVSimpleOriented): \(P = A\, f_{act}\, \eta\, \eta_{DC/AC}\, (H_{dir} + H_{dif})\) on the plane of the modules, metered as EPro.
  • HVAC.IdealHeatingCooling (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC): the heat flow rate \(Q\) is an input <element>_Q, split between the room air and the radiant star by its radiant share.
  • HVAC.IdealHeater (FastSmoothBuildings): an ideal emitter delivers \(Q = y\,Q_{nom}\), \(y\) from its emission control.
  • HVAC.IdealHeatingCoolingPI (FastSmoothBuildings): a PI controller per mode (\(k = 0.1\) per kelvin, \(T_i = 300\) s) towards the day tables of the heating and cooling set points, limited by the capacities, metered as EHea and ECoo.

The meters are states in kWh: EFue (fuel), EEle (heat pump electricity), EFan (fans), EPro (PV production); the comfort temperatures are the TAir states of the zones. trano_optimization.Roles.infer reads these roles from the model: an input with a min and a max is a control, any other input a disturbance.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Not modelled: generating a model stops with a message naming the element. Boilers with a storage tank, water-to-water heat pumps, chillers, domestic hot water tanks, batteries, EV chargers, VAV boxes and their controls, air handling units other than the balanced unit with heat recovery (system_d), and power sensors.

Simplifications:

  • Controllers without events (FastSmoothBuildings). The controllers follow those of trano's Buildings models, but a hysteresis switches within 10 s instead of at an instant, and the safety controls of the heat pump (minimum on and off times) are not modelled: the heat pump starts and stops more often than in Buildings, which shows in the water temperatures (about 2 K RMSE) and in the hour-by-hour heat of the radiators (6–16 % CV(RMSE)), less in the zones and the meters. The boiler controls default and complex charge a storage tank, which FastSmoothBuildings does not model: a boiler without storage driven by them always has demand, its temperature control alone sets its firing.
  • The controls are inputs (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC). The controllers are left out: the optimal control decides, or the runnable model replays the controls of the external data. Without data, building holds every control at 1.
  • Flows. With set flows (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC), each valve sets the flow of its branch: the sharing of flow between branches (pump curves, valve authorities, balancing) is not computed. With pressure-driven flows (FastSmoothBuildings), the resistances are linearised at their nominal flows (as Buildings does with linearized=true), and the components that have none in Buildings (sensors, the condenser of the heat pump) have a small one. One production per hydraulic circuit, and mixing three-way valves only: diverting valves are not modelled.
  • Ventilation units are balanced (supply = extract) and run at constant pressure rise; infiltration is a constant air change rate (no wind- or stack-driven air flows).
  • The envelope follows Buildings, not IDEAS: the floor on ground sees a fixed ground temperature (IDEAS models the ground with ISO 13370), and overhangs and side fins of the windows are not modelled. The long-wave exchange in a room is linearised at 20 degC, the interior convection uses the natural convection laws of Buildings.
  • No moisture: sensible heat only, with constant air properties; the co2 occupancy variant only brings its heat gains.
  • The heat pump is the Vitocal 251-A08 of Buildings scaled to the capacity of the YAML, heating only, without the safety controls (minimum on and off times) of Buildings.
  • Tools: the runnable model needs OpenModelica (or Dymola) and Buildings for the weather reader; the CasADi export of the connected building_mpc, closed loop or not, needs rumoca 0.10.3 (rumoca main up to c74cddf, 2026-10-13: the later commits stop the export of these models at residual_equations). The closed-loop model exports too, but its fast controllers and pressure nodes make it stiff: CVODES takes about 100 s per simulated day for the renovated house, where OpenModelica runs its four weeks in under two minutes.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
The validation simulates the Buildings (or IDEAS) model of a YAML file with its own controls and compares it with FastSmoothBuildings in two ways: the closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings with its own controllers, and the FastSmoothBuildingsMPC model replaying the controls of Buildings (the heat of the ideal emitters, or the flow of each radiator branch, the position of each three-way valve, the boiler part load ratio or the heat pump speed and the fan speed; everything else is simulated by FastSmoothBuildings). Zone air temperature RMSE per case:

Case Zones Systems Closed loop (FastSmoothBuildings) Replay (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) BESTEST 600FF / 900FF (a year) 1 free floating 0.39 K / 0.33 K 0.39 K / 0.33 K BESTEST 600 / 900 (a year) 1 ideal heating and cooling 0.06 K / 0.14 K 0.65 K / 0.41 K Three zones (January) 3 ideal heaters, walls between zones 0.06–0.11 K 0.18–0.49 K Heat pump house (January) 6 heat pump, buffer, radiators 0.15–0.25 K 0.15–0.33 K Residential house before renovation (January) 6 gas boiler, radiators 0.05–0.11 K 0.12–0.20 K Residential house after renovation (January) 6 heat pump, buffer, three-way valve, radiators, ventilation with heat recovery, PV 0.06–0.14 K 0.12–0.17 K

In closed loop the controllers correct the small differences of the envelope as the Buildings controllers do, where the replayed controls are open loop: the zones follow Buildings more closely. The meters follow within a few percent (closed loop: fuel +1.2 %, heat pump electricity −1.1 and −3.1 %, fans −2.1 %, PV 0.0 %; replay: fuel +0.0 %, heat pump electricity −1.6 and −1.8 %, fans −0.6 %). The radiators deliver the heat of Buildings within 0.7–4.3 % CV(RMSE) hour by hour in the replay, 2–16 % in closed loop, where the heat pump starts and stops at other instants than in Buildings (it has no minimum on and off times). Against IDEAS, on the renovated house, the zones stay within 0.14–0.23 K in closed loop and 0.31–0.39 K in the replay (see the showcase below).

docs.title: Speed
docs.text: The showcase below times the most complex YAML file FastSmoothBuildings simulates in OpenModelica and in CasADi, against Buildings and IDEAS.

docs.title: Showcase: a renovated house with every system
docs.text:
examples/residential_after_renovation.yaml is the most complex YAML file FastSmoothBuildings simulates: the Belgian semi-detached house of the residential reference cases after a deep renovation, with every kind of system the library models.

Zones 6 (living room, kitchen, three bedrooms, bathroom), 110.6 m2, on two storeys Envelope 15 external walls and roofs, 10 windows (triple glazing), 2 slabs on ground, 3 party walls, 10 walls and floors between zones Heating air-to-water heat pump of 3 kW with a 100 l buffer, pump, mixing three-way valve, split valve, 6 radiators with their valves Ventilation balanced unit with 80 % heat recovery, 12 supply and extract ducts Electricity 4.2 kWp PV array building_mpc (FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) 189 states, 28 inputs (9 controls, 7 weather channels, 12 internal gains), 2807 parameters

The house is simulated for the four weeks of January in Uccle by Buildings and by IDEAS, each with its own controls (thermostatic valves, heating curve and safety controls of the heat pump, three-way valve control). The closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings runs the same house with its own controllers. FastSmoothBuildingsMPC then replays the controls of each library: the flow of each radiator branch, the position of the three-way valve, the compressor speed and the fan speed. The heat pump, the buffer, the water circuit, the radiators, the ventilation unit, the PV and the six zones are simulated by FastSmoothBuildings.

python -m study.replay compare residential_after --models FastSmoothBuildings FastSmoothBuildingsClosedLoop --references Buildings IDEAS
python -m study.replay.benchmark residential_after

docs.title: Zone temperatures
docs.text:
Zone Mean Buildings [degC] FastSmoothBuildings − Buildings: RMSE / bias [K] Mean IDEAS [degC] FastSmoothBuildings − IDEAS: RMSE / bias [K] Living room 20.16 0.17 / −0.13 20.14 0.36 / +0.25 Kitchen 20.08 0.14 / −0.09 20.08 0.36 / +0.25 Bedroom 1 18.14 0.13 / −0.08 18.11 0.32 / +0.14 Bedroom 2 17.90 0.12 / −0.08 17.88 0.31 / +0.16 Bedroom 3 18.02 0.12 / −0.06 17.99 0.33 / +0.18 Bathroom 19.10 0.13 / −0.06 19.05 0.39 / +0.23

Replaying the controls, FastSmoothBuildings follows Buildings within 0.12–0.17 K: its envelope and zone are those of Buildings. In closed loop, with its own controllers, it follows Buildings within 0.06–0.14 K and IDEAS within 0.14–0.23 K. Against IDEAS it stays within 0.31–0.39 K, 0.14–0.25 K too warm on average: the two libraries describe the same house with different envelope models, above all the floor on ground (IDEAS models the ground below the slab with ISO 13370, Buildings and FastSmoothBuildings hold it at 10 degC) and the heat exchanges inside the rooms. The controls replayed from IDEAS bring the heat the IDEAS house needed, which the FastSmoothBuildings house loses a little more slowly.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Buildings FastSmoothBuildings replaying Buildings IDEAS FastSmoothBuildings replaying IDEAS Heat pump electricity [kWh] 130.6 128.3 (−1.8 %) 134.8 133.5 (−1.0 %) Fan electricity [kWh] 17.2 17.0 (−0.6 %) 17.2 16.8 (−2.1 %) PV production [kWh] 139.3 139.3 (0.0 %) 139.3 139.3 (0.0 %) Radiator heat, CV(RMSE) hourly 1.8–4.3 % 1.6–4.1 % Heat pump supply water, RMSE 0.72 K 0.80 K Supply air of the ventilation unit, RMSE 0.30 K 0.27 K

The radiators deliver the heat of either library within a few percent hour by hour, and the meters agree within 2 %. The water temperatures differ most (supply 0.7–0.8 K, return 1.7 K) at the start and stop of the heat pump: the Buildings heat pump has a condenser and a pump of its own, the FastSmoothBuildings one heats a mixed buffer.

In closed loop, FastSmoothBuildings with its own controllers:

Buildings FastSmoothBuildings (closed loop) IDEAS FastSmoothBuildings (closed loop) Heat pump electricity [kWh] 130.6 129.2 (−1.1 %) 134.8 129.2 (−4.1 %) Fan electricity [kWh] 17.2 16.8 (−2.1 %) 17.2 16.8 (−2.1 %) PV production [kWh] 139.3 139.3 (0.0 %) 139.3 139.3 (0.0 %) Radiator heat, CV(RMSE) hourly 5.8–14.6 % 10.3–24.6 % Heat pump supply water, RMSE 1.93 K 1.96 K Supply air of the ventilation unit, RMSE 0.37 K 0.12 K

The zones and the meters stay close; the radiator heat and the water temperatures differ more than in the replay, hour by hour: the heat pump of FastSmoothBuildings, without the minimum on and off times of the Buildings control, starts and stops at other instants, and the thermostatic valves answer the zones of FastSmoothBuildings rather than those of the reference.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Four weeks of January, OpenModelica 1.26.9 (DASSL, tolerance 1e-6), on the same 4-core machine:

Model Translation and compilation [s] Simulation [s] Buildings 182 886 IDEAS 167 373 FastSmoothBuildings (building, replaying the controls) 24 99 FastSmoothBuildings closed loop (building, its own controllers)* 10 105 FastSmoothBuildingsMPC in CasADi (building_mpc, CVODES, inputs held over 5-minute steps) 30 (rumoca) 9

* Measured later on another 4-core machine, where the replay simulates in 84 s: the closed loop costs about a quarter more than the replay.

FastSmoothBuildings simulates the four weeks 9 times faster than Buildings and 4 times faster than IDEAS in OpenModelica, and about 100 times faster than Buildings once translated to CasADi. The Buildings and IDEAS runs record the signals the replay needs every minute, the FastSmoothBuildings run every 15 minutes.

The CasADi model is the same model as the OpenModelica one: simulated with the inputs of the OpenModelica run, its zone temperatures stay within 0.014 K of it over the four weeks.

Optimal control. A day-ahead problem of the house (hourly steps, the 9 controls, comfort at 20 degC from 7 to 22 h and 17 degC otherwise, electricity bought at 0.30 and sold at 0.05 per kWh) is solved by IPOPT from the middle of January:

Radau collocation points per hour (CollocationSettings.degree) NLP variables IPOPT iterations Solve time [s] 1 about 9 600 100 39 2 about 14 200 97 117 3 (default) about 18 700 165 380–475

The model itself costs little (about 2 s of evaluations in the slowest solve): the time goes into the factorisations of the KKT system, whose Hessian blocks couple the 189 states at every collocation point. For a model of this size, fewer collocation points per step, or a shorter horizon, keep the solve within a minute.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings
docs.text:
Building models for model predictive control: close to Buildings, translated into an explicit CasADi ODE

FastSmoothBuildings, package (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Package.

Class Description UsersGuide User's Guide Examples Examples: rooms, water circuits, ventilation and ideal systems Icons Icons Types Types and constants Utilities Smooth functions (after Buildings.Utilities.Math.Functions) and parameter computations Interfaces Connectors Data Records of constructions and glazings, written by trano from the YAML file BoundaryConditions Weather and solar irradiance (after Buildings.BoundaryConditions) Envelope Walls, floors, roofs and windows (after Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed and Buildings.HeatTransfer) Zones Thermal zones Hydronics Water circuits after Buildings.Fluid. Two modes, set by the evaluated parameter pressureDriven of every component: set flows (each valve sets the flow of its branch, the production closes the balance: the model of optimal control), or pressure-driven flows (closed-loop simulation: a pressure node at the inlet of every component, the flow of every outlet from its conductance, the pumps on their curves, as the linearized circuits of Buildings) Ventilation Mechanical ventilation (after trano's Buildings system D) Controls Controllers of the closed-loop model: the controls of trano's Buildings models without events (smooth limits and set point changes, hysteresis as fast bistable states, anti-windup PI). The width of every smooth transition and the switching time of every hysteresis are parameters (dU, dY, dMax, dT, dtSet, tau), at values that reproduce the switching controllers by default; wider transitions and slower switches give a controller that collocation and gradient-based calibration can follow Electrical Electricity production HVAC Ideal heating and cooling

FastSmoothBuildings models buildings and their heating, cooling and ventilation systems as smooth, event-free explicit ordinary differential equations: close to the Modelica Buildings library in closed loop, and translated by rumoca into a CasADi model for model predictive control, state estimation and calibration.

Start with the User's Guide and the Examples.
