docs.title: TiltedSurface
docs.text:
Solar irradiance on a tilted surface: direct, Perez diffuse (sky and ground), incidence

FastSmoothBuildings.BoundaryConditions.TiltedSurface, model (source)

Purpose

Solar irradiance on a surface of azimuth azi and tilt til, from the weather bus of Weather: the cosine of the incidence angle cosInc, the direct irradiance HDir and the diffuse irradiance HDif from sky and ground.

Equations

With the declination δ, the hour angle ω, the latitude φ, the tilt s and the azimuth γ,

cos θ = cos s (cos δ cos ω cos φ + sin δ sin φ) + sin s (sin γ cos δ sin ω + cos γ (cos δ cos ω sin φ − sin δ cos φ)),

Hdir = max(cos θ Hdir,nor, 0),

and the Perez model, with the coefficients F1, F2 of the bus and the ground reflectance ρ:

Hdif = Hdif,hor ((1 − F1) (1 + cos s)/2 + F1 max(0, cos θ)/max(cos 85°, cos ζ) + F2 sin s) + Hglo,hor ρ (1 − cos s)/2.

Smoothing

The maximum of Hdir is positivePart (width 0.01), the two others smoothMax over 0.01. The irradiance is continuous when the sun crosses the plane of the surface or the horizon.

Use

The sun on OuterWall, Window and Photovoltaic.

docs.text: Parameter Type Unit Default Description azi Real rad Surface azimuth: 0 south, pi/2 west til Real rad Surface tilt: 0 roof, pi/2 wall rho Real 0.2 Ground reflectance

docs.title: Weather
docs.text:
Weather data, solar position and Perez coefficients for the site

FastSmoothBuildings.BoundaryConditions.Weather, model (source)

Purpose

The weather bus of a model: the weather data, given as inputs (the top-level inputs of the CasADi model), with the site, the solar position and the coefficients of the Perez sky model computed from them, without table or event.

Equations

Solar position, with t the model time in seconds, the standard clock time from the beginning of the year:

  • declination δ = asin(−sin 23.45° cos(2π (t/86400 + 10)/365.25));
  • equation of time E = 60 (9.87 sin 2B − 7.53 cos B − 1.5 sin B) s, B = π ((t + 86400)/86400 − 81)/182;
  • solar time tsol = t − timZon + lon 43200/π + E, hour angle ω = 2π (tsol/3600 − 12)/24;
  • cos ζ = cos φ cos δ cos ω + sin φ sin δ.

Perez model, with ζ the zenith angle:

  • relative air mass m = exp(−0.0001184 alt) / (cos ζ' + 0.15 (93.9 − ζ')−1.253), ζ' = min(ζ, 90°), in degrees in the second term;
  • sky brightness Δ = min(Hdif,hor m / (1366.1 (1 + 0.033 cos(2π (tsol/86400 + 1)/365))), 1);
  • sky clearness ε = ((Hdir,nor + Hdif,hor) / Hdif,hor + κ ζ3) / (1 + κ ζ3), κ = 5.534·10−6 (ζ in degrees), limited to [1, 8];
  • with ak the weight of the clearness bin k of eight (edges 1.065, 1.23, 1.50, 1.95, 2.80, 4.50 and 6.20) and ζ in radians, F1 = max(0, Σk ak (F11,k + F12,k Δ + F13,k ζ)), F2 = Σk ak (F21,k + F22,k Δ + F23,k ζ).
Smoothing

Each bin weight is the difference of two regStep over 0.01 at its edges: the weights sum to 1 and pass from one bin to the next continuously. The minima, maxima and limits are smooth (smoothMin, smoothMax, smoothLimitInside), and Hdif,hor is bounded below by 0.5·10−4 W/m2 in the clearness.

Parameters
  • lat, lon, timZon: the site and its time zone, Uccle by default.
  • alt: the altitude of the site, in the relative air mass.
  • pAtm: the atmospheric pressure on the bus, constant, the default of Buildings; the runnable model takes the pressure of the altitude of the site when the YAML reads the pressure from the weather file.
Relation to Buildings

The solar position of Buildings.BoundaryConditions.SolarGeometry and the Perez coefficients of Buildings.BoundaryConditions.SolarIrradiation.BaseClasses.

Use

TiltedSurface computes the irradiance on each surface from its bus; Examples.BaseClasses.SyntheticWeather gives it clear days.

docs.title: BoilerDemand
docs.text:
Demand of a production (trano BoilerControl, variant simple): on when a valve of its circuits opens beyond 0.5, off when all are below 0.01

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.BoilerDemand, model (source)

Purpose

Demand of a production (trano's BoilerControl, variant simple): 1 when a valve of its circuits opens beyond 0.5, back to 0 when all are below 0.01.

Equations

y = hys.y, a Hysteresis with uLow = 0.01 and uHigh = 0.5 of u = smoothMaxN(yMax, dMax), the largest opening over the circuits. The demand is a bistable state, without pre or when.

Parameters

n = 1 circuits; dMax = 10−3, the width of the smooth maximum. The hysteresis keeps its defaults, hys.tau = 10 s and hys.dU = 0.049; a calibration can widen them by modifiers.

Use

Each input is the yMax of the CollectorControl of a circuit; the output feeds the demand of HeatPumpControl in Examples.HeatPumpCircuit.

docs.title: BoilerTemperatureControl
docs.text:
Firing of a boiler without storage (trano Buildings boiler): P controller (k) on the boiler temperature, while there is demand

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.BoilerTemperatureControl, model (source)

Purpose

Firing of a boiler without storage (trano's Buildings boiler): a proportional controller on the boiler water temperature, while there is demand.

Equations

y = demand smoothLimit(k (TempSet − T), 0, 1, dY).

The part load ratio is 1 once the boiler is about 1/k below its set point and 0 above it, exactly, by smoothLimit; the demand multiplies it instead of switching it.

Parameters

TempSet = 353.15 K, k = 1, dY = 10−3 (the half-width of the smooth limits of the part load).

Use

In Examples.BoilerCircuit, with a demand of 1.

docs.title: CollectorControl
docs.text:
Collector control of a pump (trano CollectorControl): on when a valve opens beyond 0.5, off when all are below 0.01, the speed from a P controller holding the head at dp_nominal

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.CollectorControl, model (source)

Purpose

Control of the pump of a circuit (trano's CollectorControl): the pump is on when a valve of the circuit opens beyond 0.5 and off when all are below 0.01; while on, a proportional controller holds its head at the nominal head.

Equations

yMax = smoothMaxN(yVal, dMax),   y = smoothLimit(k (yPum − dpRel), 0, 1, dY),

with yPum = hysPum.y, a Hysteresis of yMax between 0.01 and 0.5. The set point of the relative head is 1 while the pump is on and 0 while it is off; the on/off decision is a bistable state, the limits of the speed smooth, so the control has no event.

Parameters

nVal = 1 valves; k = 1; dY = 10−3, the half-width of the smooth limits of the speed; dMax = 10−3, the width of the smooth maximum of the openings. The hysteresis keeps its defaults (hysPum.tau = 10 s, hysPum.dU = 0.049).

Use

The output yMax is read by BoilerDemand. See Examples.BoilerCircuit and Examples.HeatPumpCircuit.

Extends PartialEmissionControl.

Purpose

Emission control of a zone, trano's variant onoff: on when the zone falls below its scheduled set point minus half the band, off when it rises above the set point plus half the band. The switch is a Hysteresis, a bistable state, so the thermostat has no event. It behaves as the OnOffController of the Modelica Standard Library with its bandwidth.

docs.title: HeatPumpControl
docs.text:
Control of trano's air-to-water heat pump (Buildings model): heating curve, heating season, buffer charged between TSupSet - dTHys/2 and TSupSet + dTHys/2, compressor PI on the condenser outlet towards TSupSet + dTHys (minimum speed yComMin); the minimum on and off times of the safety control are not modelled

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.HeatPumpControl, model (source)

Purpose

Control of trano's air-to-water heat pump (Buildings model): a heating curve, a heating season, the charging of the buffer within a band and a PI controller of the compressor speed on the condenser outlet. The minimum on and off times of the safety control are not modelled.

Equations

Heating curve, linear in the outdoor temperature between the design point and the heating limit, bounded by smoothMin and smoothMax of width dT:

TSupSet = smoothMin(TSet, smoothMax(TSupMin, TSet + (TSupMin − TSet) (TOut − TOutDes)/(TOutHeaLim − TOutDes), dT), dT).

Two Hysteresis states and the filtered measurement:

  • warOut: 1 (outside the heating season) when TOut rises above TOutHeaLim + 1 K, 0 when it falls below TOutHeaLim − 1 K;
  • bufCha: charging the buffer, from TBuf < TSupSet − dTHys/2 until TBuf > TSupSet + dTHys/2, charging at the start (y_start = 1);
  • τSen dTCon/dt = TConOut − TCon, TCon(0) = TSet.

Compressor:

heaOn = demand (1 − warOut.y) bufCha.y,   y = heaOn conCom.y,

conCom a PI controller of the error TSupSet + dTHys − TCon between yComMin and 1, enabled by heaOn and relaxed to yComMin while disabled. The compressor stops through the product with heaOn, whose factors are bistable states that switch within their time constants: the control has no event.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning TSet323.15 Ksupply temperature at the design outdoor temperature TSupMin303.15 Ksupply temperature at the heating limit TOutDes265.15 Kdesign outdoor temperature TOutHeaLim289.15 Kheating limit dTHys5 Kband of the buffer charging kCom, TiCom0.1, 300 s gain and integral time of the compressor controller yComMin0.3minimum compressor speed tauSen30 stime constant of the condenser outlet temperature dT0.1 Kwidth of the smooth limits of the heating curve dY10−3 (1 − yComMin) half-width of the smooth limits of the compressor speed

The hystereses keep their defaults (tau = 10 s, dU a tenth of their band: 0.2 K for warOut, dTHys/10 for bufCha), which modifiers such as bufCha.tau can change. With dT and dY, they are the smoothing that a calibration can widen.

Use

In Examples.HeatPumpCircuit, the demand from BoilerDemand.

docs.title: Hysteresis
docs.text:
y goes to 1 when u rises above uHigh and back to 0 when u falls below uLow (CDL Hysteresis), as a bistable state switching within tau

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.Hysteresis, model (source)

Purpose

A hysteresis without events: the output y goes to 1 when the input u rises above uHigh and back to 0 when it falls below uLow. Instead of the pre(y) of a switching hysteresis, the memory is a state with two stable values, and the threshold is crossed by regStep instead of an if: the model stays an explicit ODE that CasADi and IPOPT can differentiate.

Equations

τ dy/dt = regStep(u − uthr, 1, 0, dU) − y,   uthr = uHigh + (uLow − uHigh) y,   y(0) = y_start.

The threshold moves with the output: it is uHigh at y = 0 and uLow at y = 1. For uLow + dU < u < uHigh − dU, both y = 0 and y = 1 are equilibria and the output keeps the one it is at. When u comes within dU of the threshold, the target of y leaves its value; as y moves, the threshold moves away from u and the switch completes, y relaxing to its new value with the time constant τ.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning uLow, uHigh thresholds of the switches to 0 and to 1 tau10 sswitching time dU(uHigh − uLow)/10 half-width of the smooth transition at each threshold y_start0initial output

tau and dU are the smoothing of the switch: the defaults reproduce a switching hysteresis, and a model exported for calibration or optimal control can lengthen tau and widen dU. The band where the output is held is not empty only while dU < (uHigh − uLow)/2.

Relation to Buildings

The Hysteresis block of CDL, with the output a Real state between 0 and 1 instead of a Boolean.

Use

The output is the variable y, read as hys.y; u is usually bound in the declaration. It switches the on/off emission control EmissionOnOff, the demand of BoilerDemand, the pump of CollectorControl and the heating season and buffer charging of HeatPumpControl. See Validation.Hysteresis.

docs.text: Parameter Type Unit Default Description uLow Real Threshold of the switch to 0 uHigh Real Threshold of the switch to 1 tau Real s 10 Switching time dU Real (uHigh - uLow)/10 Half-width of the smooth transition of the switch y_start Real 0 Initial output

docs.title: PI
docs.text:
PI controller with limits and anti-windup (Modelica LimPID: back-calculation with Ni), its integral relaxed to the reset value while disabled

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.PI, model (source)

Purpose

A PI controller with limits and anti-windup, and a reset without events: while it is disabled, its integral relaxes to the value that gives the reset output, instead of being reset by a trigger. The limits are smoothLimit, which reaches them exactly.

Equations

With the control error e and the integral I,

yunl = k (e + I),   y = smoothLimit(yunl, yMin, yMax, dY),

dI/dt = enable (e/Ti + (y − yunl) / (k Ni Ti)) + (1 − enable) (yReset/k − e − I) / τReset,   I(0) = yReset/k.

  • enable = 1: the integral of e/Ti, with back-calculation: when the output is limited, y − yunl draws the integral back with the anti-windup gain Ni.
  • enable = 0: the integral relaxes with the time constant tauReset so that the unlimited output tends to yReset; the controller restarts from there when it is enabled again.

enable is a Real and the two parts are blended by it, so it can be the output of a Hysteresis. The output is not multiplied by enable: a model that needs no output while disabled multiplies it, as HeatPumpControl does.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning k, Ti gain and integral time yMin, yMax0, 1limits of the output Ni0.9anti-windup gain yResetyMinoutput after a reset tauReset30 stime constant of the reset while disabled dY10−3 (yMax − yMin) half-width of the smooth limits

dY and tauReset are the smoothing of the controller: a calibration or an optimal control problem can widen them.

Relation to the Modelica Standard Library

The limits and the anti-windup of LimPID (back-calculation with Ni); the reset of a trigger is replaced by the relaxation above.

Use

In EmissionPI, HeatPumpControl and HVAC.IdealHeatingCoolingPI. See Validation.PIControl.

docs.title: PartialEmissionControl
docs.text:
Emission control of a zone (trano EmissionControl): set point of its day schedule, output y to the valve or the ideal emitter

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.PartialEmissionControl, partial model (source)

Purpose

Base class of the emission controls of a zone (trano's EmissionControl): the heating set point TSet from a day schedule, the zone air temperature TZon as input and the output y, the opening of a valve or the share of the power of an ideal emitter. An extending class gives the equation of y.

Equations

TSet = THeaSetBack + (THeaSet − THeaSetBack) occupancy(timeOfDay(t), schedule, dtSet).

occupancy is 1 between the pairs of instants of schedule and 0 otherwise, each change a smooth step over dtSet: the set point changes without an event.

dY and dtSet are smoothing widths that a calibration can widen.

Use

Extended by EmissionP, EmissionPI and EmissionOnOff; EmissionMonitored reads its set point as an input instead.

docs.title: smoothMaxN
docs.text:
Smooth maximum of a vector

FastSmoothBuildings.Controls.smoothMaxN, function (source)

Purpose

The largest element of a vector, once continuously differentiable: the controls of the circuits take the largest opening of their valves with it.

Equations

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
Opaque construction: layers from the outside (side a) to the inside (side b), each split into nSta[i] sublayers of equal thickness (Buildings.HeatTransfer.Data.OpaqueConstructions.Generic and its nSta)

FastSmoothBuildings.Data.Construction, record (source)

Purpose

An opaque construction: its layers from the outside (side a) to the inside (side b), the split of each layer into sublayers of equal thickness, and the radiative properties of its two faces. The walls of Envelope read it (PartialOpaque).

Fields FieldMeaning nLaynumber of layers x, k, c, d thickness, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity and density of each layer nSta[l]number of sublayers of layer l: the states Buildings gives it, at most 3, in the closed-loop model; 1, a node at each layer boundary, in the model for optimal control nNodnumber of sublayers, the sum of nSta; there are nNod + 1 nodes, numbered from the outside lay[j]the layer of sublayer j nod[b]the node of layer boundary b (nLay + 1 of them, nod[1] = 1, nod[nLay + 1] = nNod + 1) sub[m]the nodes inside the layers (nNod − nLay of them) absIR_a, absIR_blong-wave emissivity of side a and side b absSol_a, absSol_bsolar absorptance of side a and side b

The counts and the indices follow from nSta but are written out, without defaults: rumoca sizes arrays and evaluates subscripts from literal parameters only (see Translation into CasADi). For instance, four layers with nSta = {2, 2, 3, 1} have nNod = 8, lay = {1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4}, nod = {1, 3, 5, 8, 9} and sub = {2, 4, 6, 7} (Examples.Constructions.CavityWall); with one sublayer a layer, nod = {1, 2, ..., nLay + 1} and sub = fill(0, 0).

Relation to Buildings

Buildings.HeatTransfer.Data.OpaqueConstructions.Generic and its nSta.

docs.title: AdiabaticWall
docs.text:
Wall without heat flow through its outer surface

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.AdiabaticWall, model (source)

Extends PartialOpaque.

Purpose

A construction of a zone without heat flow through its outer surface (Q_a = 0): the conduction of PartialOpaque stores heat and exchanges it with the room only. All the layer boundaries T[1] to T[nLay + 1] are states.

Equations

Room surface: Q_b = Qrad − Qint, with Qrad the radiation the zone gives to the surface and Qint the convection to the room air (interiorConvection). On the bus: the room face at T[nLay + 1], emissivity absIR_b, solar absorptance absSol_b, no transmission.

Use

The ceilings of Examples.TwoZones.

Floor on ground or over outdoor air: the outer surface is held at a temperature

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.BoundaryWall, model (source)

Extends PartialOpaque.

Purpose

Floor on the ground or over outdoor air: the conduction of PartialOpaque with the outer surface held at a temperature, the ground temperature TGro or, with outdoorAir = true, the outdoor dry-bulb temperature.

Equations

The outer surface (node 1) is not a state: its temperature is set and its balance is not solved (Q_a = 0, the heat to the ground is not computed). The other layer boundaries are states, T[1] to T[nLay] being the boundaries 2 to nLay + 1 of the construction; the room surface is T[nLay].

Room surface: Q_b = Qrad − Qint, with Qrad the radiation the zone gives to the surface and Qint the convection to the room air (interiorConvection). On the bus: emissivity absIR_b, solar absorptance absSol_b, no transmission.

Parameters
  • TGro: a constant ground temperature, under the layers of the construction.
Use

The floors of Examples.TwoZones.

docs.title: InternalWall
docs.text:
Wall or floor between two zones: side a faces the zone of propsBus_a, side b the other

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.InternalWall, model (source)

Extends PartialOpaque.

Purpose

Wall or floor between two zones: the conduction of PartialOpaque with side a facing the zone of propsBus_a and side b the zone of propsBus_b. The layers are given from side a; all the layer boundaries T[1] (side a) to T[nLay + 1] (side b) are states.

Equations

At each face, Q = Qrad − Qint: the radiation the zone of that side gives to the face minus the convection to its air (interiorConvection). azi and til are those of side a; side b faces the other way, its natural convection coefficients are taken at the tilt π − til, and it is the floor of its zone when side a is a ceiling (til = 0).

Parameters
  • epsLw, absSol: the long-wave emissivity and the solar absorptance of both faces, 0.84 by default as Buildings' surBou; the emissivities and absorptances of the construction record are not used.
Use

The partition of Examples.TwoZones.

docs.title: OuterWall
docs.text:
Exterior wall or roof: wind and sky at the outside, sun, conduction, room exchanges

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.OuterWall, model (source)

Extends PartialOpaque.

Purpose

Exterior wall or roof: the conduction of PartialOpaque between the sun, the outdoor air and the sky on the outside and the room on the inside. The layer boundaries T[1] (outer surface) to T[nLay + 1] (room surface) are states.

Equations

Outer surface: Q_a = Qsol − Qext, with the absorbed sun

Qsol = αa A (Hdir + Hdif),

αa = absSol_a of the construction and the irradiance from TiltedSurface, and the heat to the outdoor air and the sky Qext from exteriorExchange (emissivity absIR_a; the natural convection coefficients of the outer face, which faces the other way, at the tilt π − til).

Room surface: Q_b = Qrad − Qint, with Qrad the long-wave and solar radiation the zone gives to the surface (propsBus_a.rad) and Qint the convection to the room air from interiorConvection.

On the bus: the room face at T[nLay + 1], emissivity absIR_b, solar absorptance absSol_b, no transmission.

Use

The walls and the roof of Examples.FreeFloatingRoom. The convection coefficients may be fixed by the zone (hConExt, hConInt on the bus).

docs.title: PartialOpaque
docs.text:
Conduction through the layers of a construction split into sublayers, a node at each sublayer boundary: the temperatures of the layer boundaries are T, the same states in FastSmoothBuildings and FastSmoothBuildingsMPC (a state copied from one library into the other by its name stays at its place), those of the nodes inside the layers TSub

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.PartialOpaque, partial model (source)

Extends PartialSurface.

Purpose

Conduction through the layers of an opaque construction (Data.Construction), from side a (outside) to side b (room). Layer l is split into nSta[l] sublayers of equal thickness, with a node at each sublayer boundary: nSub = nNod sublayers between nSub + 1 nodes, outside first.

Equations

Sublayer j of layer l = lay[j] has the thickness xj = xl/nStal, the conductance Gj = A kj/xj, and gives half of its capacity to each of its two nodes:

Ci = A (xi−1 di−1 ci−1 + xi di ci)/2,

the terms of a sublayer that does not exist left out at the surfaces. The heat into node i is

Qi = Gi−1 (Ti−1 − Ti) − Gi (Ti − Ti+1),

with Q_a, the heat into the outer surface from the outside, in place of the first term at node 1, and Q_b, the heat into the inner surface from the room, in place of the second term at the last node. Each node inside a layer, sub[m], has the state TSub[m]: C dTSub[m]/dt = Q.

Extending classes

They declare the temperatures T of the layer boundaries (nodes nod[b]), with C dT/dt = Q at each node whose temperature is free, and give Q_a and Q_b from the exchanges at the two faces. T and TSub keep their names and places whatever the number of sublayers: with one sublayer a layer (the model for optimal control) there is no TSub (see Conventions).

Parameters
  • stateAtSurface_a: true when the outer surface has a capacity and a state; BoundaryWall, whose outer surface is held at a temperature, sets it to false.
Relation to Buildings

The layers are split into the sublayers Buildings gives them (nSta of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Data.OpaqueConstructions.Generic), at most three a layer in the closed-loop model.

A surface of a zone: area, orientation and its bus

Purpose

It computes, from the tilt, the coefficients of the interior natural convection (convectionCoefficient): cIntPos when the surface is warmer than the air, cIntNeg when it is colder; and isFloor, 1 for a surface of tilt π (a floor), 0 otherwise.

docs.title: Window
docs.text:
Glazing with its frame: panes, gas gaps, optics of the glazing (Buildings), sky and wind outside

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Window, model (source)

Extends PartialSurface.

Purpose

A window of area A: the glazing of Data.Glazing on the glass area Agla = A (1 − frac), with a temperature state per pane (T[1] outside to T[nPan] room side), the gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes, the angular optics of the glazing, an optional overhang and side fins, and a frame without capacity on the rest of the area.

Equations

Balance of pane i, of capacity Ci = Agla xi di ci (cGla when the glazing gives no ci):

Ci dTi/dt = Qabs,i + Qin,i − Qin,i+1,

where Qin,i flows inwards across interface i: Qin,1 = −Qext from the outside, Qin,nPan+1 = Qint − Qrad to the room (convection to the room air (interiorConvection) minus the radiation the zone gives to the inner pane), and between panes i and i + 1

Qin,i+1 = Ggap,i Rgap0,i / (Ri/2 + 1/hgap,i + Ri+1/2) (Ti − Ti+1),

with Ri = xi/ki the resistance of a pane and hgap,i the conductance of the gap at the current temperatures of its panes (gapConductance, with the height hWin). Rgap0,i is the resistance between the centres of the two panes at the reference state of EN 673 (mean 10 °C, 15 K across the glazing) and Ggap,i = Agla/Rgap0,i: the factor Ggap Rgap0 is Agla, and Ggap sets the scale of the exchange for a calibration.

Outside, the outer pane exchanges with the outdoor air and with sky and ground (skyExchange, emissivity absIR_a):

Qext = Agla (4 + 4 √(v2 + 0.01)) (T1 − Tout) + Qsky,

v the wind speed. The frame conducts Qfra = Gfra (Tair − Tout) from the room air to the outdoor air, with Gfra = A frac / (1/hFraExt + 1/UFra + 1/hFraInt).

Optics: the transmittance and the absorptance of each pane for the direct sun are quartics in cos θ, fitted by least squares to the values of the glazing at 0, 10, ..., 90° (polynomialFit); the diffuse sun takes the hemispherical values. With fsun the sunlit fraction of the glass and the irradiance Hdir, Hdif of TiltedSurface,

Qabs,i = Agla (fsun Hdir αi(cos θ) + Hdif αi,hem),   QTraDir = Agla fsun Hdir τ(cos θ),   QTraDif = Agla Hdif τhem,

cos θ bounded below by 0 with positivePart (width 0.01). The transmitted sun goes to the zone through the bus, which sees the room face of the glazing with the emissivity absIR_b, the hemispherical absorptance of the inner pane and the hemispherical transmittance.

Shading

From the weather bus the window computes the solar altitude β = asin(cos ζ), the angle γ between the horizontal projection of the sun's rays and the normal, cos γ = cos θ/cos β (the relation of a vertical window), and the side of the sun. The sunlit fraction is

Shadingfsun none1 haveOverhang fove from overhangSunlitFraction haveSideFins ffin from sideFinsSunlitFraction bothsmoothMax(fove + ffin − 1, 10−3, 5·10−4)

Only the direct sun is shaded; the diffuse sun is not.

Parameters
  • frac: the share of the frame in A; 0 by default, no frame.
  • hWin, wWin: the height and width of the window, √A by default; the height enters the convection of the gaps (the aspect ratio of the cavity) and both enter the shading.
  • haveOverhang, haveSideFins: evaluated; a window without them keeps fsun = 1 and none of the shading functions. The geometry (depOve, gapOve, wLOve, wROve, depFin, gapFin, hFin) is that of Buildings' Overhang and SideFins; left and right are seen from outside.
Relation to Buildings

The glazing data and its angular optics are those of Buildings (Buildings.HeatTransfer.Data.GlazingSystems.Generic), the gaps follow Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.GasConvection (see gapConductance), the overhang and the side fins Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.Overhang and SideFins with smooth minima, maxima and steps, and both combine as Buildings combines them. As in Buildings, the diffuse sun is not shaded.

Validation

BESTEST cases 610, 630, 910 and 930 (overhangs, and overhangs with side fins): every result inside its band, within 2.2 % of Buildings.

Use

The windows of Examples.FreeFloatingRoom and Examples.TwoZones.

docs.title: exteriorExchange
docs.text:
Heat from an outer surface to the outside: natural and wind-driven convection (Buildings TemperatureWind) or a fixed coefficient, and long-wave exchange with sky and ground

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.exteriorExchange, function (source)

Purpose

Heat flow rate Q from an outer surface to the outside: convection with the outdoor air and long-wave exchange with sky and ground. Used by OuterWall.

Equations

With a fixed coefficient hFix > 0,

Q = hfix A (T − Tout) + Qsky;

otherwise natural and forced convection,

Q = Qnat + A hF (T − Tout) + Qsky,   hF = 2.537 W R (2/A1/4) (v2 + 0.252)1/4,

Qnat from naturalConvection with the coefficients cPos and cNeg of the outer face, Qsky from skyExchange, R the roughness factor (1.67, rough) and W the wind direction modifier:

W = 0.75 + (0.5 sdir − 0.25) sv,

sdir a smooth step from 0 to 1 when cos(azi + π − dir) rises above cos 100° (the wind blows on the surface; width 0.05), sv a smooth step from 0 to 1 when the wind speed v rises above 0.25 m/s (width 0.125 m/s). W is 1 on the windward side, 0.5 on the leeward side and 0.75 without wind.

Smoothing
  • The steps of W are x/√(x2 + δ2) ramps.
  • √v is regularised as (v2 + 0.252)1/4: finite derivative without wind.
Relation to Buildings

The TemperatureWind law of the exterior convection of Buildings, with smooth steps; 2/A1/4 is √(P/A) for a square surface of perimeter P = 4 √A.

docs.title: gapConductance
docs.text:
Conductance of a vertical gas gap between two panes per unit area: convection of the gas (Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.GasConvection and convectionVerticalCavity) and long-wave exchange between the two panes, opaque to it, at their temperatures (Buildings exchanges exactly)

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.gapConductance, function (source)

Purpose

Heat transfer coefficient hgap of a vertical gas gap between two panes, per unit area, at the temperatures of the panes: convection of the gas and long-wave exchange between the two faces. The window computes the conductance of each gap with it at every time, so the U-value of the glazing follows the temperatures as in Buildings.

Equations

Density of the gas at atmospheric pressure, at the mean temperature Tm = (Ta + Tb)/2:

ρ = p M / (R Tm),   p = 101325 Pa, R = 8.314462618 J/(mol K).

Rayleigh number, with the temperature difference regularised at 0.1 K and bounded below by 100:

Ra = smoothMax(ρ2 x3 g c √((Ta − Tb)2 + 0.01) / (Tm μ k), 100, 10),   μ = μa + μb Tm.

Nusselt number: the correlations of Wright (1996) for the vertical cavity, blended over 100 around Ra = 104 and 5·104, against the correlation of the tall cavity of ISO 15099,

RangeNu1 Ra > 5·1040.0673838 Ra1/3 104 < Ra ≤ 5·104 0.028154 Ra0.4134 Ra ≤ 1041 + 1.7596678·10−10 Ra2.2984755

Nu = smoothMax(Nu1, 0.242 (Ra x/h)0.272, 0.1).

Conductance, the long-wave part exact for two grey parallel faces opaque to long-wave radiation:

hgap = Nu k/x + σ (Ta2 + Tb2) (Ta + Tb) / (1/εa + 1/εb − 1).

Smoothing
  • |Ta − Tb| is replaced by √((Ta − Tb)2 + 0.01): differentiable when both panes are at the same temperature.
  • The branches of Wright's correlation are joined by regStep over 100 (Buildings joins them the same way), the bounds by smoothMax.
Relation to Buildings

Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.GasConvection with convectionVerticalCavity for the convection. Buildings solves the long-wave exchange between the panes with their radiosities; here it is the closed form above, equal for panes opaque to long-wave radiation.

Validation

The free-floating BESTEST cases with double glazing: the zone temperatures within 0.38 K of Buildings on average (0.80 K with a constant gap conductance).

References
  • J. L. Wright (1996). A correlation to quantify convective heat transfer between vertical window glazings. ASHRAE Transactions 102(1), 940–946.
  • ISO 15099:2003. Thermal performance of windows, doors and shading devices — Detailed calculations.

docs.title: overhangSunlitFraction
docs.text:
Fraction of a window lit by the direct sun below an overhang: the superposition of rectangles of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.Overhang, with its smooth minima, maxima and steps, explicit

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.overhangSunlitFraction, function (source)

Purpose

Fraction f of the area of a window lit by the direct sun below an overhang of depth dep, at the distance gap above the top of the window and extending wL and wR beyond its left and right edges (seen from outside). The sun is given by its altitude alt, the angle verAzi between the horizontal projection of its rays and the normal of the wall, and side, positive when it is left of the normal.

Equations

The extension on the side of the sun, w = wL when side > 0 and wR otherwise, and the corner of the shadow,

y1 = dep tan(alt)/cos(verAzi),   x1 = dep tan(verAzi).

The shaded area is the superposition of four rectangles of heights H = {gap, gap + hWin, gap, gap + hWin} and widths W = {w + wWin, w, w, w + wWin}; for each, with x2 = x1 H/y1 and u = min(x1, x2) − W,

a = min(y1, H) W − min(y1, H) min(x2, y1)/2 + max((y1/x1) u, 0) max(u, 0)/2,

Ashd = a4 + a3 − a2 − a1. The whole window is in the shade when the sun is behind the wall (verAzi > π/2) or below the horizon (alt < 0):

f = 1 − Ashd/Awin, limited to [0, 1],   Awin = hWin wWin.

Smoothing
  • min and max are smoothMin and smoothMax over a hundredth of the width of the window, the limits of f over 0.01.
  • The tangents are a sine over a cosine bounded below by 10−3; x1 and y1 are bounded below by 10−8 hWin where they divide.
  • The side of the sun is chosen by regStep over 0.005, the shade behind the wall and below the horizon by regStep over 0.01 rad.
Relation to Buildings

The superposition of rectangles of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.Overhang, written explicitly with smooth minima, maxima and steps.

Validation

Within 0.0006 of the closed form of the shadow; for instance 0.5000 = 1 − tan 45°/2 for a sun facing the wall 45° high and an overhang 1 m deep, 10 m wider on each side, flush with the top of a window 2 m high.

Use

Window with haveOverhang = true; Validation.ShadingFractions.

docs.title: sideFinsSunlitFraction
docs.text:
Fraction of a window lit by the direct sun between two side fins: the superposition of rectangles of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.SideFins, with its smooth minima, maxima and steps, explicit

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.sideFinsSunlitFraction, function (source)

Purpose

Fraction f of the area of a window lit by the direct sun between two side fins of depth dep, at the distance gap from the side edges of the window and extending h above its top. The sun is given by its altitude alt and the angle verAzi between the horizontal projection of its rays and the normal of the wall; both fins being alike, the side of the sun is not needed.

Equations

With tan(verAzi), cos(verAzi) and tan(alt) bounded below by δ = 10−6, and λ = tan(alt)/tan(verAzi), the tangent of the angle between the horizontal and the sun's rays projected on the wall, the corner of the shadow of a fin is at

y2 = dep tan(alt)/cos(verAzi),   x2 = dep tan(verAzi).

The shaded area is the superposition of four rectangles of heights H = {h + hWin, h, h + hWin, h} and widths W = {gap + wWin, gap + wWin, gap, gap}; for each,

mx = min(H/λ, x2, W),   my = min(H, y2, W λ),   a = H mx − mx my/2,

Ashd = a1 + a4 − a2 − a3, and f = 1 − Ashd/Awin, the whole window Awin = hWin wWin in the shade when the sun is behind the wall (verAzi > π/2) or below the horizon (alt < 0).

Smoothing
  • min is smoothMin over a hundredth of the width of the window; the bounds at δ are smoothMax, and the tangents a sine over a cosine bounded below by 10−3.
  • The shade behind the wall and below the horizon is chosen by regStep over 0.01 rad, the larger of the two shaded areas by smoothMax over 10−4 Awin.
Relation to Buildings

The superposition of rectangles of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.BaseClasses.SideFins, written explicitly with smooth minima, maxima and steps.

Use

Window with haveSideFins = true; Validation.ShadingFractions.

docs.title: skyExchange
docs.text:
Long-wave exchange with sky and ground (Buildings SkyRadiationExchange)

FastSmoothBuildings.Envelope.Functions.skyExchange, function (source)

Purpose

Long-wave heat flow rate from an outer surface to sky and ground, for OuterWall and Window.

Equations

With the sky view factor F = (π − til)/π (1 for a roof, 1/2 for a wall), the environment temperature

Tenv = (F Tsky4 + (1 − F) Tout4)1/4,

the ground being at the outdoor air temperature, and the exact grey-body exchange

Q = σ ε A (T4 − Tenv4) = σ ε A (T2 + Tenv2) (T + Tenv) (T − Tenv),

written as the second form, a conductance times the temperature difference. A linearisation at Tenv understates the loss of a sun-lit surface at 60 °C by a quarter.

Relation to Buildings

The view factor and the environment temperature of Buildings' SkyRadiationExchange.

docs.title: BoilerCircuit
docs.text:
Room heated by a gas boiler and a radiator, in closed loop with pressure-driven flows

FastSmoothBuildings.Examples.BoilerCircuit, model (source)

Extends BaseClasses.PartialHydronicRoom.

The circuit of trano's single-zone hydronic test, in closed loop: a gas boiler held at 80 °C, a pump whose speed follows the opening of the valve, a three-way valve (open: its set point is above the boiler), a radiator and its valve, opened by a PI room controller (21 °C by day, 16 °C at night). docs.title: IdealHeater
docs.text:
Ideal emitter (trano radiator variants ideal and idealbus): Q_flow_nominal times the control y, split between the room air and its radiant star

FastSmoothBuildings.HVAC.IdealHeater, model (source)

Purpose

An ideal emitter (trano's radiator variants ideal and idealbus): the nominal power times the control signal, without water or inertia, split between the room air and its radiant star.

Equations

Q = Qnominal smoothLimit(y, 0, 1, 10−3),

heatPortCon.Q_flow = −(1 − fRad) Q,   heatPortRad.Q_flow = −fRad Q.

smoothLimit reaches its bounds exactly: no heat at y ≤ 0, the nominal power at y ≥ 1. Its half-width 10−3 is fixed. The ports carry the heat into the component, hence the signs: the heat leaves the emitter into the room.

Parameters

Q_flow_nominal, the nominal power; fraRad = 0, the radiant share.

Use

Connect heatPortCon to heaPorAir and heatPortRad to heaPorRad of a zone (Zones.Zone), and y to an emission control such as EmissionOnOff, as in Examples.TwoZones.

docs.title: IdealHeatingCoolingPI
docs.text:
Ideal heating and cooling of a zone towards day schedules of set points (trano IdealHeatingCooling): a PI controller per mode, limited by the capacities

FastSmoothBuildings.HVAC.IdealHeatingCoolingPI, model (source)

Purpose

Ideal heating and cooling of a zone towards day schedules of set points (trano's IdealHeatingCooling): one PI controller per mode, its output the share of the capacity of that mode, and the energy of each mode metered.

Equations

With T the temperature of heatPortCon (the zone air) and the set points interpolated in their day tables by dayTable,

  • conHea: error TSetHea(t) − T,   QHea = conHea.y QHea,max;
  • conCoo: error T − TSetCoo(t),   QCoo = conCoo.y QCoo,max;
  • dEHea/dt = QHea/3.6·106,   dECoo/dt = QCoo/3.6·106 (kWh);
  • heatPortCon.Q_flow = −(1 − frad) (QHea − QCoo),   heatPortRad.Q_flow = −frad (QHea − QCoo).

Both controllers are always enabled, their outputs between 0 and 1 by smooth limits that reach their bounds exactly: a saturated mode gives no heat at all, and the anti-windup keeps its integral from running away while the other mode works. The schedules are interpolated without events.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning TSetHea[0, 293.15] heating set point: time of day (s) and set point (K) TSetCoo[0, 300.15] cooling set point: time of day (s) and set point (K) QHea_flow_max, QCoo_flow_max106 W heating and cooling capacities k0.1 1/Kgain of both controllers Ti300 sintegral time of both controllers frad0radiant share

The controllers keep the other defaults of PI, among them the half-width dY = 10−3 of their limits.

Use

Connect heatPortCon to heaPorAir and heatPortRad to heaPorRad of a zone; the meters EHea and ECoo give the demands. See Examples.IdealHeatingRoom.

docs.text:
Water circuits after Buildings.Fluid. Two modes, set by the evaluated parameter pressureDriven of every component: set flows (each valve sets the flow of its branch, the production closes the balance: the model of optimal control), or pressure-driven flows (closed-loop simulation: a pressure node at the inlet of every component, the flow of every outlet from its conductance, the pumps on their curves, as the linearized circuits of Buildings)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics, package (source)

It must stay small against the branches it feeds: at 1000 Pa, the manifold of six radiators of the renovated house took a fifth of the head of the living room branch, whose valve then opened fully a third more often than in Buildings Pipe Pass-through (junctions, sensors, pumps without a power model) TemperatureSensor Pass-through: T is the water temperature Pump Pump: pass-through with set flows; with pressure-driven flows, the flow at its head from the curve of Buildings.Fluid.Movers.Preconfigured.SpeedControlled_y (1.14, 1 and 0.42 times dp_nominal at 0, 1 and 2 times the nominal flow), scaled to the speed y by the affinity laws Valve Two-way valve: sets the flow of its branch to y*m_flow_nominal (set flows), or opens to y as Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.Valves.TwoWayEqualPercentage, linearized (pressure-driven flows) ThreeWayValve Mixing valve: the share y of the outlet flow comes from port_1 (supply), 1 - y from port_3 (set flows), or Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.Valves.ThreeWayEqualPercentageLinear, linearized: port_1 equal-percentage on y, port_3 linear on 1 - y (pressure-driven flows) Junction Split valve: its inlets (port_1) mix, its outlets (port_2, port_3) leave at the mixed temperature; docs.title: Boiler
docs.text:
Boiler (Buildings BoilerPolynomial): water and metal heated by the part load ratio y; with set flows, the reference of its circuit (no mass balance)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Boiler, model (source)

Extends PartialFlow.

Purpose

Boiler fired at the part load ratio y: a single node of water and metal at the temperature T, heated by the fuel and losing heat to the boiler room. The water leaves at T.

Equations

Fuel power and efficiency, the coefficients a padded with zeros to six:

Qfue = y Q_flow_nominal / ηnom,

effCurηηnom QuadraticLinear a1 + a2 y + a3 y2 + (a4 + a5 y + a6 y2) T η at y = 1 and T = T_nominal Constant, Polynomial a1 + a2 y + … + a6 y5 η at y = 1

Energy balance of the water and metal, with the heat capacity C = ρ VWat cp + 500 J/(kg K) mDry:

Qwat = η Qfue + UA (TAmb − T),   C dT/dt = mTra cp (TIn − T) + Qwat.

The fuel meter EFue integrates Qfue in kWh: a state, exact whatever the output interval.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, the boiler is the reference of its circuit: it has no mass balance, the circuit closes it, and its flows are set by the valves. With pressure-driven flows, each of the nb outlets passes the flow of a quadratic resistance, port_b[j].m_flow = −quadraticFlow(pin − pb,j, m_flow_nominal/nb, dp_nominal, deltaM), regularized below deltaM times the nominal flow.

Parameters
  • UA: heat loss conductance to the boiler room, twice 10−4 Q_flow_nominal by default, because BoilerPolynomial of Buildings 13 counts its loss twice.
  • m_flow_nominal: by default the flow that carries Q_flow_nominal with a 20 K temperature difference; used with pressure-driven flows only.
  • VWat, mDry: water volume and dry mass, by default proportional to Q_flow_nominal.
Relation to Buildings

Buildings.Fluid.Boilers.BoilerPolynomial, with the efficiency curves of Types.EfficiencyCurves. Buildings 13 injects η Qfue and the heat flow of its loss conductance into the water, then conducts that loss out of the water again: the loss counts twice, which the doubled UA reproduces.

Use

Fired by Controls.BoilerTemperatureControl in Examples.BoilerCircuit.

docs.title: HeatPump
docs.text:
Air-to-water heat pump (Buildings ModularReversible AirToWaterTableData2D, Vitocal 251-A08 scaled to its capacity) charging a mixed buffer; with set flows, the reference of its circuit (no mass balance)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.HeatPump, model (source)

Extends PartialFlow.

Purpose

Air-to-water heat pump at the compressor speed y, its performance from the table of the Viessmann Vitocal 251-A08 (HeatPumps.Vitocal251A08) scaled to Q_flow_nominal. It charges a mixed buffer at the temperature T, a storage tank or a hydraulic separator, from which the heating circuit draws at T. The source is the outdoor air of the weather bus.

Equations

With Qtab and Ptab the heating capacity and electrical power of the table, as smoothTable gives them at the condenser outlet temperature and the outdoor dry-bulb temperature Tsou:

Tcon,out = T + dTCon y,

Qcon = y s Qtab(Tcon,out, Tsou),   Pele = y s Ptab(Tcon,out, Tsou),   COP = Qtab/Ptab,

C dT/dt = mTra cp (TIn − T) + Qcon + UA (TAmb − T).

Both Qcon and Pele scale with y, so the COP is defined at every speed, also with the compressor off. The electricity meter EEle integrates Pele in kWh.

Parameters
  • scaFac (s): Q_flow_nominal over the capacity of the table at the supply temperature TSet and the outdoor temperature TOutDes, by the linear interpolation of interpolate.
  • mCon_flow: the condenser flow of the record scaled by scaFac; dTCon = Q_flow_nominal/(cp mCon_flow), the rise of the condenser outlet above the buffer at full speed.
  • useStorageTank: with a tank, the water volume is VTan and the heat loss conductance that of a cylinder of volume VTan and height hTan (side and both ends) insulated by dIns of conductivity kIns; without, a hydraulic separator without loss, of 1.5·10−5 m3 per W of Q_flow_nominal.
  • C: heat capacity of the buffer water and of the water in the condenser, taken as mCon_flow tauCon.
  • dTSou: width over which the kinks of the table in the source temperature are smoothed.
Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, the heat pump is the reference of its circuit: it has no mass balance, the circuit closes it. With pressure-driven flows, its outlets have the small linear conductance m_flow_nominal/dpLink, shared evenly by the outlet connections; the heating side of Buildings has no resistance.

Relation to Buildings

Buildings.Fluid.HeatPumps.ModularReversible.AirToWaterTableData2D with the Vitocal 251-A08 data, scaled to its capacity.

Use

Examples.HeatPumpCircuit: a buffer and two radiators in closed loop.

docs.title: Junction
docs.text:
Split valve: its inlets (port_1) mix, its outlets (port_2, port_3) leave at the mixed temperature; with pressure-driven flows the resistance of Buildings' Junction (dp_nominal[1] at m_flow_nominal[1], linearized) is placed on each outlet

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Junction, model (source)

Purpose

Split of a circuit into an outlet port_2 and a second outlet port_3 (e.g. the bypass of a ThreeWayValve). The connections of the inlet port_1 mix, and both outlets leave at the mixed temperature T.

Equations

Mixed temperature, with δ = m_flow_small and T̄1 the mean of the inlet temperatures:

T = (∑i wi T1,i + δ T̄1) / (∑i wi + δ),

where wi is the inlet flow with set flows and its positive part with pressure-driven flows.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, the junction conserves mass, ∑ port_1.m_flow + ∑ port_2.m_flow + ∑ port_3.m_flow = 0, and the split between the outlets is set by the rest of the circuit.

With pressure-driven flows, the inlet is a pressure node of small compliance and each outlet connection has the linear conductance G = |m_flow_nominal[1]| / max(dp_nominal[1], dpLink):

port_k[j].m_flow = −G (pin − pk,j),   τhyd G (n2 + n3) dpin/dt = sum of the flows of all ports.

Only dp_nominal[1] and m_flow_nominal[1] enter the equations; when dp_nominal[1] is not positive, the conductance takes dpLink.

Relation to Buildings

The resistance of Buildings.Fluid.FixedResistances.Junction on its first port, dp_nominal[1] at m_flow_nominal[1], linearized and placed on each outlet.

Use

The return of Examples.BoilerCircuit: to the boiler and to the bypass of the three-way valve. Junction2 is the same without the second outlet.

docs.title: PartialConserving
docs.text:
Mass is conserved: what enters leaves

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.PartialConserving, partial model (source)

Extends PartialFlow.

Purpose

PartialFlow with the mass balance of the component: with set flows, what enters leaves,

m_flow + ∑j port_b[j].m_flow = 0.

With pressure-driven flows, the balance is the equation of the pressure of the inlet node in PartialFlow: inflow and outflow differ only by the mass held in its small compliance.

Extending classes

They give TOut and, with pressure-driven flows, the flows of the outlets.

docs.title: PartialFlow
docs.text:
Water ports as arrays, one element per connection: the inlets mix, every outlet leaves at TOut; with pressure-driven flows, the inlets meet in a pressure node of small compliance

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.PartialFlow, partial model (source)

Purpose

Base class of the water components with one inlet and one outlet. Each port is an array with one element per connection (nPorts_a, nPorts_b): the inlets mix, every outlet leaves at TOut, and all inlets share the pressure pIn of the inlet node.

Equations

Flow through the component, from the inlets: ṁ = ∑i ṁa,i (m_flow).

Mixed inlet temperature, with δ = m_flow_small and T̄a the mean of the inlet temperatures:

Tin = (∑i wi Ta,i + δ T̄a) / (∑i wi + δ),

where wi = ṁa,i with set flows and wi = positivePart(ṁa,i, δ) with pressure-driven flows. At zero flow the inlet takes the mean inlet temperature, and TIn stays defined.

The flow that carries the inlet water through the component, used by the energy balances of the extending classes, is mTra = ṁ with set flows and positivePart(ṁ, δ) with pressure-driven flows, so that a flow reversing while the pressures settle carries no water backwards through the balance.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows
  • Set flows (pressureDriven = false): pIn = 0.
  • Pressure-driven flows: the inlet node is a pressure state of small compliance, τhyd Ghyd dpin/dt = ṁ + ∑j ṁb,j, with τhyd = tauHyd and Ghyd = GHyd. When GHyd is the conductance of the outlets, as the extending classes set it, the pressure of the node settles with the time constant tauHyd.
Extending classes

An extending class gives TOut and, with pressure-driven flows, the flow of every outlet port_b[j].m_flow from pIn and the pressure port_b[j].p of the node downstream. With set flows it adds the mass balance (PartialConserving), or leaves it to the circuit when the component is the reference of its circuit (Boiler, HeatPump).

docs.title: PartialLink
docs.text:
Pressure-driven outlets of a component without resistance in Buildings: a small linear one, dpLink at the nominal flow of each outlet. It must stay small against the branches it feeds: at 1000 Pa, the manifold of six radiators of the renovated house took a fifth of the head of the living room branch, whose valve then opened fully a third more often than in Buildings

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.PartialLink, partial model (source)

Extends PartialConserving.

Purpose

Pressure-driven outlets of a component that has no flow resistance in Buildings (a sensor, a pass-through). With pressure-driven flows every outlet needs a conductance; this class gives it a small linear one.

Equations

With pressure-driven flows, for each of the nb = nPorts_b outlets,

port_b[j].m_flow = −Glink (pin − pb,j),   Glink = m_flow_nominal / (nb dpLink),

so that the nominal flow, shared evenly by the outlets, passes at the pressure drop dpLink. The compliance of the inlet node is scaled by the total conductance GHyd = nb Glink. With set flows, the class adds nothing to PartialConserving.

Parameters

dpLink must stay small against the pressure drops of the branches the link feeds. At 1000 Pa, the manifold of six radiators of the renovated house took a fifth of the head of the living room branch, whose valve then opened fully a third more often than in Buildings; the default is 100 Pa.

Extending classes

They give TOut, e.g. Pipe and TemperatureSensor.

docs.text:
Pass-through (junctions, sensors, pumps without a power model)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Pipe, model (source)

Extends PartialLink.

Purpose

A pass-through: the water leaves at the mixed inlet temperature, TOut = TIn, without storage or heat loss. It stands for the components that change neither the temperature nor, in Buildings, the pressure: junctions, sensors, pumps without a power model.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, what enters leaves. With pressure-driven flows, each outlet has the small linear resistance of PartialLink: dpLink at the nominal flow.

docs.title: Pump
docs.text:
Pump: pass-through with set flows; with pressure-driven flows, the flow at its head from the curve of Buildings.Fluid.Movers.Preconfigured.SpeedControlled_y (1.14, 1 and 0.42 times dp_nominal at 0, 1 and 2 times the nominal flow), scaled to the speed y by the affinity laws

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Pump, model (source)

Extends PartialConserving.

Purpose

Circulation pump. With set flows the circuit flows are set by the valves and the pump only passes the water through and computes its power; with pressure-driven flows it delivers the flow of its curve at the head the circuit puts on it, at the relative speed y.

Equations

The water passes at the inlet temperature, TOut = TIn. The head is dp = p̄b − pin, p̄b the mean pressure of the nodes downstream (0 with set flows).

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, what enters leaves, and the electrical power is taken at the nominal head: P = dp_nominal ṁ / (ρ η), η = eta. The input y is not used.

With pressure-driven flows, the head of the pump relative to Δp0 = dp_nominal follows a parabola in the flow relative to the nominal flow, x, through the points (0, 1.14), (1, 1) and (2, 0.42):

h(x) = a + b x + c x2,   a = 1.14, b = 0.08, c = −0.22,

scaled to the speed y by the affinity laws (flow as y, head as y2). For each of the nb outlets, the flow is the root of the parabola at the head of that outlet:

xj = (−b − √positivePart(b2 − 4 c (a − hj), 10−3)) / (2 c),   hj = (pb,j − pin) / (Δp0 (y2 + 10−4)),

port_b[j].m_flow = −y m_flow_nominal xj / nb.

Beyond the shut-off head the argument of the root would be negative: positivePart keeps it positive and the flow stays at the top of the curve. The 10−4 keeps the relative head defined at y = 0. The power counts the forward head and flow only, P = positivePart(dp, 1) mTra / (ρ η), so the pump draws no negative power while the pressures settle. The compliance of the inlet node is scaled by m_flow_nominal/dp_nominal.

Relation to Buildings

The curve is that of Buildings.Fluid.Movers.Preconfigured.SpeedControlled_y: 1.14, 1 and 0.42 times dp_nominal at 0, 1 and 2 times the nominal flow. The electrical power is not added to the water (TOut = TIn).

Use

In Examples.BoilerCircuit, the speed follows the opening of the radiator valve through Controls.CollectorControl.

docs.title: Radiator
docs.text:
EN 442 radiator (Buildings RadiatorEN442_2): nEle water and metal elements in series

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Radiator, model (source)

Extends PartialConserving.

Purpose

Radiator after EN 442: nEle elements of water and metal in series, each giving heat to the room air (heatPortCon) and to the room surfaces (heatPortRad) by the power law of EN 442.

Equations

For element i at the water temperature Ti, with UA = UAEle, f = fraRad, n the exponent and δ = dT0:

Qcon,i = (1 − f) UA ΔTcon (ΔTcon2 + δ2)(n − 1)/2,   ΔTcon = Ti − Tair,

Qrad,i = f UA ΔTrad (ΔTrad2 + δ2)(n − 1)/2,   ΔTrad = Ti − Tsurf,

(C/nEle) dTi/dt = mTra cp (Ti−1 − Ti) − Qcon,i − Qrad,i,

with T0 = TIn; the water leaves at the temperature of the last element, TOut = TnEle. Far from ΔT = 0 the law is ΔT |ΔT|n − 1; around it, it is linear, its slope δn − 1 times the conductance, so the derivative stays finite where that of the exact power law does not. A radiator colder than the room takes heat from it.

The heat capacity C = ρ VWat cp + 500 J/(kg K) mDry is shared evenly by the elements. UAEle is computed by radiatorConductance so that the radiator gives Q_flow_nominal at the nominal temperatures and at the nominal flow m_flow_nominal = |Q_flow_nominal / (cp (T_a_nominal − T_b_nominal))|.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, what enters leaves. With pressure-driven flows, the outlets have the linear conductance m_flow_nominal/dp_nominal, shared evenly by the outlet connections.

Relation to Buildings

Buildings.Fluid.HeatExchangers.Radiators.RadiatorEN442_2, its pressure drop linearized.

Use

Connect heatPortCon to the air and heatPortRad to the radiant node of a zone, and a Valve in series, as in Examples.BoilerCircuit.

docs.title: ThreeWayValve
docs.text:
Mixing valve: the share y of the outlet flow comes from port_1 (supply), 1 - y from port_3 (set flows), or Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.Valves.ThreeWayEqualPercentageLinear, linearized: port_1 equal-percentage on y, port_3 linear on 1 - y (pressure-driven flows)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.ThreeWayValve, model (source)

Purpose

Mixing valve: the outlet port_2 takes water from the supply inlet port_1 and from the bypass inlet port_3, in the share set by y. The connections of each inlet mix first, at T1 and T3, as the inlets of PartialFlow do (weighted by the positive parts of their flows with pressure-driven flows).

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, y is the share of the supply in the outlet flow ṁ:

ṁ1 = y ṁ,   ṁ3 = (1 − y) ṁ,   T2 = y T1 + (1 − y) T3,

the outlet flow being set downstream, and the pressures p1, p3 are 0.

With pressure-driven flows, y is the opening of the supply path, limited to [0, 1] by smoothLimit (ys). Each path has the conductance of valveConductance with its fixed resistance in series:

PathCharacteristicPressure drop of the open pathFixed resistance supply, port_1 equalPercentage(ys, R, l[1], delta0) dpValve_nominaldpFixed_nominal[1] bypass, port_3 l[2] + (1 − ys) (1 − l[2]) dpValve_nominal/fraK2dpFixed_nominal[2]

Each inlet is a pressure node of small compliance, the outlet takes the mean pressure p2 of the nodes downstream:

ṁ1 = G1 (p1 − p2),   ṁ3 = G3 (p3 − p2),

τhyd G1,nom dp1/dt = ∑ port_1.m_flow − ṁ1,   τhyd G3,nom dp3/dt = ∑ port_3.m_flow − ṁ3,

with G1Nom and G3Nom the conductances of the open paths. The outlets share ṁ1 + ṁ3 evenly and leave at the temperature mixed with the positive parts of the two path flows (positivePart with 10−5 kg/s).

Parameters
  • fraK: Kv of the bypass path relative to the supply path; the open bypass drops dpValve_nominal/fraK2 at the nominal flow.
  • l: leakages of the supply and bypass paths.
Relation to Buildings

Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.Valves.ThreeWayEqualPercentageLinear, its flow laws linearized: the supply path equal-percentage in y, the bypass path linear in 1 − y.

docs.title: Valve
docs.text:
Two-way valve: sets the flow of its branch to ym_flow_nominal (set flows), or opens to y as Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.Valves.TwoWayEqualPercentage, linearized (pressure-driven flows)*

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.Valve, model (source)

Extends PartialConserving.

Purpose

Two-way valve of a branch, for instance the thermostatic valve of a radiator. The water passes at the inlet temperature, TOut = TIn.

Set flows and pressure-driven flows

With set flows, the valve sets the flow of its branch: ṁ = y m_flow_nominal, the input y being the flow relative to the nominal flow.

With pressure-driven flows, y is the opening. Limited to [0, 1] by smoothLimit (blends of 10−3), it gives the equal-percentage characteristic φ = equalPercentage(y, R, l, delta0): Ry − 1 above 1.5 delta0, linear from the leakage l at y = 0 below delta0/2, a cubic between. The conductance of the valve and of the pipes in series (valveConductance) is

G = m_flow_nominal / (dpFixed_nominal + dpValve_nominal / φ2),

and each of the nb outlets passes port_b[j].m_flow = −G (pin − pb,j) / nb: the flow is linear in the pressure drop at a given opening. The compliance of the inlet node is scaled by the conductance of the open valve and its pipes, GNom.

Relation to Buildings

docs.title: radiatorConductance
docs.text:
UAEle of Buildings RadiatorEN442_2: the conductance of each element giving the nominal power (bisections)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.radiatorConductance, function (source)

Purpose

Conductance UAEle of each element of a Radiator such that the radiator gives Q_flow_nominal at its nominal temperatures and flow.

Algorithm

The nominal flow is ṁ = Q_flow_nominal / (cp (T_a_nominal − T_b_nominal)). Starting from the conductance of a single element at the mean water temperature,

UA0 = Q_flow_nominal / (((T_a_nominal + T_b_nominal)/2 − ((1 − f) TAir_nominal + f TRad_nominal))n nEle),

80 bisections on [UA0/10, 10 UA0] find the conductance at which the nEle elements in series give Q_flow_nominal. For a given conductance, the water of each element is at the temperature Tw it leaves with, solved by 80 bisections between min(TAir_nominal, TRad_nominal) and the temperature of the water entering it:

Tw = Tup − Qele(Tw) / (ṁ cp),   Qele = UA (f max(Tw − TRad_nominal, 0)n + (1 − f) max(Tw − TAir_nominal, 0)n),

with f = fraRad, and the water leaving one element enters the next.

Relation to Buildings

The parameter UAEle of Buildings.Fluid.HeatExchangers.Radiators.RadiatorEN442_2.

Use

Called in the binding of the parameter UAEle of Radiator. It depends on parameters only, so its branches and its max cause no event in the model.

docs.title: interpolate
docs.text:
Linear interpolation in the table, as CombiTable2Ds (rows: condenser, columns: source)

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.HeatPumps.Vitocal251A08.interpolate, function (source)

Purpose

Heating capacity (heating = true) or electrical power of the Vitocal 251-A08 at a condenser outlet temperature and a source temperature, by linear interpolation in the table: first along the source temperature TSou in each row, then along the condenser outlet temperature TCon between the rows. Beyond the first and last breakpoints of either axis the value is held at the edge of the table.

Use

The value of the table at design conditions, for the scaling scaFac of HeatPump. It is evaluated from parameters only; the model itself uses the differentiable smoothTable.

Relation to Buildings

Within the table, the linear interpolation of CombiTable2Ds (rows: condenser, columns: source).

docs.title: smoothTable
docs.text:
Quadratic in the condenser temperature through the rows at 35, 45 and 55 degC, linear between the source columns with the kinks smoothed over dTSou: a differentiable version of the table

FastSmoothBuildings.Hydronics.HeatPumps.Vitocal251A08.smoothTable, function (source)

Purpose

Heating capacity (heating = true) or electrical power of the Vitocal 251-A08 at a condenser outlet temperature and a source temperature: a version of the table with continuous derivatives, for the equations of HeatPump.

Equations

In the condenser outlet temperature Tc, a quadratic through the first three rows of the table, at TC,1, TC,2, TC,3 = 35, 45 and 55 °C, with the Lagrange basis

Lk(Tc) = ∏m ≠ k (Tc − TC,m) / (TC,k − TC,m),   vj = ∑k=1..3 Lk Yk,j

at each source temperature TS,j of the table, Y being QHea or PEle. In the source temperature Ts, the piecewise linear interpolation of the vj, written as the first segment plus the change of slope at each inner breakpoint, each kink smoothed by positivePart over δ = dTSou:

y = v1 + s1 (Ts − TS,1) + ∑j=2..8 (sj − sj−1) positivePart(Ts − TS,j, δ),   sj = (vj+1 − vj) / (TS,j+1 − TS,j).

Accuracy
  • At 35, 45 and 55 °C the quadratic passes through the rows of the table; the rows at 65 and 70 °C are not used, and above 55 °C the quadratic extrapolates.
  • At a distance x from a breakpoint of the source temperature, the value differs from the linear interpolation by (√(x2 + δ2) − |x|)/2 times the change of slope there: δ/2 at the breakpoint, about δ2/(4 |x|) away from it.
  • Below the first and above the last source temperature of the table, the value follows the first and the last segment: it extrapolates linearly, where interpolate holds the edge value.

docs.title: UsersGuide
docs.text:
User's Guide

FastSmoothBuildings.UsersGuide, package (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Information.

Class Description Conventions Conventions Smoothing Smoothing Translation Translation into CasADi ReleaseNotes Release notes License License Contact Contact

FastSmoothBuildings models a building and its systems as one explicit ordinary differential equation dx/dt = f(t, x, u, p), smooth in its states, inputs and parameters. The same classes give two models of a building:

  • a closed-loop model, with the controllers of the library and pressure-driven water circuits, to simulate the building as Buildings would, and to calibrate it on measurements;
  • a model for optimal control, with the controls of the systems (valve openings, pump speeds, compressor and burner loads) as inputs and set flows in the water circuits, that rumoca translates into CasADi for model predictive control and state estimation.

The pages of this guide:

  • Conventions: units, signs, geometry, constructions and the names of the states;
  • Smoothing: how switches, limits and schedules stay differentiable;
  • Translation into CasADi: what keeps a model translatable by rumoca;
  • Release notes, License, Contact.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
Contact

FastSmoothBuildings.UsersGuide.Contact, class (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Information.

Questions, bugs and contributions: github.com/andoludo/FastSmoothBuildings.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Conventions

FastSmoothBuildings.UsersGuide.Conventions, class (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Information.

Units and signs
  • SI units throughout; temperatures in kelvin.
  • A heat port carries the temperature of its node and the heat flow rate into the component.
  • A water port carries the mass flow rate into the component (negative when the water leaves), the temperature of the water crossing it, set by the component the water leaves, and the pressure of the inlet node of the component downstream (0 with set flows).
  • An air port of the ventilation carries the mass flow rate into the component, the temperature of the air crossing it and the relative speed of the fan that moves it.
  • Internal gains are given per floor area (W/m2), split into a convective and a radiant part.
Geometry
  • Azimuth of a surface: 0 facing south, π/2 facing west.
  • Tilt: 0 for a roof or a ceiling (the surface faces up), π/2 for a wall, π for a floor (see Types.Tilt).
  • Side a of a construction is the outside, side b the room; the layers of a construction and the panes of a glazing are given from the outside.
Constructions and states

Each layer of an opaque construction is split into nSta sublayers of equal thickness, with a node at each sublayer boundary. The temperatures of the layer boundaries are T, those of the nodes inside the layers TSub. A model for optimal control uses one sublayer per layer (no TSub); a closed-loop model up to three, as Buildings: a state copied from one model into the other by its name stays at its place.

The records Data.Construction and Data.Glazing carry the counts of layers, sublayers and panes, and the indices of the nodes, written out (see Translation into CasADi).

Water circuits

Every component of Hydronics has the evaluated parameter pressureDriven:

  • false (set flows): each valve sets the flow of its branch and the production closes the balance; the model of optimal control;
  • true (pressure-driven flows): a pressure node at the inlet of every component, the flow of every outlet from its conductance, the pumps on their curves, as the linearized circuits of Buildings; the closed-loop model.

docs.title: Smoothing
docs.text:
Smoothing

FastSmoothBuildings.UsersGuide.Smoothing, class (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Information.

A model of the library has no event: no when, pre, sample or if on a variable that would switch during the simulation. Where Buildings switches, the library blends:

FunctionReplaces regStep a step: once continuously differentiable over a given width smoothMax, smoothMinmax, min smoothLimit a limiter: exactly at its bounds beyond the blends, never outside them positivePart max(x, 0) timeOfDay, occupancy, dayTable daily schedules, without the events of a table or a clock

The controllers of Controls are written with them: a hysteresis is a fast bistable state, a PI controller has an anti-windup and a smooth reset, a change of set point takes dtSet. The width of every transition and the switching time of every hysteresis are parameters (dU, dY, dMax, dT, dtSet, tau), at values that reproduce the switching controllers by default: a model exported for calibration or optimal control can widen them.

docs.title: Translation
docs.text:
Translation into CasADi

FastSmoothBuildings.UsersGuide.Translation, class (source)

Extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Information.

rumoca translates a model of the library into a CasADi function dx/dt = f(t, x, u, p), the inputs u being the top-level inputs of the model (weather, gains, controls). From Python, with the package fastsmoothbuildings: 

import rumoca
import fastsmoothbuildings

session = rumoca.Session(roots=[str(fastsmoothbuildings.LIBRARY)])
model = session.loads(source, model="MyBuilding.building").to_casadi()

The library keeps to what rumoca translates, and a model built from it has to as well:

  • the sizes of arrays and the subscripts are evaluated from literal parameters only, not from a sum, a function or the default of a record: the records of the constructions carry their counts and node indices written out;
  • the model is an explicit ODE: no algebraic loop that rumoca would have to solve, no event;
  • every function is smooth (see Smoothing), and conditions on parameters only are evaluated before the translation;
  • equations carry no description strings;
  • a table given to dayTable is a parameter, not a literal matrix in the call, and at the top level of a model the call is an equation, not the binding of a declaration: rumoca 0.10.3 expands the loop of the function into extra equations otherwise (the zones and the ideal systems of the library call it this way).

The release 0.10.3 of rumoca on PyPI keeps "residual projection stages" for five more shapes, which its CasADi target refuses (residual_equations, initialization); the library avoids them:

  • in a function, a variable set by an if-expression and used by a later statement: one assignment per function, as smoothLimit calls smoothLimitBelow and smoothLimitAbove;
  • in a function, a scalar reassigned in a loop (an accumulation, or a value passed to a smooth function): an array element per step, or one sum;
  • in an equation, a smooth function of a smooth function (smoothMin(a, smoothMax(b, c))): the inner value in a variable of its own;
  • in a for loop of equations, a derivative multiplied by a coefficient (C[i]*der(T[i]) = Q[i]): the derivative alone, der(T[i]) = Q[i]/C[i];
  • a parameter bound to an if-expression whose branch is more than a name or a literal: the branch in a parameter of its own.

The library translates with rumoca 0.10.3 from PyPI and with the commit 33c21141 of its main branch; the release 0.10.2 does not export connected models to CasADi.

docs.text:

docs.title: convectionCoefficient
docs.text:
Natural convection coefficient of Buildings for a surface tilt: wall 1.3, ceiling 0.76/1.51, floor 1.51/0.76

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.convectionCoefficient, function (source)

Purpose

The coefficient c of the natural convection law q = c |ΔT|1/3 ΔT of Buildings (see naturalConvection), in W/(m2 K4/3), from the tilt of the surface and the sign of the temperature difference.

Equations SurfaceTiltSurface warmer than the airSurface colder Ceilingsin(til) = 0, cos(til) > 00.761.51 Floorsin(til) = 0, cos(til) < 01.510.76 Any other1.31.3

A surface counts as horizontal when |sin(til)| < 10−6; an inclined surface takes the coefficient of a wall. A warm ceiling and a cold floor stratify the air: the lower coefficient.

Use

The function switches on its arguments: call it on parameters only, as the surfaces do (til for the room side, pi - til for a side that faces the other way: the outside of a window, side b of an internal wall), so that the coefficients are evaluated before the simulation. The tilt follows Types.Tilt.

docs.title: dayTable
docs.text:
Linear interpolation in a day table [time of day (s), value], repeated daily

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.dayTable, function (source)

Purpose

Linear interpolation in a day table, without the events of a table: rows [time of day (s), value], the time increasing, evaluated at the time of day tod, typically timeOfDay(time).

Equations

With the rows (ti, vi), i = 1 … n:

  • y = v1 up to t1;
  • between ti and ti+1, the linear interpolation of vi and vi+1; where the table repeats an instant, the denominator is bounded by 10−6 s: a step;
  • after tn, a linear return from vn to v1, reached at t1 + 86400 s.

The result is continuous and piecewise linear (C0) apart from the repeated instants, and continuous across midnight when t1 = 0. A table of one row is a constant.

Use

The table is a parameter, not a literal matrix in the call, and at the top level of a model the call is an equation, not the binding of a declaration (see Translation into CasADi). The zones read their ventilation schedule with it.

docs.title: equalPercentage
docs.text:
Equal-percentage valve characteristic with leakage (Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.BaseClasses.equalPercentage): linear below delta0/2, R^(y-1) above 1.5delta0, a cubic Hermite joining them*

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.equalPercentage, function (source)

Purpose

Equal-percentage characteristic φ(y) of a valve with leakage, once continuously differentiable.

Equations

With the rangeability R, the leakage l and δ0 = delta0:

Rangeφ y < δ0/2 l + y (Rδ0−1 − l)/δ0 δ0/2 ≤ y ≤ 1.5 δ0 cubic Hermite polynomial matching the value and slope of both neighbours y > 1.5 δ0Ry−1

φ(0) = l, φ(1) = 1; the linear branch passes through Rδ0−1 at y = δ0. C1.

Relation to Buildings

Buildings.Fluid.Actuators.BaseClasses.equalPercentage.

Use

The two-way and three-way valves of Hydronics pass it, their opening limited to [0, 1] by smoothLimit, to valveConductance.

docs.title: naturalConvection
docs.text:
Heat flow from a surface to the air q = Ac|dT|^(4/3) (Buildings natural convection), smooth at dT = 0

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.naturalConvection, function (source)

Purpose

Heat flow rate from a surface to the air by natural convection, Q = A c |ΔT|1/3 ΔT as in Buildings, regularised at small temperature differences so that it is infinitely differentiable.

Equations

With ΔT = dT, the surface minus the air temperature, and ΔT0 = dT0,

Q = A ((c+ + c−)/2 + (c+ − c−)/2 ΔT/√(ΔT2 + ΔT02)) ΔT (ΔT2 + ΔT02)1/6.

For |ΔT| >> ΔT0, Q tends to A c+ ΔT4/3 when the surface is warmer (cPos) and to −A c− |ΔT|4/3 when it is colder (cNeg). At ΔT = 0 the conductance is A (c+ + c−)/2 ΔT01/3 instead of 0, and the switch between the two coefficients is spread over a few ΔT0. C-infinity for ΔT0 > 0.

Use

dT0 = 0.1 K by default. The coefficients come from convectionCoefficient; the interior convection and the exterior exchange of the surfaces call this function when no fixed coefficient is given.

docs.title: occupancy
docs.text:
1 between the pairs of instants of a day schedule {on, off, on, off, ...} [s] (Buildings OccupancySchedule with firstEntryOccupied), each change a smooth step over dt

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.occupancy, function (source)

Purpose

Occupancy from a day schedule of instants {on, off, on, off, …} in seconds since midnight: 1 between the instants of each pair, 0 outside, each change a smooth step without events.

Equations

With the schedule s and Δt = dt,

y = ∑k [regStep(tday − s2k−1, 1, 0, Δt/2) − regStep(tday − s2k, 1, 0, Δt/2)],

over the complete pairs (a last unpaired instant is ignored). Each change is a regStep over Δt centred on its instant: C1, with the value 1/2 at the instant itself. The result stays in [0, 1] when the instants increase and are at least Δt apart, and is continuous across midnight when they lie between Δt/2 and 86400 s − Δt/2.

Relation to Buildings

The schedule of Buildings.Controls.SetPoints.OccupancySchedule with firstEntryOccupied = true; the result is a Real between 0 and 1 instead of a Boolean.

Use

Call it with tod = timeOfDay(time); dt = 60 s by default. See Validation.Schedules.

Purpose

Value of a polynomial, its coefficients from the constant term up.

Equations

docs.title: polynomialFit
docs.text:
Least-squares quartic c[1] + c[2]x + ... + c[5]x^4 through 10 points (x, y)

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.polynomialFit, function (source)

Purpose

Least-squares fit of a quartic c1 + c2 x + … + c5 x4 through 10 points (xk, yk).

Equations

The normal equations A c = b, with Aij = ∑k xki+j−2 and bi = ∑k yk xki−1, solved by Gaussian elimination without pivoting (the normal matrix is symmetric positive definite when at least five of the xk differ) and back substitution.

Use

Called on parameters: the windows fit the solar transmittance and the absorptance of each pane, given at the incidence angles 0, 10, …, 90 degrees, as quartics in the cosine of the angle, and evaluate them with polynomial.

docs.title: positivePart
docs.text:
Smooth max(x, 0): 0.5(x + sqrt(x^2 + delta^2))*

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.positivePart, function (source)

Purpose

Smooth approximation of max(x, 0), strictly positive: a flow or a cosine that can divide or weight without a singularity at 0.

Equations

y = (x + √(x2 + δ2))/2.

Infinitely differentiable (C-infinity) for δ > 0. Always above max(x, 0): y = δ/2 at x = 0, and the difference (√(x2 + δ2) − |x|)/2 tends to δ2/(4|x|) for |x| >> δ: y tends to 0 for x → −∞ and to x for x → ∞.

Use

delta is the width of the rounding, in the unit of x; unlike smoothMax, the result is nowhere exact.

docs.title: quadraticFlow
docs.text:
Flow through a quadratic resistance (m_flow_nominal at dp_nominal), regularized below deltaMm_flow_nominal*

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.quadraticFlow, function (source)

Purpose

Mass flow rate through a quadratic flow resistance, Δp = Δpnom (ṁ/ṁnom)2, regularised at small flows so that it is infinitely differentiable.

Equations

ṁ = ṁnom/√Δpnom · Δp / (Δp2 + (δm2 Δpnom)2)1/4,   δm = deltaM.

For |Δp| >> δm2 Δpnom, the pressure drop of the flow δm ṁnom, the flow tends to sign(Δp) ṁnom √(|Δp|/Δpnom); near Δp = 0 it is linear, ṁ ≈ ṁnom Δp / (δm Δpnom). Odd in Δp, C-infinity for δm > 0.

Use

deltaM = 0.1 by default. The boiler computes the flows of its outlets with it when the flows are pressure-driven.

docs.title: regStep
docs.text:
Once continuously differentiable step from y2 (x < -x_small) to y1 (x > x_small)

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.regStep, function (source)

Purpose

A step from y2 to y1 around x = 0 whose value and first derivative are continuous. It replaces the if conditions and the events of a switch, so that the model stays an explicit ODE with continuous derivatives that CasADi and IPOPT can differentiate.

Equations

With ε = x_small,

RangeValue x > εy = y1 x < −εy = y2 |x| ≤ ε y = (x/ε) ((x/ε)2 − 3) (y2 − y1)/4 + (y1 + y2)/2

The cubic meets both constants with a zero slope at x = ±ε; its slope at x = 0 is 3 (y1 − y2)/(4 ε).

Relation to Buildings

The same function as Buildings.Utilities.Math.Functions.regStep, without its derivative annotation (rumoca differentiates the expression itself).

Use

The width ε is the trade-off of every smooth switch of the library: the wider it is, the easier the optimal control problem and the further the model from the switching controller it replaces. The controllers of FastSmoothBuildings.Controls expose it as a parameter.
