docs.title: smoothLimit
docs.text:
Once continuously differentiable limitation of x to [l, u]: exactly l below l - deltaX and u above u + deltaX, x between l + deltaX and u - deltaX, quadratic blends in between that never leave [l, u]

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.smoothLimit, function (source)

Purpose

Limitation of x to [l, u], once continuously differentiable and without events: exactly at the bounds beyond the blends, never outside them (see Smoothing).

Equations

With δ = deltaX, x is first limited from below to z (smoothLimitBelow), then z from above to y (smoothLimitAbove):

RangeValue x < l − δz = l |x − l| ≤ δ z = l + (x − l + δ)2/(4 δ) x > l + δz = x z < u − δy = z |z − u| ≤ δ y = u − (u + δ − z)2/(4 δ) z > u + δy = u

Each parabola meets the constant bound with a zero slope and the identity with a unit slope (C1). The result is l below l − δ, u above u + δ, x between l + δ and u − δ, and non-decreasing in x.

Use

deltaX is the half width of the blends; below (u − l)/2, the result stays within [l, u]. The controllers limit their outputs with it, and the valves their opening.

docs.title: smoothLimitAbove
docs.text:
Once continuously differentiable limitation of x from above by u: exactly u above u + deltaX, x below u - deltaX

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.smoothLimitAbove, function (source)

Limitation of x from above by u, once continuously differentiable and without events: the second half of smoothLimit, which applies smoothLimitBelow, then it.

docs.title: smoothLimitInside
docs.text:
Once continuously differentiable limitation of x to [l + deltaX, u - deltaX], strictly inside [l, u] (for arguments of functions singular at the bounds, as acos at -1 and 1)

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.smoothLimitInside, function (source)

Purpose

Limitation of x strictly inside [l, u], once continuously differentiable: for the argument of a function singular at the bounds, as acos and asin at −1 and 1.

Equations

With δ = deltaX,

y = smoothMin(smoothMax(x, l + δ, δ), u − δ, δ),

with smoothMax and smoothMin. For u − l ≥ 4 δ: y = l + δ for x < l, y = x between l + 2 δ and u − 2 δ, y = u − δ for x > u. In the blends the result passes at most 0.087 δ beyond l + δ and u − δ, so it stays at least 0.91 δ away from the bounds. C1.

Use

The weather and the windows bound the cosines they give to acos and asin with it, whose derivatives are infinite at −1 and 1.

docs.title: smoothMax
docs.text:
Once continuously differentiable approximation of max(x1, x2)

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.smoothMax, function (source)

Purpose

Once continuously differentiable approximation of max(x1, x2), without events (see Smoothing).

Equations

y = regStep(x1 − x2, x1, x2, Δx): y = x1 when x1 − x2 > Δx, y = x2 when x1 − x2 < −Δx, and in between a weighted mean of the two arguments whose weight goes from 0 to 1 along the cubic of regStep.

The result is exact outside the blend and continuous with its first derivative (C1). Inside the blend it lies between the two arguments, at most 0.087 Δx below max(x1, x2); it equals it when x1 = x2.

Use

deltaX (> 0) is the half width of the blend, in the unit of the arguments. The arguments are those of Buildings.Utilities.Math.Functions.smoothMax.

docs.title: timeOfDay
docs.text:
Seconds since midnight, without events

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.timeOfDay, function (source)

Purpose

Time of day, in seconds since midnight, without the events of floor.

Equations

tday = t − 86400 floor(t/86400), inside noEvent.

A sawtooth from 0 to 86400 s that drops back to 0 at each midnight (t a multiple of 86400 s), with a slope of 1 in between: discontinuous at midnight, but without an event.

Use

The argument of the daily schedules occupancy and dayTable: a schedule whose values at 0 and 86400 s are equal stays continuous across midnight. See also Validation.Schedules.

docs.title: valveConductance
docs.text:
Conductance m_flow/dp of a valve with a fixed resistance in series, its flow law linearized as Buildings does (linearized=true): m_flowm_flow_nominal = k^2dp, 1/k^2 = 1/kFixed^2 + 1/(phiKv)^2*

FastSmoothBuildings.Utilities.valveConductance, function (source)

Purpose

Conductance G = ṁ/Δp of a valve and a fixed resistance in series, the flow law linearized as Buildings does with linearized = true.

Equations

G = 1 / (ṁnom (Δpfix,nom/ṁnom2 + Δpval,nom/(φ ṁnom)2)),

that is ṁ ṁnom = k2 Δp with 1/k2 = 1/kfix2 + 1/(φ Kv)2, kfix2 = ṁnom2/Δpfix,nom, Kv2 = ṁnom2/Δpval,nom. Fully open (φ = 1), the valve passes ṁnom under Δpval,nom + Δpfix,nom.

Use

φ must stay positive: the valves give the characteristic of equalPercentage, at least its leakage.

Purpose

A duct of a balanced ventilation: it carries its nominal flow times the relative speed of the fan of its unit, read from its inlet, without heat losses or pressure.

ṁ = ∑ port_a[i].m_flow = port_a[1].y ṁnominal,   ∑ port_b[i].m_flow = −ṁ,

docs.title: HeatRecoveryUnit
docs.text:
Balanced ventilation with a constant-effectiveness heat recovery and constant-pressure fans (trano's system D); the reference of its air loop

FastSmoothBuildings.Ventilation.HeatRecoveryUnit, model (source)

Purpose

Air handling unit of a balanced ventilation (trano's system D): outdoor air through a heat recovery of constant effectiveness, warmed by constant-pressure fans, and the electricity of the fans metered. The unit is the reference of its air loop: it sets the speed y that the ducts downstream turn into their flows, and the supply air temperature.

Equations

Mixed extract air temperature, regularised by m_flow_small so that it is defined at zero flow (the mean of the port temperatures):

TExt = (∑ ṁi Ti + ṁsmall ∑ Ti/n) / (∑ ṁi + ṁsmall).

Supply air and fans:

TSup = TDryBul + ε (TExt − TDryBul) + ΔTFan,   PFan = y (PSup + PRet),   dEFan/dt = PFan/3.6·106 (kWh),

with the fan powers at nominal flow PSup = ΔpSup ṁnominal/(ρAir ηFan), likewise PRet, and the heating of the supply air by the fans (supply fan after the exchanger, return fan before it) ΔTFan = (PSup + ε PRet) / (ṁnominal cp). The power of constant-pressure fans and the flow are both proportional to y, so ΔTFan is the same at every speed.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning m_flow_nominal nominal supply flow eps0.8heat recovery effectiveness dpSup_nominal, dpRet_nominal200 Pa pressure rises of the supply and return fans etaFan0.5overall efficiency of the fans m_flow_small10−6 kg/s regularisation of the mixed extract temperature nPorts_a, nPorts_b1 numbers of extract and supply connections Use

Connect the weather to weaBus, the supply port_b through a Duct to a Zones.VentilatedZone and its extract back through another duct to port_a, as in Examples.VentilatedRoom.

Purpose

docs.title: PartialZone
docs.text:
Room air, long-wave exchange between its surfaces, distribution of the transmitted solar radiation

FastSmoothBuildings.Zones.PartialZone, partial model (source)

Purpose

Base class of the thermal zones: the heat balance of the room air, the long-wave exchange between the surfaces through a radiant star, the distribution of the transmitted solar radiation, infiltration, scheduled outdoor air and internal gains. Each surface connects to an element of propsBus. An extending class gives QVen, the heat brought by a ventilation system.

Equations

Long-wave exchange. Each surface i of emissivity εi, area Ai and temperature Ti exchanges with a radiant star through

Gi = 4 σ TLin3 εi Ai,   TRad = (∑ Gi Ti + QRad,emi + AFlo qRad) / ∑ Gi,

with TLin = T0Rad when linearizeRadiation is true, and otherwise the mean surface temperature weighted by εi Ai, explicit in the states of the surfaces. The radiant heat of the emitters (heaPorRad) and the radiant internal gains reach the surfaces in proportion to εi Ai; heaPorRad is at the mean surface temperature ∑ Gi Ti / ∑ Gi.

Transmitted solar radiation. With ai and τi the solar absorptance and transmittance of the surfaces, each surface absorbs

  • of the diffuse radiation the share ai Ai / ∑ (aj + τj) Aj;
  • of the direct radiation, if the zone has floors: a floor ai Ai / AFloSur, and the other surfaces share what the floors reflect, in proportion to ai Ai over the sum of (aj + τj) Aj of the surfaces that are not floors; without floors, as the diffuse radiation.

The heat to the radiation side of surface i is Gi (TRad − Ti) plus its absorbed solar radiation.

Room air. With ρ = pAtm/(RAir TAir) and ṁVen the scheduled outdoor air flow,

fmSen ρ cp V dTAir/dt = ∑ Qcon,i + QCon,emi + AFlo qCon + (ρ V ACH/3600 + ṁVen) cp (TDryBul − TAir) + QVen,

where Qcon,i is the convective heat of surface i, held at TAir, QCon,emi the heat of heaPorAir and qCon, qRad the internal gains per floor area. The infiltration is a volume flow of zone air at the pressure of the site; ṁVen is interpolated in ventilationSchedule by dayTable, repeated daily.

Parameters NameDefaultMeaning nSurf number of surfaces AFlo, hRoo floor area and height VAFlo hRooair volume ACH0 1/hair changes per hour by infiltration of outdoor air ventilationSchedule[0, 0] outdoor air on top of the infiltration: time since midnight (s) and mass flow rate (kg/s); a step where the table repeats an instant mSenFac1factor for the sensible heat capacity of the air T_start294.15 Kinitial air temperature hConInt, hConExt0 fixed interior and exterior convection coefficients passed to the surfaces, 0 for the natural and the wind laws T0Rad293.15 Klinearization temperature of the long-wave exchange linearizeRadiationtrue linearise at T0Rad, or at the current mean surface temperature Relation to Buildings

After Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed.MixedAir. The radiant star is the exact equivalent of the linearized radiosity exchange of Buildings with view factors Aj/∑ A; the transmitted solar radiation is distributed as in its SolarRadiationExchange; the infiltration is ACH V times the density of the zone air at the pressure of the site, as in Buildings. linearizeRadiation = true is the default of Buildings; false comes close to its exact exchange.

Use

Extended by Zone (no ventilation system) and VentilatedZone (supply and extract air).

docs.title: VentilatedZone
docs.text:
Thermal zone with supply and extract air of a ventilation unit

FastSmoothBuildings.Zones.VentilatedZone, model (source)

Extends PartialZone.

Purpose

A thermal zone with the supply and extract air of a ventilation unit: PartialZone with air ports.

Equations

QVen = ∑ ṁa,i cp (Ta,i − TAir) over the supply ports ports_a.

The extract ports ports_b leave at the zone air temperature and pass on the mean fan speed of the supply ports, so that the extract ducts downstream run at the speed of the supply ones.

Parameters

nPorts_a = 1 supply and nPorts_b = 1 extract connections, and those of PartialZone.

Use

Connect a Duct from the supply of a HeatRecoveryUnit to ports_a and another from ports_b back to its extract, as in Examples.VentilatedRoom.

docs.title: Migration from trano's FastModel, phase 0: trials
docs.text: Phase 0 of the migration of trano's FastModel package (trano/library/FastModel.mo) to the FastSmoothBuildings library tried the split into the directory layout and its use from OpenModelica and rumoca before anything was pushed. Source: trano commit c70f8d2 (branch feat/smooth-controller-parameters, PR #60), OpenModelica 1.26.9, rumoca 0.10.3.

docs.title: 1. The split
docs.text:
scripts/migration/split_library.py renames the package (FastModel → FastSmoothBuildings; the library refers to itself by its full name once, extends FastSmoothBuildings.Icons.Package, and two description strings name trano's configurations, now FastSmoothBuildings and FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) and writes the directory layout of the Modelica specification (13.4):

  • every package that holds a model, block, function, connector or record (directly or below) is a folder with package.mo and package.order: 15 folders;
  • every other class of such a package is a file <name>.mo: 92 files; Icons and Types (constants only) stay one file each, as in Buildings;
  • constants and short classes (connector RealInput = input Real) stay in package.mo; package.order lists classes and constants in the order of the source.

fastsmoothbuildings.bundle.bundle() writes the folder back as one file (to embed it in a generated model). The split checks that the bundle gives back the renamed source character for character.

docs.title: 2. OpenModelica
docs.text:
Check Single file Folder (MODELICAPATH) messages while loading (missing or extra package.order entries) none none classes (getClassNames(recursive=true)) 112 the same 112 checkModel of the 38 models and blocks that are not partial 31 pass the same output, word for word

The 7 models that do not check are the walls, the window and the zones: their construction records have no defaults on purpose (nLay, nPan, nSurf must be literal for rumoca), so they check only inside a model that gives them a record; phase 1 adds such examples.

The runnable models of four trano inputs, generated with the library embedded and with the library loaded from the folder, simulated for two days (tolerance 1e-6, 576 intervals) give the same values for every variable, bit for bit:

Input Variables tests/models/single_zone_hydronic.yaml 1634 BESTEST 960 (sun-space) 2142 examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml 8116 examples/residential_after_renovation.yaml 9249

docs.title: 3. rumoca and CasADi
docs.text:
For six inputs, each as MPC model and as closed-loop model (12 exports), rumoca.Session().loads of the model with the library embedded (as trano writes it) and rumoca.Session(roots=[...]).loads of the model with the library referenced from the folder give the same CasADi model: the same names of states, inputs and parameters, and no difference in the start states, the parameters and the derivatives at four times of the day.

Input MPC: states / inputs / parameters Closed loop: states / inputs / parameters Translation, embedded / roots (s) BESTEST 600FF 25 / 9 / 550 54 / 9 / 782 2.9–3.2 / 2.7 BESTEST 630 (overhang, fins) 27 / 10 / 667 60 / 9 / 923 4.0–4.3 / 4.0 BESTEST 960 42 / 12 / 835 96 / 11 / 1259 4.1–4.8 / 4.0–4.3 single_zone_hydronic 27 / 12 / 758 52 / 9 / 903 6.3–7.0 / 6.8–6.9 residential_after_renovation 189 / 28 / 4165 278 / 19 / 4770 43–50 / 45 residential_before_renovation 160 / 27 / 3544 224 / 19 / 3955 38 / 40–41

Loading from roots costs no time.

docs.title: Found: the records name the embedded copy
docs.text: trano's three data templates (library.json, construction twice and glazing) write record x = <package>.FastModel.Data.Construction(...): the qualified name of the copy inside the generated package, the one thing that stops a reference to the library. Written as FastSmoothBuildings.Data.Construction, the name finds the embedded copy first (Modelica looks in the enclosing packages) and the library otherwise: with the library embedded, the 6 exports tried and the OpenModelica simulation of single_zone_hydronic are identical to the qualified names. Phase 2 writes the plain name, so that the switch to a reference (phase 3) needs no change of these templates.

docs.title: 4. Documentation
docs.text:
Utilities.regStep and Envelope.Functions.gapConductance carry a sample of the documentation of phase 4 (purpose, equations as implemented, smoothing, relation to Buildings, validation, references, revisions) in HTML with tables, sub- and superscripts, entities, escaped quotes and modelica:// links; phase 1 kept it in both classes. The documentation of gapConductance as a browser shows it: phase0/gap_conductance_documentation.png.

  • OpenModelica loads it without a message and getDocumentationAnnotation returns it whole (3687 characters for gapConductance, the quotes unescaped, the links kept);
  • rumoca translates the models with it, from the folder and embedded, to the same CasADi model.

A copy with a 3 kB documentation on each of the 107 files (a bundle of 494 896 characters, three times the 163 390 of the library today) measures the cost: OpenModelica loads it, as folder and as one file, and checks every class as without it; rumoca translates it to the same CasADi model, from the folder and embedded, in the same time (best of three):

MPC model No documentation (roots) Sample (roots / embedded) 3 kB on every file (roots / embedded / embedded, stripped) single_zone_hydronic 6.3 s 6.5 / 6.4 s 6.4 / 6.2 / 6.6 s residential_after_renovation 42.2 s 43.3 / 42.5 s 44.4 / 43.1 / 42.6 s

strip_documentation (the documentation removed from the bundle) gives the same model too, but is not needed for speed.

docs.title: Found: the bundle must put the classes before the annotation of their package
docs.text: The first bundle put the classes of a folder at the end of its package.mo, after the annotation of the package: not valid Modelica (an annotation ends a class), which rumoca refused once the packages had a Documentation. bundle() now inserts them before the annotation; the folder itself was never affected.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The split, the bundle and both ways of using the library (embedded or referenced) give the same models in OpenModelica and in CasADi. Phase 1 can create the repository from the split.

Scripts of the trials (outside the repository): equivalence.py (rumoca), om_simulate.py and the check_*.mos scripts (OpenModelica), documentation.py (documentation and timing).

docs.title: Migration from trano's FastModel, phase 1: the repository
docs.text: Phase 1 created this repository from trano's FastModel package at trano commit c70f8d2 (PR andoludo/trano#60).

docs.title: What it holds
docs.text:
• main starts with the 23 commits of trano that changed trano/library/FastModel.mo, imported with git filter-repo (the file as FastModel.mo, each message ending with Imported-from: andoludo/trano@<sha>, pull requests referred to as andoludo/trano#<n>); the next commit splits it into the library.
  • FastSmoothBuildings/: the library in the directory layout, with a User's Guide, the documentation of every package, examples and validation models, and their reference results from OpenModelica 1.26.9 (Resources/ReferenceResults/OpenModelica).
  • src/fastsmoothbuildings: the Python package (LIBRARY, ROOT, bundle(), the version from the version annotation of the library); the wheel carries the library.
  • tests/: the layout, the bundle, rumoca and CasADi, OpenModelica (Docker).
  • .github/workflows: CI (lint, tests on Python 3.11 and 3.13, OpenModelica, build) and the release on a tag v<version> (PyPI trusted publishing, a GitHub release with the library as a zip).

docs.title: Found on the way
docs.text:
• rumoca reads every Modelica file below a root. Given the root of a checkout, it also found a copy of the library in .venv (hatchling's editable install copies the force-included folder) and refused the duplicates. Tools pass fastsmoothbuildings.LIBRARY, the folder of the library, as the root; ROOT is for MODELICAPATH.
  • rumoca 0.10.3 and dayTable. With a table of several rows, rumoca translates dayTable when the table is a parameter and, at the top level of the model, when the call is an equation; with a literal matrix in the call or in the binding of a declaration, it expands the loop of the function into extra equations ("unbalanced model") or leaves a residual equation. The library and the models trano generates use the working form (BESTEST 950 with its night ventilation and 940 with its set-back schedule translate); the User's Guide states the rule.
  • A mixing valve after the pump. With the pump upstream of the three-way valve (trano's circuits), a supply set point below the boiler temperature closes the supply path and dead-heads the pump; trano runs these circuits with the set point above the boiler (the valve open), and so does Examples.BoilerCircuit.
  • The CasADi models of the examples, integrated by CVODES, follow OpenModelica's DASSL results within 2 to 7 mK on the rooms, the boiler and the buffer; 0.09 K with the on/off thermostat of Examples.TwoZones, whose switching instants differ slightly between the solvers.

docs.title: BESTEST (ASHRAE Standard 140)
docs.text:
The BESTEST validation runs in trano, on the models trano generates from the YAML descriptions of the 27 cases of ASHRAE Standard 140 with every library it supports: see trano's BESTEST page for the cases, the acceptance bands and the other libraries. FastSmoothBuildings gates there as Buildings and IDEAS do: pytest -m bestest fails when one of its KPIs leaves its band or drifts from its frozen value. This page is the section of FastSmoothBuildings, as trano rendered it when the library moved to this repository; the analysis of these results, now and along the history of the library, is in the BESTEST report of the analysis.

The FastSmoothBuildings library gives trano a reduced model of the same building: the closed-loop model whose components rumoca translates to a CasADi ODE for optimal control and calibration. It runs the same YAML files in OpenModelica. Its walls are discretised as Buildings discretises them (number_of_states, at most three sublayers per layer), its zones take the air density of the site and exchange long-wave radiation as the YAML asks (linearised at 20 degC or around the current surface temperatures), its outer surfaces exchange with sky and ground exactly, the gas gaps of its glazings conduct at the temperatures of their panes (long-wave exchange and convection of the gas, as Buildings), its windows are shaded by overhangs and side fins as in Buildings, and its controllers are smooth and without events. It gates as Buildings and IDEAS do, on the 27 cases. The column Buildings gives the frozen value of Buildings for the same case (expected/Buildings.json), so that the gap between the two libraries reads next to the band. How the two libraries compare hour by hour, and how they respond to a change of the parameters, is studied in FastSmoothBuildings against Buildings on BESTEST and a house before and after renovation; how FastSmoothBuildings came to these results is told in the improvement plan.

105 of 105 KPIs of 27 cases are inside their band. Against Buildings, the loads differ by 1.1 % on average and 4.4 % at most, the temperatures of the free-floating zones by 0.38 K on average and 1.70 K at most.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings improvement plan
docs.text:
What to change in the FastSmoothBuildings library so that it stays within the bands of Buildings on the zone temperatures, the heating power and the heating demand and responds to a parameter change as Buildings does. The plan follows from the study of BESTEST 950FF, 940, 960 and the house before and after renovation and from a reading of the equations of the library (then trano/library/FastModel.mo) against the Buildings components they stand for. Each item names the gap, the evidence, the change, its cost in states or in smoothness (FastSmoothBuildings must stay an explicit, event-free ODE for rumoca and CasADi) and the validation that closes it.

The study ranks the gaps by what they change. When it started, in Denver, where the air is thin and the BESTEST walls are heavy, FastSmoothBuildings heated 7 to 16 % more than Buildings and responded 12 to 30 % more to the infiltration; in Uccle, with the renovated house, it stayed within 1 % of the meters and 5 % of the sensitivities, except where thermostatic valves share the flow of the circuit (set point response 0.80). Two defects were fixed during the study: the night ventilation that FastSmoothBuildings dropped and the 1 kW leak of its ideal systems. Three stages of changes followed (see Progress); the extended study (sweeps, glazing, sun, gains, sun-space, ventilation, radiators) then found the gaps of the last stage and the ones still open.

The study is the yardstick: each change is merged with its run of python -m study.buildings (the workflow study.yaml) and the BESTEST run of FastSmoothBuildings, and the tables of the study and of the BESTEST page are rendered from the new results.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
The first phases are in the library (then trano/library/FastModel.mo), its templates and library.json. Every step kept the models smooth and without events, and every FastSmoothBuildings model still exports to CasADi with rumoca (trano's tests/test_fast_model.py, now tests/test_rumoca.py here). Each step was measured on the BESTEST cases FastSmoothBuildings can describe (23 of 27 until the four with shading could run, all 27 since) against the band of the standard and against the values of Buildings for the same YAML:

Library Cases KPIs inside their band Annual heating against Buildings, mean (range) Annual cooling against Buildings, mean (range) Loads, mean gap Free-floating temperatures, mean gap (largest) Before (first FastSmoothBuildings run) 22 83 of 85 +9.0 % (+5.0 to +20.4 %) +3.1 % (+1.5 to +4.3 %) 5.6 % 0.48 K (1.49 K) Air density, exact smooth limits (phase 1) 22 85 of 85 −0.4 % (−3.6 to +2.6 %) +5.5 % (+3.0 to +9.2 %) 3.4 % 1.04 K (4.39 K) Discretised walls, single glazing (phase 2) 23 87 of 89 −0.6 % (−3.3 to +2.1 %) +5.5 % (+1.7 to +9.3 %) 3.1 % 1.16 K (4.57 K) Room long-wave exchange around the surface temperatures 23 89 of 89 −0.6 % (−3.2 to +1.6 %) +5.0 % (−0.1 to +8.1 %) 2.7 % 0.93 K (3.82 K) Exact long-wave exchange with sky and ground 23 89 of 89 +0.6 % (−1.0 to +2.5 %) +2.4 % (−2.2 to +6.6 %) 2.0 % 0.80 K (3.52 K) Gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes, small hydraulic links (phase 3) 23 89 of 89 +0.2 % (−0.9 to +2.5 %) +1.4 % (−2.3 to +4.4 %) 1.2 % 0.38 K (1.70 K) Overhangs and side fins (phase 4) 27 105 of 105 +0.2 % (−0.9 to +2.5 %) +1.3 % (−2.3 to +4.4 %) 1.1 % 0.38 K (1.70 K)

What each step did:

  • Air density at the site (phase 1). The weather bus carries the atmospheric pressure (101325 Pa, or the pressure of the site's altitude when the YAML reads it from the weather file), and the zone uses the ideal-gas density at that pressure and its air temperature. The heating of the Denver cases fell from +9 % to −0.4 % of Buildings. It also showed that the excess infiltration had hidden a heat surplus: with it gone, FastSmoothBuildings cooled 5 % more than Buildings and its free-floating peaks rose by up to 4 K above those of Buildings.
  • Smooth limits that reach their bounds (phase 1). smoothLimit is exactly its bound beyond a quadratic blend and never leaves the range; it used to saturate 0.1 % inside, which made the ideal systems leak 1 kW of heating and of cooling at all times. The solar angles keep the interior limit (smoothLimitInside), acos being singular at the bounds.
  • Discretised walls (phase 2). The closed-loop model splits each layer into the states Buildings gives it, at most three sublayers; FastSmoothBuildingsMPC keeps one node per layer boundary, its states being the decision variables of the optimal control. The reheat peak of 940 after the night set-back fell from +8 % to +2 % of Buildings. The single glazing of 670 runs at last: its record wrote an empty array, {}, that OpenModelica does not parse.
  • Long-wave exchange in the room around the mean surface temperature when the YAML sets linearize_emissive_power: false, as every BESTEST case does (Buildings then exchanges exactly). The cooling excess fell by about half a point and the free-floating peaks by up to 0.8 K.
  • Exact long-wave exchange with sky and ground for outer walls and windows, \(\sigma\varepsilon A (T^4 - T_{env}^4)\) instead of its linearisation at \(T_{env}\): a sun-lit outer surface loses a quarter more at 60 degC. The cooling excess fell from +5.0 to +2.4 % on average.
  • Gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes (phase 3). FastSmoothBuildings held each gap of a glazing at its EN 673 conductance, computed by trano's Python at 10 degC; Buildings recomputes the long-wave exchange across the gap (\(\sigma (T_a^4 - T_b^4)/(1/\varepsilon_a + 1/\varepsilon_b - 1)\), which grows as \(T^3\)) and the convection of the gas (Wright's correlations of the vertical cavity) at the temperatures of the panes. A sun-lit glazing at 40 degC conducts a fifth more than at 10 degC, so FastSmoothBuildings kept too much of the sun in the zones that nothing cools. Envelope.Functions.gapConductance now computes both in Modelica from the data of the YAML (the conductivity of the panes, the properties of the gas, the emissivities facing each gap), an explicit and smooth function of the pane temperatures; GGap stays a parameter (the conductance at the EN 673 state, scaled by the temperatures), so that mpctrano still calibrates it. The free-floating temperatures came within 0.38 K of Buildings on average (0.80 K before) and 1.70 K at the hottest hour (3.52 K); 680FF went from 1.17 to 0.53 K hourly RMSE.
  • Small hydraulic links (phase 3). The study blamed the flow law for the set point responses of the renovated house; trano's Buildings valves and radiators are linearised too (linearized=true), with the same conductances as FastSmoothBuildings. Measured branch by branch, the gap was elsewhere: with the living room valve fully open, FastSmoothBuildings passed 36.6 g/s against 43.9 g/s in Buildings, because the components that have no resistance in Buildings (the sensor feeding the six radiators, the water side of the heat pump) had a linear one of 1000 Pa at their nominal flow, a fifth of the head of a radiator branch. At 100 Pa, the living room warms by 0.75 K with a set point +1 K (Buildings 0.80 K, before 0.71 K) and the kitchen by 0.64 K (0.71, 0.60).
  • Layers split in Modelica (phase 3). The construction record carries the layers of the YAML and the number of sublayers of each (the states Buildings gives it, at most 3; one for FastSmoothBuildingsMPC); PartialOpaque splits them. The counts stay literal in the record: rumoca 0.10.3 sizes arrays only from literal parameters (not from a sum, nor from a default of the record). Same results within 3e-5. The walls name T the temperatures of the layer boundaries, the states of both FastSmoothBuildings and FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, and TSub the nodes inside the layers (FastSmoothBuildings only): a state of one model copied into the other by its name stays at its place. Before, T[2] of the MPC model was a layer boundary and T[2] of the closed-loop model a node inside the first layer; mpctrano's spin-up, which copies the states by name, started the MPC model with the inner surfaces of its walls inside the insulation.
  • The house before renovation (study, fourth run, no change of the library). The gas boiler at 75 degC, its three-way valve and six radiators with thermostatic valves follow Buildings in closed loop: rooms within 0.02 to 0.09 K hour by hour, heating +1.7 %, gas +1.9 %, and the six changes that move the results (cavity insulation, airtightness, supply temperature, radiator size, set point) alike, gas included. It exports to CasADi (160 states as FastSmoothBuildingsMPC, 224 in closed loop) and IPOPT solves its optimal control with the boiler and the valves as controls. The study now reads the gas and the electricity of both libraries from the energy meters: samples of the powers five minutes apart put the gas 0.6 to 0.75 % off when the boiler fires at full power for two minutes as the valves open; per unit of heat FastSmoothBuildings burns the same gas as Buildings within 0.2 %.
  • Overhangs and side fins (phase 4). The window takes the geometry of the YAML (overhang, side_fins) and shades its direct irradiance by the sunlit fraction of Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.Overhang and SideFins, ported to Envelope.Functions.overhangSunlitFraction and sideFinsSunlitFraction: the same areas of the shadow in the plane of the window, with smoothMax/smoothMin in place of max/min, the tangents written as a sine over a cosine kept away from zero, and regStep blends where Buildings switches (the sun behind the wall, below the horizon). With both, the fractions combine as in Buildings (\(f_{ove} + f_{fin} - 1\), kept above 0.001). The diffuse irradiance is not shaded, as in Buildings. A unit test checks the fractions against their closed form at a few sun positions. The four shading cases run and pass every KPI, within 2.2 % of Buildings (910 peak cooling), and FastSmoothBuildings gates in BESTEST as Buildings and IDEAS do. A window without shading keeps its fraction at 1 through an evaluated parameter: the six-zone house still exports with rumoca (189 states, 28 inputs for FastSmoothBuildingsMPC) and IPOPT solves its 12-hour optimal control in about a minute.

Still open. The free-floating zones of the light, well-insulated constructions still peak 1 to 1.7 K above Buildings (600FF, 650FF, 680FF) and the 960 sun-space is 0.4 K warm on average. FastSmoothBuildings responds 8 % less than Buildings to the solar absorptance of the outer surfaces (priority 8). In the renovated house, the supply water is 0.4 K cooler when the heat pump runs at full load, and the responses to the set point (heating 0.87, electricity 0.85), to the buffer and to the peaks go through the heat pump (priority 9). Unbalanced ventilation, wind- and stack-driven infiltration and the ISO 13370 ground are not modelled (priority 6). The proposals give a formulation of each that keeps the model explicit and smooth.

docs.title: Gaps found by reading the equations
docs.text: These differences exist whatever the case; the study measures how much each of them weighs.

docs.title: 1. One node per layer boundary in the opaque constructions
docs.text:
Envelope.PartialOpaque puts one capacity at each boundary between the layers of a construction (\(n\) layers, \(n + 1\) nodes), half of each adjacent layer lumped into the node. Buildings discretises each layer into nSta states; the BESTEST cases ask for 18 states per 0.2 m of layer (number_of_states in the YAML, ignored by FastSmoothBuildings). A 0.1 m concrete block is one lumped capacity in FastSmoothBuildings and about nine in Buildings. The conductance of a layer and its total capacity are the same, so the steady-state heat loss is identical and a conductivity change moves the demand alike; what differs is the dynamics: the lumped wall responds faster to a step of the room or outdoor temperature and stores the diurnal solar gain differently. That weighs on the free-floating extremes, on the morning reheat peak after a set-back and on the response to a change of the thermal mass.

Change: discretise each layer into nSta nodes as Buildings does, with nSta read from number_of_states (default 1 to keep today's models) and a cap for the MPC export; or, cheaper, two nodes per layer thicker than a threshold. Cost: states (a heavy BESTEST wall goes from 4 to about 12 nodes), none in smoothness.

docs.title: 2. Air density and the site pressure
docs.text:
The zone uses \(\rho = 1.2\) kg/m3 for the infiltration (rhoAir*V*ACH/3600). Trano's Buildings zone takes the density of the air at the atmospheric pressure of the weather file when the YAML asks for it (atmospheric_pressure_source: File, as the BESTEST cases do): in Denver, 1609 m above sea level, that is about 0.98 kg/m3. The infiltration heat flow of FastSmoothBuildings is then about 20 % larger than that of Buildings for the same air change rate, and so is its response to a change of the air change rate. The scheduled night ventilation is a mass flow in both libraries and is not affected.

Change: rhoAir from the pressure of the weather bus (pAtm, ideal gas at the zone temperature or at 20 degC), one algebraic expression. Cost: none.

docs.title: 3. Long-wave exchange linearised at 20 degC
docs.text: The radiant star of the zone uses \(G_i = 4\sigma T_0^3 \varepsilon_i A_i\) at \(T_0 = 20\) degC; the BESTEST cases ask Buildings for the non-linear exchange (linearize_emissive_power: false). The error grows with the spread of the surface temperatures: a sun-lit floor at 35 degC and a window at 5 degC in winter, the free-floating zone at 60 degC in summer. Change: linearise around the current mean surface temperature (\(T_0 = T_{rad}\) of the previous step is not available in an ODE; \(T_0^3\) as a smooth function of the mean surface temperature is), or keep the exact \(\sigma \varepsilon (T_i^4 - T_{rad}^4)\) with the star temperature solved implicitly. Cost: the exact form adds an algebraic loop; the moving linearisation adds none.

docs.title: 4. Controllers without events and without safety times
docs.text: A hysteresis switches over tau (10 s by default, a parameter since this branch) instead of at an instant, and the heat pump has no minimum on and off times. The heat pump starts and stops at other instants than in Buildings, which shows in the water temperatures and the hour-by-hour heat of the radiators (see the replay validation), less in the zones and the meters. Change: a smooth minimum on/off time (a first-order timer gating the compressor), and smooth_controllers widths chosen per use (simulation: narrow; calibration: the x5, 600 s of mpctrano). Cost: one state per heat pump.

docs.title: 5. Hydraulics linearised, one production per circuit, mixing valves only
docs.text: Pressure-driven flows with resistances linearised at their nominal flows, as trano's Buildings models are (linearized=true on the valves and radiators: the same conductances), and a small resistance for the components that have none in Buildings, each inlet a pressure node of small compliance so that the flows stay explicit. That small resistance was 1000 Pa at the nominal flow, a fifth of the head of a radiator branch behind a six-way manifold; it is 100 Pa since phase 3 (2 % of the branch). A pressure node keeps its last value when its pump stops (the head of a stopped pump reads 20 kPa instead of 0), which changes nothing but the reported head.

docs.title: 6. Heat pump performance map
docs.text: The Vitocal 251-A08 table of Buildings is scaled to the capacity of the YAML, interpolated and smoothed in the source temperature, quadratic in the condenser temperature; the condenser outlet is approximated from the buffer temperature. Change: fit the condenser side on the EN 14511 table too (bilinear smooth interpolation), keep the scaling. Cost: none in states.

docs.title: 7. Balanced ventilation and fans at constant pressure
docs.text: The unit is balanced (supply = extract) while in Buildings part of the supply leaves by the infiltration paths, so that the recovery works on a smaller extract stream; the fans run at constant pressure rise. Change: an extract flow equal to the supply minus the infiltration pushed out, as the pressures of Buildings set it. Cost: none.

docs.title: 8. Missing features
docs.text: Storage tanks on boilers, water-to-water heat pumps, chillers, domestic hot water, batteries, EV chargers, VAV, air handling units other than system D, power sensors, moisture, wind- and stack-driven infiltration, the ISO 13370 ground of IDEAS. The night ventilation schedule and the overhangs and side fins (BESTEST 610, 630, 910, 930) were missing and are added by this branch.

docs.title: Proposals for the remaining gaps
docs.text:
What rumoca and CasADi need of FastSmoothBuildings, learnt on the way: an explicit ODE (every algebraic variable a function of the states, the inputs and the parameters: no algebraic loop, a pressure node of small compliance where Buildings solves the flows of a circuit), once continuously differentiable equations without events (regStep, smoothMax, \(\sqrt{x^2 + \delta^2}\) for \(|x|\), no when, pre or sample), and, for rumoca 0.10.3, array sizes and subscripts given by literal parameters: not a sum, not the result of a function, not a default of a record (the sublayers of a construction are written out by trano for that reason), and no loop in a function over a parameter that stays tunable. Each proposal below keeps to that; its cost is in states and in parameters, its gate in the study or in BESTEST.

Gap Proposal Cost Gate Response to the outer solar absorptance (0.91) Find where the heat goes: compare the outer surface temperatures and the conduction into the room of a sun-lit wall in both libraries (the irradiance, the outside convection with its wind modifier, the sky exchange and the sublayers, up to 9, are ruled out); the room-side long-wave exchange of the opaque surfaces (radiant star against Buildings' radiosity) is the next suspect none until the cause is known absorptance ratios 0.95 to 1.05 Supply water at full load The condenser outlet and the capacity from the EN 14511 table of the heat pump, interpolated as the other optics and curves of FastSmoothBuildings are (a polynomial fit evaluated in Modelica, smooth in the source and condenser temperatures) instead of the buffer temperature parameters only supply within 0.2 K of Buildings at full load, set point responses within 5 % Heat pump safety times A first-order lag on the compressor command, \(\tau \dot y = y_{on} - y\), with \(\tau\) a third of the minimum run time of the YAML: the compressor follows its hysteresis but cannot start and stop faster than the safety times allow, on average, without an event (Buildings holds each start and stop exactly, with events) one state per heat pump buffer and supply peak ratios 0.8 to 1.2 Unbalanced ventilation The extract of a ventilation unit equal to its supply minus the air the infiltration paths push out, as the pressures of Buildings share it: an explicit expression of the flows none supply air within 0.1 K Wind- and stack-driven infiltration \(\dot m = \rho A_L \sqrt{C_s \sqrt{\Delta T^2 + \delta^2} + C_w v^2}\) (LBL), explicit in the weather and the zone temperature parameters only infiltration responses within 10 % against IDEAS Ground (ISO 13370) A virtual layer of soil with its periodic temperature, as IDEAS: two states per floor on the ground two states per floor ground losses within 10 % of IDEAS

docs.title: Phase 1: the steady state (days)
docs.text:
1. Air density at the site. PartialZone takes the atmospheric pressure of the weather bus (pAtm, already in the weather data of trano) and computes \(\rho = p_{atm} / (R_{air} T_{air})\) for the infiltration and the scheduled ventilation of the zone, as Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed.MixedAir does through its medium (an ideal gas at the pressure of the site); the heat capacity of the air volume takes the same density. For the MPC export the pressure is a disturbance already, so the ODE stays explicit. Gate: 940 heating within 5 % of Buildings (today +15.6 %), 940 infiltration ratio 0.9 to 1.1 (today 1.30), the renovated house unchanged within 0.5 %.
  2. Smooth limits that reach their bounds. Replace smoothLimit(x, l, u, dX) (saturating at \(l + dX\) and \(u - dX\)) by a limit whose smooth transitions lie inside \([l, u]\) and end exactly on the bounds (the regStep blends of smoothMax and smoothMin shifted inwards by \(dX\), clipped so that they cannot overshoot), in every controller and actuator, and drop the per-component rescaling added during the study. Gate: a unit test on the controllers (saturated output exactly 0 and 1, no output outside \([0, 1]\)), the ideal-system test of the rumoca tests, BESTEST cooling and heating of FastSmoothBuildings within their bands.

docs.title: Phase 2: the dynamics (weeks)
docs.text:
1. Layers discretised as Buildings does. PartialOpaque gets nSta[nLay] (from number_of_states of the YAML, which trano already renders for Buildings, scaled to the layer thickness as nStaRef does), each layer split into nSta conductances and capacities. The default keeps today's model (one node per boundary) for MPC, where the state count matters; the closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings takes the YAML. A middle option is a minimum of two nodes for a layer whose time constant exceeds a few hours. Gate: 940 peak heating within 5 % (today +12 %), night heating within 20 kWh, 950FF mass ratios 0.9 to 1.1 (today 1.13 to 1.45), sun-space bias within 0.2 K (today +0.53 K), the MPC export of the renovated house below 1.5 times its states.
  2. Long-wave exchange around the current temperatures. Linearise each radiant conductance at the mean of the surface temperatures of the zone (\(G_i = 4\sigma\varepsilon_i A_i \bar T^3\), \(\bar T\) a smooth function of the states) instead of 20 degC, or keep the exact \(\sigma\varepsilon(T_i^4 - T_{rad}^4)\) with the star solved implicitly in the closed-loop model only. Gate: sun-space RMSE below 0.5 K (today 0.87 K), 960 and 600FF/900FF extremes within 0.5 K of Buildings.

docs.title: Phase 3: the systems (weeks)
docs.text:
1. Flow sharing between radiator branches. Done differently: the flow laws are the same as trano's Buildings models (linearised); the resistances of the links that Buildings does not have are ten times smaller (phase 3). Gate kept: the set point and radiator responses of the renovated house within 10 %.
  2. Heat pump safety times and condenser. Minimum on and off times as a smooth timer state gating the compressor, and the condenser outlet from the EN 14511 table rather than the buffer temperature. Gate: the water temperatures of the replay validation within 1 K (today about 2 K in closed loop), buffer and supply peak ratios 0.8 to 1.2.

docs.title: Phase 4: coverage
docs.text:
1. Overhangs and side fins (Buildings.HeatTransfer.Windows.Overhang and SideFins geometry, a smooth shaded fraction of the direct irradiance), so that BESTEST 610, 630, 910 and 930 run with FastSmoothBuildings. Done: the four cases inside their bands, within 2.2 % of Buildings.
  2. Unbalanced ventilation (extract = supply minus the air pushed out by the infiltration paths), wind- and stack-driven infiltration, the ISO 13370 ground of IDEAS for the comparisons with IDEAS.

docs.title: Gates kept after the plan
docs.text:
• The study runs on every change of the library (then trano/library/FastModel.mo) or of the FastSmoothBuildings templates (the workflow does so when the commit carries [study]); a test reads its committed results and fails when a zone RMSE exceeds 0.5 K (1 K for a free-floating BESTEST zone), a heating demand deviates by more than 10 %, or a sensitivity ratio leaves 0.8 to 1.25, with the deviations understood listed as BESTEST does.
  • FastSmoothBuildings gates in the BESTEST validation as Buildings and IDEAS do (pytest -m bestest, the workflow bestest.yaml): its 27 cases inside their bands, the direction of every change between two cases as the reference programs, and frozen values (expected/FastSmoothBuildings.json) that catch the drifts inside the bands.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings against Buildings and IDEAS
docs.text:
The models of the FastSmoothBuildings library translate into a CasADi ODE: FastSmoothBuildings simulates the building in closed loop with its own controllers, FastSmoothBuildingsMPC takes the controls as inputs for optimal control. How close they stay to the Buildings and IDEAS models of the same YAML file is measured by study/replay, in two ways:

  • --models FastSmoothBuildings replays the controls of the reference through the runnable FastSmoothBuildingsMPC model: the envelope, the zones and the systems are compared with the controls taken out of the comparison;
  • --models FastSmoothBuildingsClosedLoop simulates the closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings model with its own controllers, as the reference runs with its own: nothing is replayed.
python -m study.replay compare 600FF residential_before --models FastSmoothBuildings FastSmoothBuildingsClosedLoop
python -m study.replay compare residential_after --models FastSmoothBuildings FastSmoothBuildingsClosedLoop --references Buildings IDEAS
python -m study.replay report

For each case the Buildings model (or the IDEAS model, --references IDEAS) is simulated with its own controls, then the runnable model of the other library replays what its systems did:

  • the heat of the ideal emitters of each zone, for the envelope cases;
  • the flow of each radiator branch, the position of each three-way valve and the part load ratio of the boiler (or the speed of the heat pump compressor), for the hydronic cases, and the air flow of the ventilation unit. Everything else is simulated by the FastSmoothBuildings model: the production, the water circuits, the radiators, the ventilation, the PV array and the zones.

Weather, solar irradiance (direct, Perez diffuse) and occupancy come from the same Buildings blocks in both models. The zone air temperatures are compared every 15 minutes; the radiator heat hour by hour (ASHRAE Guideline 14 CV(RMSE) and NMBE); the water temperatures of the circuits every 15 minutes. The thermostatic valves of the hydronic cases modulate the flows faster than that, so their Buildings reference is recorded every minute and the controls are replayed as means over 5 minutes, which conserves the heat the water carries.

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
Envelope. The FastSmoothBuildings zone follows Buildings within 0.33–0.39 K (RMSE) in the free-floating BESTEST cases. In the heated and cooled BESTEST cases the replay of the Buildings heat is open loop, so that any difference accumulates until the envelope removes it; the FastSmoothBuildings zone stays within 0.41–0.65 K.

Multi-zone envelope. With walls and floors shared between zones, the three-zone house stays within 0.18–0.49 K of Buildings.

Hydronics. In the three hydronic houses (the residential house before renovation with its gas boiler, after renovation with its heat pump, ventilation and PV, and the heat pump test house), only the branch flows, the three-way valve positions and the boiler part load ratio or the heat pump compressor speed are replayed; the production, the water circuits, the radiators and the zones are simulated by the FastSmoothBuildings model. The radiators deliver the heat of Buildings within 0.7–4.3 % CV(RMSE) and a bias below 1 % (the 28 % of the nearly unheated bedroom 3 of the heat pump house is on 4 kWh in four weeks); the zones follow within 0.12–0.33 K; the boiler supply and the heat pump buffer within 0.55–0.75 K. The supply errors were 0.3–0.5 K before the Buildings models took trano's default performance options, with the same zone temperatures and meters: most likely the Buildings sensors, now without dynamics, follow every start and stop of the production that the 5-minute replay smooths. The meters of the renovated house follow Buildings over the four weeks: heat pump electricity −1.8 % (−1.6 % in the heat pump test house), fans −0.6 %, PV production 0.0 %.

IDEAS. The renovated house is also replayed from its IDEAS simulation: FastSmoothBuildings stays within 0.31–0.39 K of the IDEAS zones, 0.14–0.25 K too warm on average, the radiators within 1.6–4.1 % CV(RMSE), the heat pump electricity within −1.0 % and the fans within −2.1 %. The envelope of FastSmoothBuildings is that of Buildings: the bias comes from the envelope models of the two libraries, above all the ground below the slab (ISO 13370 in IDEAS, a fixed temperature in Buildings and FastSmoothBuildings). See the FastSmoothBuildings reference for the figures.

Ventilation. The supply air of the renovated house's unit stays within 0.30 K of Buildings, 0.29 K too warm on average: in Buildings the extract flow is 3 % below the supply flow (part of the supply leaves through the infiltration paths of the zones, as the pressures set it), so that the heat exchanger recovers on a smaller stream; the FastSmoothBuildings unit is balanced. The return temperatures (1.35–1.75 K, small bias) mix the outlets of radiators whose flows the thermostatic valves modulate within the replay interval.

Closed loop. With its own controllers, FastSmoothBuildings follows the zones of Buildings within 0.05–0.25 K, closer than the replay: a controller corrects the small differences of the envelope as the Buildings controller does, where the replayed heat is open loop (BESTEST 600 and 900: 0.06 and 0.14 K against 0.65 and 0.41 K). The free-floating cases have no controller and match the replay. Against IDEAS, the renovated house stays within 0.14–0.23 K. The meters follow within a few percent: boiler fuel +1.2 %, heat pump electricity −1.1 to −3.1 % (−4.1 % against IDEAS), fans −2.1 %, PV 0.0 %. The boiler supply follows within 0.11 K. The heat pump circuits differ most: the supply and return water within about 2 K and the radiator heat within 6–16 % CV(RMSE) hour by hour (the bedrooms that barely need heat aside), because the heat pump of FastSmoothBuildings has no minimum on and off times and its hysteresis switches within 10 s, so that it starts and stops at other instants than in Buildings.

docs.title: Differences that remain
docs.text:
• In the replay, each Valve of FastSmoothBuildingsMPC sets the flow of its branch, y·m_flow_nominal, as an MPC decides it; in Buildings the flow that a valve opening gives depends on the pressures of the whole circuit. The closed-loop FastSmoothBuildings computes them, with the resistances linearised at their nominal flows.
  • The closed-loop controllers have no event: a hysteresis switches within 10 s, and the heat pump has no minimum on and off times (see above).
  • The heat pump interpolates the EN 14511 tables in the source temperature as Buildings does, smoothed at the knots, and is quadratic in the condenser temperature (within 1 % of the tables up to 55 °C); its condenser outlet is approximated explicitly from the buffer temperature.
  • Ventilation units are balanced (see above).

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings against Buildings: BESTEST and a house before and after renovation
docs.text: This page compares the FastSmoothBuildings library with Buildings on the three signals a heating study or a calibration rests on: the zone air temperatures, the heating power hour by hour and the heating demand over the period, and asks a second question that the replay validation does not: when a parameter of the YAML changes, does FastSmoothBuildings move the way Buildings moves? A reduced model is fit for design studies and for calibration only if the derivative of its results with respect to the parameters is right, not only its results at one point. The improvement plan draws the consequences.

docs.title: What is compared and how
docs.text:
Both libraries are generated by trano from the same YAML file and simulated by OpenModelica in the same container (FastSmoothBuildings is a Modelica library; its CasADi export plays no part here). The FastSmoothBuildings model runs in closed loop with its own controllers, as the Buildings model runs with its own: nothing is replayed, the two models are two simulations of the same building description. The hourly means of the zone air temperatures, of the heat delivered to each zone by its emitters (ideal system or radiators), of the gas of the boiler, of the electricity of the heat pump and the fans and of the PV production (from their energy meters, exact whatever the output interval) are extracted from both result files by study/buildings and committed with their KPIs; the tables and figures below are rendered from those files.

The cases, chosen among the complex ones:

Case What it is Why it is here BESTEST 950FF the heavy zone of ASHRAE 140 (concrete block walls, concrete slab), free floating, with a night ventilation fan of 1700 m3/h from 18:00 to 07:00 the free-floating case with the most physics: thermal mass, solar gains through 12 m2 of south glazing, a scheduled air flow that no controller corrects BESTEST 940 the heavy zone with ideal heating to 20 degC by day and 10 degC at night (ramp from 07:00 to 08:00) and cooling at 27 degC the most complete BESTEST system with heating: a set-back schedule makes the morning reheat peak depend on the mass and the control BESTEST 960 the light zone heated and cooled behind an unconditioned heavy sun-space, coupled by a common wall two zones, an internal wall, a passive zone driven by the sun Residential, after renovation examples/residential_after_renovation.yaml: six zones, air-to-water heat pump with a 100 l buffer, radiators with thermostatic valves, balanced ventilation with heat recovery, PV, Uccle every system FastSmoothBuildings models, in closed loop, over 28 days of January Residential, before renovation examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml: the same house with uninsulated cavity walls and attic, old double glazing, infiltration n50 = 12 1/h, a non-condensing gas boiler at 75 degC, a three-way valve and radiators with thermostatic valves, Uccle a boiler house: a hydronic circuit at high temperature and a gas meter, in closed loop over 28 days of January

For each case the perturbations change one field of the YAML and are simulated with both libraries; the table "Response to the perturbations" of each case gives, for each KPI, the change seen by Buildings, the change seen by FastSmoothBuildings and their ratio (1.0 would be a perfect agreement on the sensitivity, whatever the offset between the two libraries). Two parameters of 940 and one of each house are swept: scaled by several factors, so that the study shows whether FastSmoothBuildings follows Buildings over a range of values and bends as it does, not only for one step.

Case Envelope Use and systems 950FF insulation conductivity x1.5, infiltration x2, wall mass x0.5, solar transmittance of the glazing x0.75, solar absorptance of the outer surfaces 0.9 instead of 0.6 internal gains x2 940 insulation conductivity x0.5, x0.75, x1.5, x2 and infiltration x0.5, x1.5, x2, x3 (sweeps), wall mass x0.5, gas of the glazing gap x0.5 (U-value of the glazing 2.9 to 2.6 W/(m2.K)), solar transmittance x0.75, solar absorptance 0.9 internal gains x2, heating set points +2 K 960 solar transmittance of the sun-space glazing x0.75, conductivity of the common wall x2, mass of the sun-space walls x0.5, infiltration of the sun-space x2 residential_after EPS conductivity x0.5, x1.5, x2 (sweep), n50 x2 heat pump 2 kW instead of 3 kW, supply set point +10 K, radiators x0.7, buffer tank x3, heat recovery 0.5 instead of 0.8, living room and kitchen set point +1 K, flow of the ventilation x1.5, radiator exponent 1.33 instead of 1.24 residential_before cavity of the walls filled with insulation (U 1.47 to 0.52 W/(m2.K)), n50 x0.5, x1.5 (sweep), air of the glazing gaps x0.5 boiler 10 kW instead of 16 kW, supply set point −10 K, radiators x0.7, living room and kitchen set point +1 K, radiator exponent 1.33 instead of 1.24

The KPIs: mean, lowest and highest hourly zone temperature; heating and cooling demand (the heat delivered to the zones); peak heating (largest hourly mean); the heat pump electricity, the gas of the boiler and the OpenModelica time. Hour by hour, the FastSmoothBuildings temperatures are compared with the Buildings ones by their RMSE, bias and largest error, and the heating power by the CV(RMSE) and NMBE of ASHRAE Guideline 14.

The night ventilation of 950FF is modelled by ventilationSchedule in trano's Buildings zone; the FastSmoothBuildings zone did not take that parameter until this study (it silently dropped the fan), it does now.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The study was run three times. The first run (the library as it was when the study started) found FastSmoothBuildings close to Buildings on the zone temperatures, but 11 to 16 % high on the heating of the Denver cases and quicker than Buildings in its heavy walls, and it found four defects (below). The library was changed as the improvement plan says (air density at the site, smooth limits that reach their bounds, walls discretised as Buildings, long-wave exchange as the YAML asks, exact exchange with the sky) before the second run. The second run, with the perturbations extended to the glazing, the sun, the gains, the sun-space, the ventilation and the radiators and with the sweeps, found two more gaps that the library then closed: the gas gaps of the glazing held at their EN 673 conductance, and resistances in the hydraulic links that Buildings does not have. The tables below are those of the third run, on the library as it is now. The house before renovation joined in a fourth run on the same library, which also reads the gas and the electricity of both libraries from the energy meters of the systems instead of samples of their powers: samples five minutes apart caught or missed the two-minute bursts of the boiler at full power when the valves open (0.75 % of the gas of Buildings, 0.6 % of FastSmoothBuildings's, in opposite directions), and moved the electricity of the heat pump of the renovated house by 2 % and its responses by up to 0.15.

FastSmoothBuildings follows Buildings within 0.05 to 0.08 K hour by hour on the zones of the BESTEST cases (0.46 K in the unheated sun-space of 960), within 0.06 to 0.10 K on the rooms of the renovated house and within 0.02 to 0.09 K on those of the house before renovation; its heating demand is within 1.7 % of Buildings in every base case, and it responds to every change of the envelope, the sun, the gains and the ideal systems of the BESTEST cases as Buildings does: 24 perturbations out of 24 alike (every ratio within 0.9 to 1.1, or the two changes within 0.05 K or 0.5 %). In the renovated house, 10 of 12 are alike or close; the two that differ are peaks of the heat pump (the buffer x3 and the EPS x0.5). In the house before renovation with its gas boiler, the six changes that move the results are alike, the gas included (ratios 0.99 to 1.01); see below.

Case Zone temperature, hourly RMSE Heating demand, Buildings / FastSmoothBuildings Peak heating OpenModelica time 950FF, free floating, night ventilation 0.08 K (second run 0.10 K, first 0.29 K) (free floating) 80 / 34 s 940, set-back heating and cooling 0.05 K (0.08 K, 0.13 K) 1100 / 1096 kWh, −0.4 % (+0.3 %, +11 %) 3.27 / 3.30 kW, +1 % (+2 %, +8 %) 110 / 37 s 960, zone behind a sun-space 0.07 K zone, 0.46 K sun-space (0.10 and 0.68 K; 0.11 and 0.87 K) 2588 / 2575 kWh, −0.5 % (−1.0 %) 2.10 / 2.11 kW 149 / 42 s Renovated house, 28 days 0.06 to 0.10 K per room (0.06 to 0.12 K) 461 / 468 kWh, +1.5 % (+1.1 %); electricity 131 / 131 kWh, −0.2 % 2.02 / 2.05 kW 759 / 155 s House before renovation, gas boiler, 28 days 0.02 to 0.09 K per room 2755 / 2802 kWh, +1.7 %; gas 3391 / 3454 kWh, +1.9 % 8.70 / 8.78 kW 268 / 112 s

(The heating of the first run is that of the meters of the ideal system, as here: +11 % in 940. The first version of this page gave +15.6 %, read from hourly samples of the heat flow, which overstated both libraries.)

The first run found four defects, fixed before the second:

  • The night ventilation was dropped. The ventilation_schedule of a zone (BESTEST 650, 950 and their free-floating variants) never reached the FastSmoothBuildings zone, so these cases ran without their fan. The zone takes it now, as a day table added to the infiltration.
  • The ideal heating and cooling leaked. Both PI controllers of IdealHeatingCoolingPI saturated at 0.1 % of their output, which is 1 kW of heating and 1 kW of cooling around the clock with the 1 MW systems of BESTEST: the net load was right, but the heating and cooling demands were 8 and 4 times too large. smoothLimit now reaches its bounds exactly.
  • A single glazing did not translate. Its record wrote an empty array, RGap={}, that OpenModelica does not parse, and the window equations indexed a gap that a single pane does not have: BESTEST 670 never ran with FastSmoothBuildings. Both are fixed.
  • The flat Buildings model is under-determined (an electrical load of the data bus without its equation); the study renders Buildings with its containers, as the BESTEST validation does.

docs.title: Does a change of the YAML move both libraries alike?
docs.text:
A reduced model is physically sound for design and calibration when a change of a parameter of the building moves its results as it moves the results of the detailed model. The table Responses at a glance at the top of the results gives, for each of the 45 perturbations, the ratio of the changes on each main KPI and a verdict; the sections of the cases give the changes themselves and the sweeps. By family (ratios of the third run, second run in parentheses where the library changed them):

  • Conduction through the envelope. The conductivity of the insulation moves the heating of 940 by the same amount in both libraries over the whole sweep, from x0.5 to x2 (ratios 1.00 to 1.01, constant: FastSmoothBuildings bends as Buildings does), the cooling by 7 to 8 % more (9 to 11 %); the conductivity of the EPS of the house moves its heating by 0.98 to 1.00 from x0.5 to x2, and filling the cavity of the walls of the house before renovation cuts its heating and its gas by 23 % in both (1.01). The steady-state resistances are the same in both libraries; what differs a little is the share of the sun the envelope returns to the room in summer.
  • Air. The infiltration of 940 from x0.5 to x3: heating 0.99 to 1.00, cooling 1.00 to 1.01; n50 x2, heat recovery 0.5 and the ventilation flow x1.5 of the renovated house: heating 0.97 to 0.99; n50 x0.5 and x1.5 of the house before renovation: heating 1.00, gas 0.99 to 1.01. The air density at the site (first stage of the plan) made these agree; it was 1.30 in Denver at the start.
  • Thermal mass. Half the mass of the walls: 0.96 to 1.09 (1.45 at the start, before the walls were discretised as Buildings).
  • Glazing. The solar transmittance x0.75: 0.97 to 1.02 on the loads, 1.04 to 1.08 on the highest temperatures; the gas of the gap x0.5 (the U-value of the glazing): 1.02 to 1.07 (second run 1.03 to 1.21), since the gaps conduct at the temperatures of their panes.
  • Gains. Internal gains x2: 0.99 to 1.01.
  • Sun on the opaque surfaces. The solar absorptance of the outer surfaces 0.6 to 0.9: 0.91 to 0.93 on every KPI of 950FF and 940. FastSmoothBuildings takes 8 % less of the extra sun into the room. The irradiance, the outside convection with its wind modifier, the long-wave exchange with sky and ground and the discretisation of the walls (tried up to nine sublayers) are those of Buildings; the cause is still to be found (plan, priority 8). It is the one envelope parameter FastSmoothBuildings underestimates; its ratios stay within 0.9 to 1.1, the verdict alike.
  • Coupling of two zones (960). The common wall x2, the sun-space mass x0.5 and its infiltration x2: 0.94 to 1.10 (the common wall 0.97 to 1.15 in the second run).
  • Ideal systems. The heating set points of 940 +2 K: 0.99 to 1.00.
  • Heat pump house (after renovation). The supply set point +10 K (peak and electricity 1.01 and 1.04; second run 1.30 and 1.08), the radiator exponent (peak 0.93; second run 0.62) and the heat recovery are alike. The set point +1 K of the living room and kitchen (heating 0.87, electricity 0.85; second run 0.79 and 0.80) and smaller radiators (heating 1.28 and electricity 1.30, on changes of 3 %: both libraries end within 1 % of each other) are close. Two differ, both on the peak of the heat pump: a buffer three times larger (FastSmoothBuildings's peak falls by 5 %, Buildings' by 1 %) and the EPS x0.5 (peak 1.51). The heat pump of FastSmoothBuildings has no safety times and takes its condenser from the buffer temperature: it starts and stops at other instants, and at full load its supply water is 0.4 K cooler than in Buildings.
  • Boiler house (before renovation). The supply set point −10 K and radiators x0.7 lower the peak by 12 % in both libraries (1.06); the set point +1 K of the living room and kitchen raises the heating and the gas by about 5 % in both (0.99 and 0.99). A 10 kW boiler instead of 16 kW changes nothing in either, the peak of the house (8.7 kW) staying below it, nor do the radiator exponent and the glazing gap beyond 2 %. The gas follows the heat: 1.9 % above Buildings in the base case, for 1.7 % more heat delivered to the rooms; per unit of heat both burn the same gas within 0.2 %, and both water loops close their energy balance within 0.15 % over the month.

What had to be added to FastSmoothBuildings to get there, in the order of the plan: the air density of the site, smooth limits that reach their bounds, the walls discretised as Buildings, the long-wave exchange as the YAML asks (in the room, with the sky), the gas gaps at the temperatures of their panes, hydraulic links without the resistances Buildings does not have, and the overhangs and side fins of Buildings (the four shading cases of BESTEST now run and pass). What it still needs is in the improvement plan: the heat pump at full load and its safety times and the response to the sun on the opaque surfaces.

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
Free-floating zone (950FF). With its night fan, the heavy zone follows Buildings within 0.08 K hour by hour over a year from −12 to 37 degC (0.29 K in the first run); the mean, lowest and highest temperatures agree within 0.15 K. It responds to the insulation, the infiltration, the mass, the glazing and the gains as Buildings does (ratios 0.90 to 1.15 on temperature changes of a few tenths of a kelvin), and 9 % less to the solar absorptance of its walls. In the first run, doubling the infiltration cooled FastSmoothBuildings 12 % more than Buildings (the air density) and halving the mass raised its peak 13 % more (the lumped walls).

Set-back heating (940). The temperature follows within 0.05 K, the heating demand within 0.4 %, the morning peak within 1 %, the hourly heat within 4.6 % CV(RMSE). In the first run, FastSmoothBuildings heated 11 % more, its peak was 8 % higher and its hourly heat scattered by 58 % CV(RMSE), for two reasons the study separated:

Heating over the year, by period, first run Buildings FastSmoothBuildings Night set-back, 23:00 to 07:00 3 kWh 53 kWh Reheat, 07:00 to 09:00 376 kWh 433 kWh Day, 09:00 to 23:00 819 kWh 899 kWh

the lumped heavy walls cooled the room faster at night and warmed it slower on sunny mornings, and the infiltration carried a fifth too much heat: FastSmoothBuildings took 1.2 kg/m3 where the air of Denver, at 83 kPa, weighs 0.99 kg/m3 (doubling the infiltration then added 30 % more heating in FastSmoothBuildings than in Buildings; now 0 %). The sweeps show that the agreement is not a coincidence of one step: from half to twice the insulation and from half to three times the infiltration, the heating of FastSmoothBuildings moves by the change of Buildings within 1 %.

Sun-space (960). The heated zone follows within 0.07 K, its heating within 0.5 % and its cooling within 2.3 %. The unheated heavy sun-space is the weakest temperature: 0.46 K RMSE (0.68 K in the second run, 0.87 K in the first), 0.42 K too warm on average, its highest temperature 49.1 against 48.0 degC. The gas gaps of its glazing, held at their conductance at 10 degC until the third run, kept the sun in: a sun-lit glazing at 40 degC conducts a fifth more. The free-floating BESTEST cases show the same trend, smaller now (the largest gap of their temperatures went from 3.5 to 1.7 K, see the BESTEST page).

Renovated house. Every room follows within 0.06 to 0.10 K hour by hour, the heat of the radiators within 4 to 11 % CV(RMSE), and the meters within 0.2 % (heat pump), 2.0 % (fans) and 0 % (PV). The responses to the envelope (EPS conductivity from x0.5 to x2, airtightness, heat recovery, ventilation flow) agree within 3 % on the heating. The second run had attributed the gap of the set point response (0.79) to the flow laws of the radiator branches; the branch flows of both libraries, measured hour by hour, showed otherwise: the flow laws are the same (trano's Buildings valves and radiators are linearised too), but with the living room valve fully open FastSmoothBuildings passed 36.6 g/s against 43.9 g/s in Buildings, because the sensor feeding the six radiators had a resistance (1000 Pa at its nominal flow) that Buildings does not have, a fifth of the head of a branch. With 100 Pa the set point response rose to 0.87. What is left is the heat pump: while the living room valve is open, its supply water is 0.4 K cooler than in Buildings, and its electricity responds less (0.85) to the set point. FastSmoothBuildings simulates the 28 days three times faster in OpenModelica.

House before renovation. The same house with its gas boiler at 75 degC: every room follows within 0.02 to 0.09 K hour by hour (largest error 0.5 K in the first hours, as both models settle from their initial temperatures; 0.32 K at most after the first day), the heat of the radiators within 1.4 to 3.1 % CV(RMSE), and the heating demand is 1.7 % above Buildings in every variant (1.5 to 1.8 %), the gas 1.9 %, the same gas per unit of heat within 0.2 %. Every change that moves the results moves both libraries alike: the cavity insulation (−22 to −23 % of heating and of gas), the airtightness from x0.5 to x1.5 (heating ratios 1.00, the peak 0.88 to 0.98), the supply temperature and the radiator size (peak 1.06), the set point (0.99). The boiler of FastSmoothBuildings is that of Buildings (BoilerPolynomial, its heat loss counted twice as Buildings 13 does), driven by the same P controller on its water temperature; when the radiator valves open in the morning both fire at full power for a few minutes. FastSmoothBuildings simulates the 28 days 2.4 times faster.

docs.title: What FastSmoothBuildings still lacks
docs.text:
Ranked by what they change in the results above; the improvement plan gives the change, its cost and the check that closes it, with a formulation that keeps the model explicit and smooth for rumoca and CasADi.

  1. The heat pump at full load and its safety times. The supply water 0.4 K cool at full load, the electricity response to the set point (0.85), the peaks of the buffer and of the EPS x0.5: the condenser from the EN 14511 table instead of the buffer temperature, and a smooth surrogate of the minimum run time.
  2. The sun on the opaque surfaces. 8 % less response to the solar absorptance; the outside exchanges and the discretisation are ruled out.
  3. The sun kept in the zones that nothing cools, smaller now: the sun-space 0.42 K warm, the free-floating peaks of the light BESTEST zones 1 to 1.7 K high.
  4. Missing features. Unbalanced ventilation, wind- and stack-driven infiltration, ISO 13370 ground, moisture.
